nodes.name: Facebook group placement
nodes.summary: Facebook group placement was one of two channels compared in Rumah Lengkap Marketing's lead-tracker figures for the previous month, using two small traders in the same category (bedroom furniture) with near-equal spend. The Facebook group placement client (Client A) spent RM420, received 96 leads, 41 answered WhatsApp, 14 were qualified (budget, location, and timing clear), and 5 sales closed, at RM30 cost per qualified lead. Rumah Lengkap Marketing's conclusion was that the marketplace wins on lead volume while the group wins on leads that actually become sales, with both depending on listing hygiene.

nodes.name: live Q&A with industry experts
nodes.summary: Live Q&A with industry experts is held every month, 8-11 PM peak, all weekend long, per a Malaysia Reno Kaki admin announcement. The same announcement states that the trusted contractor list is updated monthly based on member feedback, and that disputes are handled through moderator mediation and fact-checking. Ah Boon Fix It and Sinar Home Marketplace both cited the announcement on 2026-11-04 and commented on it; Sinar Home Marketplace is an online-only home seller in Puchong. Kuching Home Appliance Centre cited a Kaki Corner weekly reno tips post by Malaysia Reno Kaki that repeats the monthly Live Q&A with industry experts and adds that the trusted contractor list is updated monthly; Kuching Home Appliance Centre has operated in Kuching for 30 years.

nodes.name: Budget Reno Bro
nodes.summary: Budget Reno Bro is a Twitter community focused on renovation and home improvement budgeting, whose admin team posted a "WEEKEND CHECK-IN — East Malaysia represent!" reminder for homeowners and renovators in Sabah and Sarawak. The post advised checking local East Malaysian suppliers first and comparing total landed cost (unit price + shipping to the buyer's postcode + installation + warranty coverage); noted that a "2-4 day" delivery from a KL warehouse routinely becomes 1-2 weeks once it crosses the South China Sea; asked buyers to confirm realistic transit days and courier coverage for KK, Kuching, Sandakan, Sibu, Tawau, Miri, and rural postcodes; advised knowing who services a warranty locally, since an authorised service centre within reach beats a longer warranty that only covers Semenanjung; and required contractor warnings to come with documentation (invoices, dates, photos, messages), with unverified accusations removed.

nodes.name: benchmark transparency
nodes.summary: Benchmark transparency requires the tool to publish per-category precision, how the labelled test set was built, and the false-match rate between near-identical units, since a "92% match" is decoration without them. Dr. Salina Rahmat framed this as "benchmark, not badge", and Ah Boon Fix It required verified listings to publish full model code and cut-out dimensions (W x D x H).

nodes.name: warranty
nodes.summary: Hafiz Ismail questioned how warranty would work if a frame is damaged or a cushion deflates on items delivered from Taobao over 10-18 days, and wants to view actual units at local shops before paying. Faizal Rahim requires the warranty written clearly for parts, compressor and labour, and asked whether the warranty remains valid or is voided if a third-party installer is used; he cited a prior case where a cheap installation led to a gas leak and a voided warranty. In Shah Alam he is replacing a 9-year-old, noisy, weak, costly-to-run 1.5HP unit and also asks about electrical load and earthing in an older house. Lim Wei Jie asked whether Casella displays installation terms alongside prices, and also requires full appliance dimensions with cut-out/clearance and whether the tagged price is total landed cost including delivery, installation and import tax.

nodes.name: delete button test
nodes.summary: Syafiq Hamdan tested the delete button with a photo of a small table before scanning real items, on the principle of test first, trust later.

nodes.name: aircond bilik utama
nodes.summary: Air conditioning for the main bedroom is still in planning as of the 14th month of Azlan Musa's renovation, with installation targeted for the following month; Azlan Musa expressed hope that prices stay stable.

nodes.name: Klang Valley
nodes.summary: Klang Valley is the setting for Dr. Salina Rahmat's survey of 120 consumers, whose reading is that early disclosure of an "iklan"/affiliate label before the click usually holds conversion better, not worse, than burying it after the click. She extends the finding to interviews with Klang Valley and East Malaysian buyers and to a cross-region 30-day test with three voluntary clients (one Klang Valley, one Penang, one Kuching) measured on cost per qualified lead against Facebook and marketplace baselines. She argues a 2–4 day delivery that becomes day 12 is also a disclosure failure, and that a paid listing should be labelled IKLAN in plain BM and English before the click, since the trust break is finding out late rather than the commission itself.

nodes.name: Grace Chin
nodes.summary: Grace Chin authored a 9-item "listing hygiene" checklist for home-goods sellers, audited before client ad budgets are spent; each time cost per lead drops without added spend. The checklist covers: display price vs real price (full price, or "from" with installation cost explained); sizes in cm AND inches; exact material (MDF, solid rubberwood, veneer — "kayu" alone is insufficient); delivery time by postcode ("3-5 hari" is wrong for Kuching); real stock; three photos (full shot, material close-up, real-room shot); FAQs answered in the listing rather than DMs; a single CTA (WhatsApp OR form); and a tracker for lead source. The post carries client names removed, describes "the same pattern each time," invites home-goods sellers to leave their product category in the comments, and closes "Kita kira dulu. No proof, no ringgit." The checklist drew comments from Syafiq Hamdan, Ah Boon Fix It, Lau Kok Wai, and the Rumah Bajet MY account.

nodes.name: productivity app
nodes.summary: Justin Ling installed a "productivity" app and uninstalled it before creating a single task. The splash screen took 4 seconds, onboarding ran 7 screens, and the app requested permissions for contacts, location, mic, and "nearby devices" — which Justin Ling questioned as excessive for a to-do list. He uninstalled after one attempt and called on indie developers to make apps fast, minimal, and respectful of user data.

nodes.name: West Malaysian seller
nodes.summary: A West Malaysian seller sold Farah Zainal a set of curtains, and the shipping cost to Kota Kinabalu exceeded the price of the curtains themselves. Farah Zainal, a Sabah homeowner in Kota Kinabalu, cited this purchase as the reason her rule is: total cost sampai rumah = item + shipping to Sabah + any import/tax + installation, the full model/size written down rather than a "92% match" claim, and asking before paying with a screenshot of the quote. She also holds that a Paid Partner slot must be labelled IKLAN in plain BM and English before the click, that a "Best offer" badge must show total landed cost rather than sticker price, and that room photos require clear retention terms and real permanent delete before upload. She shares landed totals with other East Malaysian shoppers and advises checking local first.

nodes.name: 1.0HP aircond
nodes.summary: 1.0HP aircond is cited as an example of a near-identical unit that a photo cannot distinguish from a 1.5HP unit, since capacity differences are invisible in a frame. Bintang Elektrik's installation checklist requires capacity to be matched to room size, noting that 1.0HP versus 1.5HP is invisible in a photo. Grace Chin names 1.0HP vs 1.5HP aircond as a case where the false-match rate between near-identical units must be published.

nodes.name: User 36
nodes.summary: User 36 is credited by Malaysia Reno Kaki as the author of the "listing hygiene" checklist of 9 items that sellers should fix before spending on ads or boost. The checklist covers display price vs real price, sizes in cm and inches, exact material, delivery time by postcode, real stock, three photos, FAQs in the listing, a single CTA, and a lead-source tracker. Malaysia Reno Kaki turned User 36's checklist into a group buyer filter for home-improvement purchases.

nodes.name: ovens
nodes.summary: Bintang Elektrik, a Peninsular independent retailer, advises that installation safety for gas stoves and ovens matters: a cheap job that skips leak-testing and proper venting is a risk rather than a saving. Buyers should confirm the seller's installer is certified and the warranty is serviced locally, since value comes from proper installation and after-sales service, not just the lowest price.

nodes.name: aircond installation
nodes.summary: Halim Yaakob is an aircond installer in Johor Bahru with 16 years of installation experience who states he installs aircond daily. He holds that photo-based matching cannot read the model code on an outdoor unit's sticker — 1.0HP and 1.5HP look the same in a photo, and different series, capacity, gas type (R32 vs R410A), warranty region and region-specific models are not distinguishable — so he advises screenshotting the sticker on both the indoor and outdoor units and checking the model code, not the listing photo. He states a "Best offer" that excludes vacuum, bracket, stabilizer, a new breaker and a 3-metre copper run (piping commonly 7 feet, with extra charged per foot) makes the cheap option expensive by the time it reaches the home; a RM199 installation quote does not cover these, and total landed cost must be itemized as unit + copper run (in metres) + bracket + stabilizer + new breaker + vacuum + labour, plus shipping to the buyer's own postcode and installation.

nodes.name: pay-per-lead model
nodes.summary: Sri Mutiara Home Centre, a family-owned furniture store in Johor Bahru operating since 2005, requires that leads be VERIFIED before committing to any pay-per-lead model. The store has engaged lead providers before and was disappointed by the lack of proof of authenticity, so it now requires evidence that a lead is real. It welcomes the local-first matching and leads inbox, on the condition that any paid Partner slot is labelled clearly as iklan front and centre, not in small print, and that the "Best offer" badge stays based on total cost, seller trust and after-sales service rather than on who paid for placement.

nodes.name: Sarah Thevi
nodes.summary: Sarah Thevi is 29, lives in Klang, and follows Indian-Malaysian home pages. She tested Casella with screenshots from those pages: a teak mandir cabinet was labelled only "wooden cabinet", a kolam-patterned rug "bohemian rug", and a stainless steel thali set was put in a random kitchen category; a batik-inspired cushion also drew a generic label. She asks whether the recognition logic covers Indian-Malaysian items or only English-language Western decor, whether it can tell a prayer-room cabinet from a wardrobe and a kolam rug from a generic patterned rug, and where room photos go, how long they are kept, and whether deletion is permanent; she tests with a plant photo first and wants guest use without a phone number. She wants the app to recognise warm wood, brass lamps, batik-inspired textiles and kolam motifs, to explain its recognition logic, to show per-class benchmarks rather than a "92% match" badge, and to disclose any affiliate influence.

nodes.name: MDF
nodes.summary: MDF is named as one of the distinct material specifications that "kayu" fails to capture; MDF, solid rubberwood, and veneer on ply are three totally different sofas that can share the same photo.

nodes.name: gas stoves
nodes.summary: Bintang Elektrik, a Peninsular independent retailer, advises that installation safety for gas stoves and ovens matters: a cheap job that skips leak-testing and proper venting is a risk rather than a saving. Buyers should confirm the seller's installer is certified and the warranty is serviced locally, since value comes from proper installation and after-sales service, not just the lowest price.

nodes.name: missed-demand data
nodes.summary: Kuching Home Appliance Centre, a family retailer in Sarawak, worries that missed-demand data reveals little in a small market.

nodes.name: creator credit and compensation
nodes.summary: Priya Nair's position is creator credit and compensation with explicit consent for listings, demos, and AI training, alongside clear retention with a real permanent delete stated up-front and commission labelled on every link before the click. Jason Reno Journal holds that credit and consent for a maker's images are non-negotiable. Priya Nair also asks that privacy terms be tested rather than trusted: she denied location permission during Casella's guest scan and found the scan still worked, sought and tested a scan-history delete control, asked for the retention period to be stated in plain language before upload, and submitted feedback requesting Tamil because the app offered only English and Malay. Rina Kecil Living frames permission, credit, and fair pay as the total landed cost of a creator's work.

nodes.name: Kaki Corner
nodes.summary: Kaki Corner is a Twitter community that publishes a "Weekly Reno Tips" series under the hashtag #MalaysiaRenoKaki. Its tips advise getting at least 3 contractor quotes and comparing scope rather than just price ("Murah belum tentu selamat"), checking total landed cost for big-ticket items such as aircon, kitchen cabinets and tiles, keeping a WhatsApp trail of quotations, payment receipts and promised dates, and insisting on certified workers for electrical and plumbing work. The community invites members to share genuine good and bad experiences, stays neutral in disputes with everything handled through moderator mediation and fact-checking, maintains a trusted contractor list updated monthly from member feedback, and holds live Q&A sessions with industry experts every month.

nodes.name: User 13
nodes.summary: User 13 translated a "listing hygiene" checklist into a measurement hygiene checklist, which Malaysia Reno Kaki commented on approvingly. The translated checklist's core claim is that cost per lead drops without added spend, framed as the reward for paying off measurement debt. It applies the same lesson to renovators: most "murah" deals look cheap because hidden costs — shipping, install, warranty, trade-in — aren't measured, so until all of it is counted, one is optimizing on vibes. The group version of "No proof, no ringgit" holds that a warning without invoice, date, or photo is just gossip, that price should be checked by total landed cost because a "95% accuracy" aggregate hides the failure mode just as a headline price hides Sabah shipping, and that if you can't measure it you can't compare it — leads or quotes. The stance is neutral, fact-checked, and consumer-protection first: "Kita kira dulu, baru belanja."

nodes.name: Mr DIY
nodes.summary: Mr DIY is a Malaysian retail store cited as a place budget renovators should visit to compare prices against app-listed prices. Budget Reno Bro advised scanning items in the app, then going to Mr DIY or a local hardware store (kedai hardware) to compare the app price versus the shop price before buying. Amirah Zulkifli, a first-time studio unit owner in Cyberjaya, follows the drill of scanning, saving, closing the app, then opening Shopee/Mr DIY manually to compare total cost to her home before deciding; she considers DIY fine for shelf and bracket purchases but wants installation included for her bed and wardrobe.

nodes.name: veneer on ply
nodes.summary: Veneer on ply is named as one of the distinct material specifications that "kayu" fails to capture; MDF, solid rubberwood, and veneer on ply are three totally different sofas that can share the same photo.

attributes.content_niche: Furniture lookalike comparisons and buying checklists
attributes.name: Tiffany Yeoh

nodes.name: Tiffany Yeoh
nodes.summary: Tiffany Yeoh is 30 years old and lives in Penang, where she rents and is design-conscious. She runs a series called "Lookalike or Not?" comparing replicas to originals via side-by-side screenshot versus actual unit, and judges whether lookalike items capture the style at all. Her criteria center on silhouette (arms 2cm too thick or seat too deep collapses the style), fabric weight/GSM and weave, and legs and joinery (tapered solid wood versus screw-on plastic caps); she asks for real dimensions because photos lie, and she once bought a mid-century lounge chair replica that arrived with wrong proportions and cheap fabric. She cited a sofa tagged "92% match" that had the wrong silhouette and cheap fabric as a hard no, and said a "Best offer" badge tells price honesty but not whether a piece captures the style. She plans to test Casella's 3 free scans on her Japandi inspiration and report back.

nodes.name: Cheah Xin Yi's air fryer
nodes.summary: Cheah Xin Yi bought an air fryer in 2022 from a viral post. The top comment's affiliate code had expired, and the shipping promised as "2-4 hari" took 11 days. Cheah Xin Yi cites this purchase as the lesson behind checking total landed cost (unit + postage to the buyer's postcode + installation + who services the warranty locally) and screenshotting everything before paying.

nodes.name: Grace Chin
nodes.summary: Grace Chin is a product manager with eight years in computer vision who evaluates computer-vision tools, including the Casella scan-and-link shopping beta in Malaysia, which she called "a demo, not a validation set." Her recurring test: a room photo must map to the correct SKU, so vendors must publish the metric (top-1 category accuracy vs. retrieval precision@1 on the exact model code), how the labelled test set was built and whether near-identical units (1.0HP vs 1.5HP AC; NR-BX418VS vs lookalike) were included, and the false-match rate. She cites a 2019 "beats Google Lens" claim that collapsed once the test set proved weighted toward the vendor's own training data, and argues a startup can beat Google Lens only in a niche with a specialized, well-curated dataset.

nodes.name: gas regulator
nodes.summary: A faulty gas regulator caused a leak in a client's home. For gas work, only certified workers should be used, and the model number of the regulator should be requested and checked against the spec sheet. Cheap online gas parts are not worth the risk. On 2026-11-04, Sim Kok Leong commented on Malaysia Reno Kaki's weekly renovation tips that buying a regulator or hose from an unknown online seller to save RM20 gambles with a family's life; some such units did not pass basic pressure tests, and the "certified" label was printed on the box rather than the unit. Sim Kok Leong advised buyers to check the total landed cost and the seller, asking whether the seller has a local physical presence and service point and following the money when a reviewer pushes a product, with no visible commission disclosure being a red flag; Sim Kok Leong discloses commissions every time.

nodes.name: RM10,000 affiliate deal
nodes.summary: Jason Reno turned down a RM10,000 affiliate deal for an untested product, and on that basis does not ask sellers to do what he won't. He requires affiliate commission from Shopee/Taobao links to be labelled clearly on every link before the click, in BM and English, since disclosure is not a disclaimer.

nodes.name: Seremban showroom
nodes.summary: Bintang Elektrik operates a Seremban showroom that offers demos so customers in Seremban can compare properly. Bintang Elektrik advises that a photo cannot carry the full model code and that "match dekat" is not the same as the correct unit, and states "We install, you relax" and "Quality service guaranteed." For aircond, water heaters, hobs and gas stoves, Bintang Elektrik stresses installation by a trained installer with proper vacuum, correct piping and a leak test, since a cheap install can void the warranty and create a safety risk, and asks customers to compare total cost until installed and tested rather than the sticker price. Bintang Elektrik advises confirming in writing the full model code, that standard installation (piping, brackets, vacuum, breaker, labour) is included, and warranty terms covering local authorised versus parallel import and whether parts, compressor and labour are covered.

nodes.name: small-space living
nodes.summary: Priya Nair writes from Petaling Jaya as a tenant and small-space living advocate, sharing rental-friendly decor tips and app privacy guidance under tags including #RentalLife, #PrivacyMatters, #PetalingJaya and #SmallSpaceLiving. Her posted tips include testing an app's guest scan/guest mode before registering, reviewing permissions one by one and declining unnecessary location access, checking language and privacy settings (she requested Tamil for one furniture app), confirming scan history and data can be deleted, and screenshotting the privacy policy. She has asked to join tenant or small-space living communities and wants to hear about tenant rights, deposits withheld without reason, and apps hiding data practices. Rental-friendly decor she favours includes foldable shelves, roll-up carpets and clip-on screwless lamps. Milo, her cat, sits on a foldable side table.

nodes.name: Best offer badge
nodes.summary: The "Best offer" badge is based on total cost rather than sticker price; total cost is item price plus delivery, installation when needed, and import tax and shipping for cross-border orders, and it also considers match, delivery, seller trust, and service. A merchant can pay for one "Partner" slot per list, at position 2, which must pass a match-quality threshold and can never receive the Best offer badge; the paid slot must be labelled "iklan" before the click in BM + English. The merchant phase announced by Casella for Malaysian stores includes verified listings, local stores matched first, a leads inbox, a dashboard, and the paid Partner slot, and is not available during the beta. Budget Reno Bro reported in the beta that the badge does not appear for cheap items below a certain threshold, and Ah Boon Fix It, a beta tester who earns affiliate commission on Shopee/Taobao links, found match accuracy hit-or-miss.

nodes.name: user 13
nodes.summary: User 13 received credit from the Sabah Sarawak Home Group admin for the point that the commercial layer only holds if the item on screen is the right item.

nodes.name: Midea
nodes.summary: Midea is named among the 1.5HP inverter aircond brands, alongside Daikin and Panasonic, that Budget Reno Bro cited in a hardware-store price breakdown. App pricing for a 1.5HP inverter unit of these brands is RM1,500–1,900, while hardware or appliance shops may offer RM1,450–1,700.

nodes.name: Casella's verification
nodes.summary: Kedai Perabot Seri Jaya, a small family furniture shop in Klang operating since 1985, completed Casella's verification and listed a selection of its pieces, though the CSV upload was challenging for the non-technical team. Jason Reno Journal has been testing the Casella beta and considers the tag-and-link concept neat, but notes a photo cannot confirm model code, capacity, or gas type (1.0HP vs 1.5HP look identical in a room shot); before recommending an app to viewers he checks whether affiliate commission is disclosed on every link, whether the "Best offer" badge shows total landed cost (delivery, installation, import tax) rather than sticker price, and whether there is any measured match accuracy or just a demo with "3 free scans." Rina Kecil Living asks whether Casella credits and compensates creators whose images or screenshots it uses, citing a 2021 incident in which a popular home design app used her before/after photos without credit or permission until a follower tagged her.

nodes.name: LRT
nodes.summary: Budget Reno Bro was editing on the LRT while reading a thread about total landed cost, and the thread's line "Dia orang tak beli harga, dia orang beli harapan" clicked for him there.

nodes.name: affiliate commission labelling
nodes.summary: Affiliate commission labelling must appear in front, before the click, in easy BM and English — not buried in a hashtag or bio. Dr. Salina Rahmat, who studies disclosure and trust, holds that commission itself is not wrong and that Casella is good because she tells people; the problem is learning about it too late. Disclosure is not a disclaimer; it is a relationship. Jason Reno Journal proposes timing the disclosure rather than just checking it exists: measure cost per qualified lead when the "iklan"/affiliate label sits before the click versus buried after, then publish the comparison, with his read being that early disclosure holds conversion better, not worse.

nodes.name: home design
nodes.summary: Vanessa Goh applies the same reasoning to home design as to accuracy claims: clients chase a "designer look" the way a field chases a headline number, and a styled photo is a benchmark that hides its test conditions — light direction, ceiling height, scale, maintenance. "95% on curated examples" and "this room looks amazing on Pinterest" fail the same way, on the messy, humid, real-world slice. Aggregate hides the failure mode: "3–5 days" is wrong for Kuching the way a lookalike is wrong for a condo facing west in the monsoon. She keeps a notebook of client quotes instead of trusting a vibe, under the principle "Kita kira dulu. No proof, no ringgit."

nodes.name: Kedai Serbaneka Aman
nodes.summary: Kedai Serbaneka Aman is a brand referenced in a post about affiliate marketing; the poster said that if brands like Kedai Serbaneka Aman do not pay for real leads, the poster wants to prove that their influence is genuine. In a November 4, 2026 post, Nadia Home Diary again cited Kedai Serbaneka Aman as a brand that never paid for online leads, as part of her stated effort to prove her influence is genuine rather than click-driven.

nodes.name: Tiffany Yeoh
nodes.summary: Tiffany Yeoh, based in Kuching, asked in Taobao Kaki Malaysia whether RM800 to ship a 3-seater sofa from Taobao to Kuching was normal, crediting Melvin Pang and other respondents. She compared a Taobao sofa at RM1,450 plus RM800 shipping with no local warranty service (RM2,250 total) against a local Kuching supplier at RM2,680 delivered and installed, a RM430 difference, and drove to the warehouse to inspect the sofa in person before deciding. Her verdict: for bulky items buy local, since the shipping quote is a hidden tax not shown in West Malaysia, while Taobao is fine for small items such as beadwork and kitchen tools. She urged comparing total landed cost rather than the displayed price and framed the issue as Sarawak wanting money spent fairly.

attributes.focus_area: Total landed cost and shipping for East Malaysian shoppers
attributes.name: Sabah & Sarawak fam

nodes.name: Sabah & Sarawak fam
nodes.summary: Sabah & Sarawak fam is a Twitter community for East Malaysian shoppers focused on total landed cost and shipping. A weekend reminder post urged members to compare unit price between apps and local kedai, check shipping to their own postcode rather than a "Peninsular rate" (RM40 can become RM180 to KK, and "2-4 days" can become 2 weeks after crossing the South China Sea), account for installation that most outstation sellers do not cover, and confirm a locally reachable service centre for warranty, since a 5-year paper covering only Semenanjung equals zero for East Malaysia. The post's rule is "no proof, no ringgit": if a seller or portal cannot show the real cost, it is not a candidate. It called for supporting local East Malaysian suppliers who know local roads, ports and prices, and for group-buys to cut shipping together, under the hashtags #CheckThatShipping, #SabahShopper and #TotalLandedCost.

nodes.name: neighbourhood shops
nodes.summary: Neighbourhood shops are among the places already used to identify where an item is from.

nodes.name: Budget Reno Bro
nodes.summary: Budget Reno Bro is a member of the East Malaysian renovation community who advises Sabah and Sarawak homeowners to compare the app price against the landed cost. Budget Reno Bro's stated rule is to print both and compare both, treating the app price as bait and the landed cost as the truth. For Sabah buyers, Budget Reno Bro cites a shipping swing from RM40 to RM180, installation that nobody covers outstation, and a "5-year warranty" that only works in Semenanjung, which Budget Reno Bro calls just a nice font on a PDF. Budget Reno Bro's guidance is "Harga app vs harga kedai local. Total landed cost or nothing. Baru fair," and Budget Reno Bro uses the hashtags #CheckThatShipping and #TotalLandedCost.

nodes.name: hardware store
nodes.summary: Budget Reno Bro works at a hardware store, where customers bring listings such as a RM299 Shopee offer and Budget Reno Bro asks for the shipping cost to their postcode and adds installation, revealing a real price of RM680.

nodes.name: Nadia's budget makeover series
nodes.summary: Nadia's budget makeover series for B40 families is one of the small steps Nadia is continuing for now as she works toward her own home decor line. She framed it alongside tidying her page/Linktree for her recommendations and carefully choosing honest, transparent brands to collaborate with. She emphasized being honest, affordable, and community-focused, and thanked her audience for staying with her, saying they are the reason she keeps making content.

nodes.name: TikTok Shop
nodes.summary: TikTok Shop is an affiliate platform that Nadia Home Diary asked followers about on November 4, 2026, seeking tips from anyone who had tried TikTok Shop or Shopee Affiliate; the post was tagged #TikTokShopMalaysia and #AffiliateMarketing, and she noted quietly testing affiliate links in her bio and tracking clicks while aiming to recommend only items she uses, following Sharifah Nadia's guidance on safe materials and clear return policies. Rumah Bajet MY also referenced TikTok Shop in a November 4, 2026 weekend post, urging buyers to check the total landed cost (unit + shipping to their postcode + installation + warranty service) before tapping Buy Now on Shopee/TikTok Shop decor finds, since "2-4 hari" delivery promises can become two weeks crossing the South China Sea.

nodes.name: CheckLocalFirst
nodes.summary: CheckLocalFirst is a hashtag used by Farah Zainal, a Sabah homeowner in KK, in posts about the Casella beta. Farah Zainal's post sets out five demands: count only total landed cost (item plus shipping to Sabah/Sarawak plus import tax plus installation); label paid partner slots as IKLAN in plain BM and English before the click; show total landed cost on "best offer" badges; state clear retention and real permanent delete for room photos before upload; and compare with trusted KK/Kuching suppliers first. Later posts add the hashtag #CreditCreators, per-class accuracy benchmarks, and delivery days by poskod. Others contributing under the tag include Hannah Lau, Nadia Home Diary, Kevin Lim, Joanne Sia of Miri, Justin Ling of Sibu, Kamala Devi of Taiping, Dr.

nodes.name: total cost sampai pasang
nodes.summary: Total cost sampai pasang — the full cost through installation rather than the sticker price — is one of the checklist points Kamala Devi holds on to. Kamala Devi asks that delivery, piping, brackets and installation costs be stated up front in one total number with no hidden fees. Farah Zainal applies the same principle in Sabah: item price plus shipping across the South China Sea plus any import tax plus installation, since sticker price alone is the trap.

nodes.name: teak mandir cabinet
nodes.summary: A teak mandir cabinet in an Indian-Malaysian home in Klang was labelled only "wooden cabinet" by Casella when Sarah Thevi, the home's user, tested the app with screenshots from local Indian-Malaysian home pages; the results were too generic and the cultural cues were missed. In the same tests, a kolam-patterned rug came back as "bohemian rug", a stainless steel thali set went into a random kitchen category, and a batik cushion drew generic labels. Sarah Thevi, a consumer voice in Klang, cited the teak mandir cabinet mislabel across multiple forum posts and Twitter as evidence that the app's recognition logic covers only English-language Western decor rather than Indian-Malaysian items and styles, asking whether it can distinguish a prayer-room cabinet from a plain wardrobe and a kolam rug from a generic patterned rug, and seeking plain answers on photo retention, permanent deletion, guest use without a phone number, and paid-recommendation disclosure.

nodes.name: Budget Reno Bro
nodes.summary: Budget Reno Bro creates room-tour content, stitching and duetting room tours daily, and has had his own breakdown clips reposted with the numbers cropped out. He beta-tests Casella and posted his own failures: a kitchen photo suggested a cabinet that did not fit, and a sofa match also did not fit. He also found that the Best offer badge does not appear for cheap items below a certain threshold, which he calls unfair for budget renovators. He set three requirements in writing: credit, consent and compensation before any creator or small-shop image is used (listings, demos, AI training); retention and real permanent delete stated before upload, tested with a plant photo first; and affiliate commission labelled on every link before the click. He supports #CreditCreators and #RumahBajetMY, and holds that no proof means no ringgit — show the benchmark, not the badge.

nodes.name: Amirah Zulkifli's small kitchen
nodes.summary: Amirah Zulkifli's planned small kitchen with a quartz top and compact appliances came in beyond her starting budget.

nodes.name: Amirah Zulkifli
nodes.summary: Amirah Zulkifli is 27, lives in Cyberjaya, and is setting up her first small studio unit, which she calls Unit 12-3. As of November 2026 she is still hunting for the bed, wardrobe, compact sofa, and study desk, all rental-friendly and small-space, and keeps a Notes list called "Unit 12-3 Wishlist" beside a mental RM-per-square-foot calculator. She has not uploaded a single real photo of her empty unit; she tests apps with a photo of her teh tarik first, then checks whether the delete button actually deletes, treating home photos as not free data. She calls herself careful with money (budget not formal) and compares items such as a RM299 shelf for three weeks before buying, wants total landed cost with delivery and installation shown rather than sticker price, prefers small-space sizes (compact sofa, slim wardrobe), and treats an unshown confidence score as "not sure" because a confident wrong match means returns and real money.

nodes.name: vetted local makers directory
nodes.summary: Vanessa Goh, an interior designer in Kuala Lumpur, is building a vetted local makers directory and invited Rimbun to join it, with her DMs open to the workshop. She framed the invitation around credit and consent, which she called non-negotiable, and asked whether Rimbun knows where its pieces appear and who earns the commission when a piece is listed through a scan-and-link app.

nodes.name: Melaka
nodes.summary: Rimbun Rattan Crafts is a small family workshop in Melaka making handmade rattan furniture and home decor since 2015, describing itself as a humble collective of artisans offering locally crafted, sustainable rattan and Melaka heritage, with customers able to see, touch and feel the weave before deciding. The workshop publicly questions whether handmade rattan pieces can ever truly match a similarity search, noting each piece has small variations — hand-tied knots, sun-deepened shades, curves that follow the cane rather than a mould. Its stated asks: any paid Partner slot must be labelled clearly as iklan front and centre, the "Best offer" badge must stay based on total cost and seller trust rather than paid placement, and verified listings plus transparent cost-per-lead would help small makers, who would be glad to test small.

nodes.name: group-buying
nodes.summary: Rumah Bajet MY's group-buying push aims to cut shipping costs for East Malaysia buyers, with readers asked to share experiences, tag the account in honest finds, and group-buy to cut shipping together under #TotalLandedCost and #CheckPrice. Its on 4 November 2026 post for East Malaysia decor and furniture lists four costs: unit price (app/TikTok Shop vs kedai local), shipping to the buyer's own postcode (RM40 can jadi RM180 to KK/Sibu), installation (RM150–400 for outstation sellers), and warranty serviceable locally; buyers should get a quote from a local East Malaysian supplier first, ask realistic transit days, screenshot price, promised date and chat logs, and report honest good and bad experiences with no politics/race/religion or unverified attacks.

nodes.name: Faizal Rahim
nodes.summary: Faizal Rahim, 43, lives in Shah Alam and is replacing a noisy, weak, expensive-to-run 9-year-old 1.5HP air conditioner in his master bedroom. He wants one written total: unit + standard installation (piping, brackets, vacuum, breaker, labour) + delivery by postcode + any import tax, plus warranty covering parts, compressor and labour, with local authorised versus parallel import identified. He repeatedly asks whether a third-party installer voids the warranty, having previously been burned by a cheap install that caused a gas leak and voided the warranty; because his house is older he also asks about electrical load and proper earthing. He wants the full model code on both indoor and outdoor stickers (1.0HP vs 1.5HP look alike in photos), capacity matched to room area, itemised written quotes with realistic delivery days, and referrals to trusted installers in Shah Alam.

nodes.name: qualified lead
nodes.summary: A qualified lead is defined in Rumah Lengkap Marketing's lead-tracker comparison as a lead with clear budget, location, and timing. In the previous month's comparison of two small bedroom-furniture traders with near-equal spend, the Facebook group placement client (Client A, RM420 spend) had 96 leads, 41 answering WhatsApp, 14 qualified leads, 5 closed sales, and RM30 cost per qualified lead, while the marketplace listing boost client (Client B, RM450 spend) had 210 leads, 58 answering WhatsApp, 9 qualified, 2 closed sales, and RM50 cost per qualified lead. Rumah Lengkap Marketing does not treat reach or total lead count as a KPI, counting cost per qualified lead and cost per closed sale first, and is collecting honest numbers on what home traders would pay for one qualified lead for its portal assessment file.

nodes.name: Rina Kecil Living's three asks
nodes.summary: Rina Kecil Living locked in three testable asks from the thread's replies: (1) credit and compensation with explicit consent before photos are used — listings, demos, AI training — with the privacy policy screenshotted like the price; (2) retention period stated before upload in plain BM and English, with a delete that really deletes, tested first with a plant photo; (3) affiliate commission labelled on every link before the click, since disclosure is a relationship, not a disclaimer. She also endorsed the technical ask to publish the actual benchmark — top-1 versus retrieval precision and the false-match rate — because a confident wrong match costs more than no match, and "3 free scans" is a demo, not validation. She is taking the asks to the platforms under #CreditCreators.

nodes.name: benchmark testing
nodes.summary: Jason Reno requires a benchmark before trusting any "scan-and-link" tool: measured per-category precision/recall, how the labelled test set was built, and the false-match rate between near-identical units (1.0HP vs 1.5HP aircond; same sofa, different fabric code). He holds that a "92% match" claim is decoration without measured numbers, that a photo cannot read a model code, and that a confident wrong match costs more than no match. His full sequence before recommending anything is: full model code (screenshot both indoor and outdoor) → cut-out/clearance dimensions → total landed cost (item + delivery + installation + import tax, East Malaysia included) → warranty in writing (parts + labour, local authorised vs parallel import) → benchmark + commission label.

nodes.name: Casella
nodes.summary: Casella is a planned mobile app for Malaysia, operating under a working name, that turns a room photo or screenshot into furniture, decor and appliance offers tagged with prices and linked to Shopee and Taobao; there is no in-app checkout and Casella earns affiliate commission on those links. Features include a Best offer badge based on total cost including delivery, installation and import charges rather than sticker price, a My Home feature saving items into rooms grouped as Considering, Decided or Bought, 3 free guest scans before sign-in via Google, Apple, phone OTP or email, and a later merchant phase (not available during beta) with verified listings, local stores matched first, a leads inbox, a dashboard and one paid Partner slot per list that cannot receive the Best offer badge.

nodes.name: paying per lead
nodes.summary: Kuching Home Appliance Centre, a family retailer in Sarawak, seeks proof that leads are real before paying per lead.

nodes.name: kitchen appliance buying
nodes.summary: Lim Wei Jie's pre-purchase checklist for any kitchen appliance in his Seremban 2 terrace house calls for full dimensions (W x D x H, mm) and cut-out dimensions before confirming cabinet work, since a contractor once built a cabinet without checking his appliance dimensions and the result did not fit; confirming installation is included in the price, because improper installation of gas appliances is a safety hazard; checking warranty length, coverage, and who services it locally (Seremban/Nilai coverage); and verifying after-sales support in writing before payment.

nodes.name: Japandi inspo
nodes.summary: Amirah Zulkifli scanned her Japandi inspo with Casella, the Malaysian app that tags furniture and appliances with prices and links to offers on Shopee and Taobao, and found everything mahal gila. She planned to test the 3 free scans available without an account before uploading anything, saying she would measure first and report back.

nodes.name: Grace Chin
nodes.summary: Grace Chin argues that a tester's anecdote and a vendor's "92% match" claim are both single observations, and that a published methodology is what closes the gap between them. Grace cited a tester's note that match accuracy is hit-or-miss — a kitchen photo suggested a cabinet that tak muat and a sofa match pun tak fit — as a real, reproducible failure, and identified it as a category-correct, identity-wrong failure that would show up as a high false-match rate rather than a low top-1. Grace's stated demands on the vendor: define the metric (top-1 category accuracy versus retrieval precision@1 on the exact model code), state how the labelled test set was built (who labelled it, how many classes, whether near-identical units were included), and publish the false-match rate per category along with the failure set, not just the failure rate.

nodes.name: price-drop alerts
nodes.summary: Price-drop alerts are planned for the next phase and are not available at beta.

nodes.name: Hafiz Ismail's sofa
nodes.summary: Hafiz Ismail waited 11 days for a sofa whose listing stated 3-5 days delivery, which he calls a disclosure failure rather than mere delay. He asks for total-to-home figures for a 3-seater sofa to KL to compare apple-to-apple.

nodes.name: fake gas appliances
nodes.summary: Ah Boon Fix It warned that fake gas appliances are a bigger problem than fake "2-4 hari" delivery promises, citing regulators and hoses bought from unknown online sellers to save RM20 as a gamble with a family's life. He tested a few of these; some did not pass basic pressure tests, and the "certified" label was printed on the box, not the unit. He advised checking the seller for a local physical presence and a service point you can drive to, and following the money when a reviewer pushes a product: no visible commission disclosure is a red flag, and he discloses his own every time.

nodes.name: home decor
nodes.summary: Nadia Home Diary, a home decor creator, identifies buying a pretty item before checking whether it fits as the number one mistake in home decor, with the rule "Ukur dulu, beli kemudian." The decor checklist covers measuring the space and item size (wall, table, corner) before buying; confirming the price includes postage and installation, not just the tag price; using a certified worker for lights and wiring; keeping receipts and chat logs as protection; and buying from sellers with a clear return policy. Cheap is not a deal if the item does not fit or breaks easily, and Nadia Home Diary recommends only what she has used and trusts. Her stated commitments include labeling honestly when a link is affiliate (before the click, not hidden in a bio), recommending only items she has used and trusts, asking sellers about dimensions, packaging protection, postcode zone, and service centre, and using total landed cost rather than tag price.

nodes.name: room photos
nodes.summary: Chua Li Ting asked how long room photos are kept, whether deletion is permanent, and whether the scanner can be used as a guest without signing in with a real name. She tests the delete button with a dummy photo — a plant, not her child's room — before trusting any scanner. Cheah Xin Yi also asked where room photos go, how long they are kept, and whether deletion is permanent, and tests with a plant photo before uploading her real unit.

nodes.name: interior designers
nodes.summary: Interior designers are among the people already used to identify where an item is from.

attributes.name: Vista Sofa Factory Outlet's sofa factory in Muar

nodes.name: Vista Sofa Factory Outlet's sofa factory in Muar
nodes.summary: Vista Sofa Factory Outlet operates a sofa factory outlet in Muar and posts from a business account. It treats Taobao and Shopee as a benchmark rather than an enemy and is watching Casella with interest, but its key question is whether the scan drives real local leads. For bulky items like sofas, a tag cannot show frame wood, foam density, fabric quality, stitching or true dimensions, so "Best offer" must mean total landed cost (unit, delivery, installation, after-sales) rather than sticker price, and any paid Partner slot must say "iklan" before the click. It will test Casella only if leads are qualified — real WhatsApp enquiries and real showroom visits in Johor/Melaka — and the cost per qualified lead works; its stance is "no proof, no ringgit," and it invites customers to sit before buying.

nodes.name: kolam rug
nodes.summary: A kolam rug was among the items Sarah Thevi uploaded to a shopping app to test its recognition, alongside a teak mandir cabinet, a batik cushion, and a thali set. The app returned only generic labels such as "wooden cabinet" and "bohemian rug" rather than recognising the items.

nodes.name: Hannah Lau
nodes.summary: Hannah Lau is planning a small apartment in KL someday. She keeps a "Rumah Impian" album of screenshots and saved a post about total cost through installation rather than sticker price into it, thanking Bintang Elektrik for the information.

nodes.name: Rawang
nodes.summary: Rawang is the home city of Thinesh Kumar, 31.

nodes.name: Kota Kinabalu
nodes.summary: Kota Kinabalu (KK) is a Sabah city and the home city of Farah Zainal, a Sabah homeowner. In the Sabah Sarawak Home Group, KK is a reference local market alongside Kuching: members are steered to "check local first" and compare trusted local suppliers in KK and Kuching before buying, since for Sabah/Sarawak "delivery + installation + import charges" often determines the whole cost and a "2-4 day" KL warehouse delivery routinely becomes 1-2 weeks once it crosses the South China Sea. The group asks for realistic transit days and courier coverage for KK, Kuching, Sandakan, Sibu, Tawau, Miri, Pantai Timur (Kangar, Kota Bharu) and rural postcodes, and warns that a warranty covering only Semenanjung is worthless to KK buyers. Farah Zainal cites a West Malaysian curtain order where shipping cost more than the curtains, and says a RM40 shipping figure can become RM180 to KK.

nodes.name: Cyberjaya
nodes.summary: Amirah Zulkifli is a 27-year-old living in a small studio unit (Unit 12-3) in Cyberjaya, furnishing it for the first time and working from a Notes list called "Unit 12-3 Wishlist"; she is still hunting a bed, a wardrobe, and a compact sofa. She tests an app with a plant photo before uploading photos of her real unit, tests the deletion function first using a photo of her teh tarik before scanning her actual unit, and will not upload if the photo retention period is unclear or if proof is lacking. She checks the total landed cost — delivery, installation, and import tax, not sticker price — and follows a scan, save, close app, compare against Shopee/Mr DIY manually, then decide routine; one scan app quoted a "compact sofa" at RM899 sticker that rose past RM1,100 with delivery to her postcode and conditional installation.

nodes.name: lampu clip-on tanpa skru
nodes.summary: Priya Nair chose a screw-free clip-on lamp as one of the small, movable items for a rental where the landlord does not allow drilling or painting; it can be removed and taken along when moving.

nodes.name: sofa total cost until installation
nodes.summary: Hafiz Ismail advises asking "berapa total sampai pasang" rather than "berapa harga": item plus delivery to the unit, installation, and disposal of the old item as one written number, since sticker price is meaningless. He asks sellers to drop their total landed cost for apple-to-apple comparison.

nodes.name: guest access without sign-in
nodes.summary: Chua Li Ting asks whether she can try as a guest without signing in with her real name, saying transparency is not just about price.

nodes.name: Taobao
nodes.summary: Taobao is a cross-border source listed in the Casella app's per-item offers comparison alongside Shopee, with a match badge and a total price in RM; the buy button opens Shopee or Taobao with no in-app checkout, and Casella earns affiliate commission on these links. Taobao offers show an estimated 10 to 18 days for delivery. A 3-seater sofa shipped from Taobao to Kuching was quoted at RM800 before import tax and installation. Taobao image search is among the tools people already use, usually one item at a time. Commenters on the Casella beta thread treat Taobao and Shopee as benchmarks for local sellers and argue that "Best offer" must reflect total landed cost (unit, delivery by postcode, installation, import tax, after-sales) rather than sticker price, with paid Partner slots labelled "iklan" before the click.

nodes.name: Mount Austin
nodes.summary: Mount Austin is where a customer cited by Halim Yaakob bought a 1.5HP unit following a "92% match" from an app scan; the outdoor unit was a different series and the price did not include vacuum and a new breaker. Halim Yaakob arrived and had to explain that the match was close but not close enough, which made the job difficult. In his warning about scan apps such as the Casella beta, Halim cited the Mount Austin case as the outdoor series mismatch example, and Jason Reno Journal also pointed to it as exactly the outdoor series mismatch case, saying "92% match" is a similarity score on a photo rather than a model code.

nodes.name: Shah Alam
nodes.summary: Shah Alam is a city in Selangor, Malaysia. Aisyah Rahman, 31, is a first-time condo buyer there on a tight RM30k budget; she speaks Malay, saves room tours in a "Rumah Impian" album, rarely knows item names, and returns if tagged prices fit her budget. She insists on total landed cost — unit price + delivery to her postcode + installation + warranty (who services it locally) — and skips sellers who cannot give full figures in writing. Faizal Rahim, in Shah Alam, is replacing a 9-year-old 1.5HP aircond in his master bedroom (now noisy, weak, expensive to run); he will not buy without written confirmation on installation and warranty, requires full indoor and outdoor model code stickers, capacity matched to room size plus electrical load and earthing checks, and itemised quotes covering unit, delivery by postcode, piping, brackets, vacuum, breaker and labour, with parts, compressor and labour warranty and third-party installer validity.

nodes.name: affiliate commission links
nodes.summary: Shopee and Taobao links in the app are affiliate commission links, meaning someone earns when a purchase is made, so the "best price" may not be the cheapest total. Ah Boon Fix It earns affiliate commission if a purchase is made through the buy button and always discloses it; Thinesh Kumar advises checking the domain first and never entering bank details or OTP on any page reached from a link.

nodes.name: Balakrishnan Nair
nodes.summary: Balakrishnan Nair is 62 and lives in Petaling Jaya. He spent 40 years in electrical maintenance and is a retired electrical technician who prefers phone calls to shops and doubts that an app helps with after-sales service. He once got stranded with a broken fridge: app-based service took several days, while one phone call to a local shop settled it in hours. His advice: verify the seller's credentials (SSM number, named trained installer, business address), ask for full model codes on both indoor and outdoor stickers, capacity matched to room size, and total cost sampai pasang and test (unit, piping, bracket, vacuum, breaker, labour), plus written warranty for parts and labour and whether a third-party installer voids it.

nodes.name: electrical maintenance work
nodes.summary: Balakrishnan Nair has done electrical maintenance work for 40 years and has seen the same problems many times. He advises buyers that a "92% match" is not a model number and that photos cannot carry the full code on a sticker, since 1.0HP and 1.5HP compressors look the same in photos. He asks three things: the full model code for both indoor and outdoor units in black and white; capacity matched to room area, not unit appearance; and total cost through installation and testing, covering unit, piping, bracket, vacuum, breaker and labour. He also asks whether using a different installer voids the warranty, and frames the matter as safety rather than cheapness, since an early compressor failure is possible and a gas leak is more dangerous.

nodes.name: Shopee
nodes.summary: Shopee is one of the marketplaces compared for each item in the Casella app, alongside Taobao; offers show a match badge and a total price in RM, with sorting, filtering and side-by-side comparison, and the buy button opens Shopee or Taobao with no in-app checkout, with Casella earning affiliate commission on those links. Casella's merchant phase lets verified Malaysian stores list products by form, CSV or Shopee shop import. Sinar Home Marketplace, an online-only Malaysian home goods seller based in Puchong, runs mainly on Shopee, keeps a Shopee link in its bio, and as of 4 November 2026 compares its Shopee advertising return against portal leads daily; it offered to share its Shopee ROAS baseline as a voluntary test client.

nodes.name: Xiaomi rice cooker
nodes.summary: Kevin Lim has a 1.8L Xiaomi rice cooker sitting in his online cart since the previous month, alongside a 1.8L Midea rice cooker, awaiting the 6.6 sale to see which one drops to a lower total price. He confirmed the seller rating, delivery days, and warranty for the items before deciding.

nodes.name: consumer electronics training
nodes.summary: Jason Reno spent five years as a consumer electronics trainer before going full-time on reviews. He draws on that background in aircond buying guidance, where he identifies the core problem as "92% match" being a similarity score on a photo rather than a model code, since 1.0HP vs 1.5HP units and inverter vs non-inverter units can look identical in a frame. His buying rules require screenshots of both indoor and outdoor stickers with the full model code, capacity matched to room size and electrical load with proper earthing for old houses, a written itemised total through installation and testing (unit, delivery by poskod, piping, bracket, vacuum, breaker, labour), black-and-white warranty covering parts, compressor and labour for local authorised vs parallel import, and clarity on whether a third-party installer voids warranty.

nodes.name: privacy settings
nodes.summary: Priya Nair, a tenant in Petaling Jaya who likes small spaces and privacy settings, shared privacy reminders: check before you click and guest scan before signing in, reject unreasonable location permission requests, and check language settings and confirm data can be deleted. She also framed rental-friendly decor as small items that can be moved rather than things that must be drilled.

nodes.name: Budget Reno Bro
nodes.summary: Budget Reno Bro is beta-testing a room-scanning app and edits on the LRT. When he scanned his parents' living room, the app gave a clean number but missed the local equivalents and installation cost; walking to the kedai hardware, the real total differed. He asks any app's "shop-the-whole-room total" to specify which items, which local SKUs, and whether installation and delivery are included — the slice, not the aggregate. He frames the issue as "harga app vs harga kedai," "a headline price that hides shipping/install = a benchmark that hides its test conditions," and "listing price ≠ landed cost." He endorsed Grace Chin's listing-hygiene checklist points 1 and 4 and Rumah Bajet MY's total-landed-cost breakdown: unit price, shipping to your own postcode, installation, and local warranty service.

nodes.name: Milo
nodes.summary: Milo is Priya Nair's cat, living with her in Petaling Jaya in a small rental in an old building where the landlord does not allow painting or drilling. Milo habitually sits or sleeps atop Priya's foldable side table, her favorite position for him. On November 4, 2026, Milo sat on the foldable side table while Priya reviewed app privacy settings and small-space decor, including in a post describing him as comfortable in that spot, later posts noting he had finished his "audit" session on the foldable rack, and one describing him as peaceful on the table.

nodes.name: Kuching Home Appliance Centre
nodes.summary: Kuching Home Appliance Centre is a small family-owned appliance retailer in Kuching, Sarawak, running a single showroom since 1995 (30 years in business). It sells large appliances including refrigerators, washing machines and air-conditioners, offering installation, delivery within Kuching, and reachable local after-sales service; it explains local warranty versus parallel import before payment and quotes delivery, installation and warranty in writing. It does not pay for online leads, relying instead on reputation, face-to-face showroom advice and after-sales, and asks for cost per qualified lead, iklan labels before the click, and a Best offer badge based on total landed cost (unit + delivery + installation + after-sales) and seller trust rather than paid placement. It notes Kuching's low volumes make cost-per-qualified-lead figures noisy and missed-demand data hard to read, and that shipping the same item to Sarawak can jump to RM80–150 with import tax versus a Klang Valley RM28.

nodes.name: shared projects with a partner
nodes.summary: Shared projects with a partner are planned for the next phase and are not available at beta.

nodes.name: aircond reviews
nodes.summary: Jason Reno went full-time on reviews after five years as a consumer electronics trainer, and aircond is where he sees the most "match dekat" heartbreak. He stresses that a "92% match" is a similarity score on a photo, not a model code, because 1.0HP vs 1.5HP and inverter vs non-inverter units can look identical in a frame. His rules: screenshot both indoor and outdoor stickers and read the full model code; match capacity to room size and electrical load and ask about earthing, especially in old houses; get the total through installation and testing in writing and itemised (unit, delivery by poskod, piping, bracket, vacuum, breaker, labour); and confirm warranty in writing for parts, compressor and labour, local authorised vs parallel import, including whether warranty starts on purchase date or installation date and whether a third-party installer voids it.

nodes.name: safety checklist
nodes.summary: Vanessa Goh, working from the design side, has started putting a safety checklist in every handover pack because of clients such as Haslinda Omar and Balakrishnan Nair, who worry about gas and electrical risks from unknown sellers. The checklist reflects three rules she tells people: full model code on both stickers, capacity matched to the room, and total cost sampai pasang + test. For non-technical buyers she adds that for anything carrying risk — aircond, water heater, gas hob — a screenshot is never enough; the physical sticker, plug type, and warranty card must be checked, and she will not recommend an appliance she has not seen switched on.

nodes.name: Thinesh Kumar
nodes.summary: Thinesh Kumar, 31, lives in Rawang and was scammed online once (RM2,300 lost in 2021); he questions every external link before tapping and advises checking the domain first and trusting later. He warns about fake courier notices (Pos Malaysia, J&T, Ninja Van) sent via WhatsApp and SMS, noting real couriers never ask for OTP or card details through a link; victims should call their bank, report to NSRC (997), and screenshot everything. He tells users to check whether an app is official or an affiliate wrapper, that Shopee and Taobao links earn someone commission, that room photos are personal data, and to test with one harmless photo of a plant before scanning an actual home; if unclear, don't scan. He advises verifying total cost (item, shipping, installation, import charges, delivery days, return window) before trusting any "Best offer" badge, asking sellers for fees in writing, and walking away from limited-time pressure.

nodes.name: ConsumerTrust
nodes.summary: ConsumerTrust is a hashtag used by Dr. Salina Rahmat in a comment on Rumah Lengkap Marketing's listing hygiene checklist, alongside #CommissionDisclosure. Her related point: if any recommendation or placement is paid, the label goes before the click, not in the fine print, because disclosure is a relationship, not a disclaimer.

nodes.name: Haslinda Omar
nodes.summary: Haslinda Omar is a safety-conscious person in the Klang Valley interviewed by Dr. Salina Rahmat. She always asks who installs, a habit that saved her from surprises. Dr. Salina Rahmat cites her as an example in discussions of consumer disclosure: safety-conscious Haslinda Omar always asks who installs, and this habit saved her from surprises. Bintang Elektrik and Vanessa Goh also name Haslinda Omar, alongside Balakrishnan Nair, as a neighbour who worries about gas and electrical installations from unknown sellers; Vanessa Goh puts a safety checklist in every handover pack because of clients like her and Balakrishnan Nair.

nodes.name: Budget Reno Bro
nodes.summary: Budget Reno Bro posted a "WEEKEND CHECK-IN — East Malaysia represent!" message addressed to homeowners and renovators of Sabah and Sarawak, advising them to check local suppliers first and compare total landed cost (unit price + shipping to their postcode + installation + warranty coverage). The post warned that a "2-4 day" delivery from a KL warehouse routinely becomes 1-2 weeks once it crosses the South China Sea, and urged asking for realistic transit days and courier coverage for KK, Kuching, Sandakan, Sibu, Tawau, Miri, and rural postcodes. It advised knowing who services warranties locally, since an authorised service centre within reach beats a longer warranty paper covering only Semenanjung. It required contractor warnings to come with documentation (invoices, dates, photos, messages), with unverified accusations removed, and encouraged before-and-after photos, supplier recommendations, and group-buy interest to cut shipping costs.

nodes.name: content credit
nodes.summary: Rina Kecil Living worries that apps profit from her content without crediting her; she wants creators to receive credit for their content.

nodes.name: retention period and permanent delete
nodes.summary: Jason Reno Journal requires a retention period stated before upload in plain BM and English, plus a delete that actually deletes; he tests the delete function with a small table photo before scanning real items. Chua Li Ting asks what the retention period is and whether deletion is real and permanent, stated before upload; after uploading a photo of her children's room to a scan-and-suggest app and feeling uneasy about who could see it and whether it was used for AI training, she deleted it and tested the delete button with a plant photo first, adopting the rule 先删，再决定 (delete first, then decide).

nodes.name: Rina Kecil Living's reading nook
nodes.summary: Rina Kecil Living styled a cozy reading nook in only 1.5 sqm using a thrifted rattan chair, a warm lamp, and a favorite plant, presented as proof that a big home is not needed to live big.

nodes.name: Pos book
nodes.summary: Pos book is the physical book in which Rosli Ahmad, an online buyer and small trader running a motorcycle workshop in Kangar, Perlis, stores screenshots of all chats, tracking information and dates related to his orders. His pre-purchase checklist requires the total landed cost to installation plus delivery and tax, the full model code on the sticker with screenshots of both sides, real delivery days by postcode with the seller's written confirmation for Kangar, and warranty terms in writing covering parts and labour, with all chats, tracking and dates screenshotted into the Pos book. He cited a February order for a sprocket set from Shah Alam listed at 2-4 working days that was still at the Petaling Jaya hub on day 12, with the seller saying Perlis is usually slower, and he lost one customer job because the motorcycle could not be finished on time.

nodes.name: Mudah
nodes.summary: Mudah is an online marketplace that Wong Kar Fai plans to open and compare against Shopee and Lazada before trusting any Best offer badge. In a November 4, 2026 Penang price-checking note, Wong Kar Fai listed Shopee, Lazada, Mudah, Harvey Norman, SenQ and one neighbourhood shop among the places he checks for a fridge purchase, comparing unit, delivery, installation, warranty and trade-in, and saving offer links to update when he finds something better. In another post that day he listed Shopee, Lazada, Mudah, Courts, SenQ and two small Penang shops as the sources he checks before signing.

nodes.name: cane furniture
nodes.summary: Chua Li Ting said honest tags on cane furniture help most: cane type, dimensions in cm (W x D x H), seat height, and whether it is self-collect or delivery to Kajang/Selangor. She asked whether she could come see and sit on it first before buying, preferring to support a small workshop with real craft over a faceless listing. On 2026-11-04 she raised questions about how long room photos and scan history are kept, whether deletion is permanent, and whether the service can be used as a guest without signing in with a real name, saying she tests the delete button with a dummy plant photo before trusting any scanner.

nodes.name: budget room makeovers series
nodes.summary: Nadia Home Diary is a home decor creator in Shah Alam whose audience is mostly young women and B40 families decorating rentals. She is planning a series on budget room makeovers for B40 families and offers to share real landed totals to Sabah/Sarawak as data points (with permission and credit, always). She tests affiliate links in her bio and refuses to hide them, holding that disclosure is a relationship, not a disclaimer, and that provenance should include a consent/credit/compensation share published beside precision and recall. She argues the metric that matters is precision@1 on the exact model code rather than top-1 category, that nearby-identical units must be in the labelled test set, that a confident wrong tag costs followers money, and that each region (Kuching, Sibu, Kangar, Kota Bharu, Klang Valley) deserves its own row. Her stated positions include rewarding recall that abstains, showing "no match" when unsure, and "Check local first."

nodes.name: cost-per-lead
nodes.summary: Cost-per-lead is a merchant metric that Rimbun Rattan Crafts said would help the workshop a lot if made transparent, alongside verified listings. Rimbun Rattan Crafts, a small family rattan workshop in Melaka, expressed willingness to test small.

nodes.name: South China Sea
nodes.summary: The South China Sea is the crossing that separates Peninsular Malaysia from Sabah and Sarawak. A "2-4 day" delivery from a KL warehouse routinely becomes 1-2 weeks once it crosses the South China Sea, plus a few more days for interior or rural areas; Sabah Sarawak Home Group and Malaysia Reno Kaki advise asking for realistic transit days for KK (88xxx), Kuching (93xxx), Sandakan (90xxx), Sibu (96xxx), Tawau (91xxx), Miri (98xxx), and rural postcodes. Jason Reno Journal and Sim Kok Leong cited "5-year warranty" papers that stop at the South China Sea as having zero value to a buyer in KK or Sibu. Farah Zainal noted the Peninsular "aggregate" shipping rate hides the failure mode of RM40 becoming RM180 once it crosses the South China Sea; Sinar Home Marketplace repeated that a KL warehouse's "2-4 hari" can become 2 minggu. Joanne Sia, a Miri homeowner, reported that a pendant light arrived cracked from poor packaging and now asks sellers for extra protection before shipping to Sarawak.

nodes.name: group buying
nodes.summary: Group buying is proposed in the Sabah Sarawak Home Group weekend check-in as a way for East Malaysian homeowners and renovators to cut shipping costs together by posting group-buy interest. Rumah Bajet MY echoed the call, asking East Malaysia shoppers to share their experiences so group-buys can cut costs together, and to check total landed cost (item + shipping + assembly) rather than the Semenanjung rate. Rumah Bajet MY repeated this across Twitter posts referencing Budget Reno Bro: get 3 quotes, screenshot everything, compare the total landed cost, and tag the page in honest finds and flops. Melissa Anak Jimbun, posting from Kuching, endorses the group-buy idea, saying that if there are enough participants they can share a container and cut shipping; she keeps a spreadsheet of landed costs (unit + shipping to Kuching postcode + installation + warranty servicer) after being quoted RM800 just to ship a 3-seater sofa from Taobao.

nodes.name: Best offer
nodes.summary: Best offer is a deal offering that Wong Kar Fai, 48, of Georgetown, tests against his own search to check whether it is really the best deal.

nodes.name: Bintang Elektrik
nodes.summary: Bintang Elektrik is addressed by Kuching Home Appliance Centre, which thanked Bintang Elektrik for a checklist covering points 1–5 that matches the showroom's daily conversation. Kuching Home Appliance Centre added an East Malaysia line to that checklist: for Sabah/Sarawak, always ask for the total landed cost by postcode, since import tax and delivery days are real and "installation included *conditions apply*" often means not for East Malaysia; for bulky items (fridge, washer, aircond), buy local where warranty and installation are handled by the same shop, because a parallel import with no service centre locally is the most expensive "cheap" deal.

nodes.name: Pos Malaysia
nodes.summary: Pos Malaysia is a courier whose name is used in fake delivery-notice scams sent by WhatsApp and SMS. Thinesh Kumar identified pos.com.my as the official domain, warning that scam links use lookalike or shortened domains instead. Real couriers such as Pos Malaysia never ask for OTP or card details through a link to release a parcel.

nodes.name: Hafiz Ismail's condo
nodes.summary: Hafiz Ismail furnished a 950 sq ft condo in the Klang Valley. The condo's lift door measures 90cm, which he cites as a reason to include lift booking and door clearance in total landed cost and to measure before paying.

nodes.name: Sabah
nodes.summary: Sabah Sarawak Home Group is an East Malaysia (Sabah and Sarawak) homeowners' and renovators' community that maintains a pinned admin note on the Casella scan-and-link app public beta. Its core position: the biggest worry is whether "delivery + installation + import charges" truly covers the East Malaysia leg, and it urges always asking whether a "total" includes shipping to Sabah/Sarawak plus import tax and installation, warning that sticker price alone is the trap and comparing with trusted local suppliers in KK (Kota Kinabalu) and Kuching before deciding. It stresses postcode-specific pricing rather than a single "Sabah/Sarawak" rate — KK (88xxx), Kuching (93xxx), Sandakan (90xxx), Sibu (96xxx), Tawau (91xxx), Miri (98xxx) and rural interiors all differ, including courier coverage — and that a KL warehouse's "2-4 days" typically becomes 1-2 weeks across the South China Sea.

nodes.name: content creators
nodes.summary: Content creators react to shoppable rooms, affiliate income, and credit for their content. On 2026-11-04 in the reno-kaki community spaces, Rina Kecil Living posted that the "TOTAL LANDED COST or nothing" approach applies to her 600 sq ft rental and to creator standards: when an app or brand wants to use a creator's content, the total landed cost is permission plus credit plus fair pay, under #CreditCreators.

nodes.name: Zarina Yusof's gas stove
nodes.summary: Zarina Yusof is seeking a replacement gas stove for her kitchen in Kota Bharu, Kelantan, because her old stove has shown signs of wear and rust on the burner knobs, and she wants everything settled before raya. On 2026-11-04 she repeatedly asked Kelantan neighbors for honest sellers who genuinely deliver to Kota Bharu (postcode 15200), not merely "Semenanjung," requesting shop names, days to arrival, any extra Kelantan charges, installation, and a locally claimable warranty, including for stoves, refrigerators, kitchen tools, and furniture. She asks every seller whether they deliver to 15200, how many days it takes and whether there are extra Kelantan charges, and whether installation and warranty can be handled locally; she keeps screenshots of delivery policies before buying anything and values honesty about shipping limits over large discounts, saying that if a seller cannot deliver to Kelantan, she does not want to hear about price.

nodes.name: Muar sofa seller
nodes.summary: A sofa seller based in Muar, referenced as comment 271, is asked by Melissa Anak Jimbun to provide a written total landed cost by poskod plus honest delivery days.

nodes.name: Priya Nair's landlord
nodes.summary: Priya Nair's landlord forbids major changes to the Petaling Jaya property Priya Nair rents.

nodes.name: Kangar, Perlis
nodes.summary: Kangar, Perlis (postcode 01000) is the location of a commenter responding to Farah Zainal's post on total landed cost. The commenter cited the same problem there: sellers advertise 2-4 day delivery, but the reality is 12 days, with tracking stuck in Petaling Jaya, and sellers answer queries with "Perlis slalu lambat boss." The commenter argued that a quote without shipping and correct transit days by postcode is not a cheap price but an unfinished one, and asked that Sarawak, Sabah, and Perlis all be included, with real dates rather than self-satisfied ones.

nodes.name: Rajesh Pillai
nodes.summary: Rajesh Pillai is 47 and renovating the kitchen of his 18-year-old terrace house in Klang on a tight budget (cabinets, countertop, sink, hob, hood, tiles, built-in oven; water damage under the sink). He requires total landed cost — unit price plus delivery, installation and import tax — not sticker price, and asks whether installation is included, hidden charges (delivery, hacking, disposal), warranty length and coverage, and whether the seller has a physical shop in Klang with recent buyer photos. He was charged RM350 extra to install a fridge bought online, faced an RM600 delivery charge revealed at the last minute, and received a leaking tap from a Shopee seller with 12 reviews who refused return shipping. He checks review count, review recency, buyer photos, physical address and warranty terms before any deposit. For gas appliances he insists on a trained/certified installer, leak test, and the regulator/hose standard; a friend had a bad stove experience.

nodes.name: Nilai
nodes.summary: Nilai is named by Lim Wei Jie as part of the after-sales service coverage area he requires, alongside Seremban, for a built-in oven or gas hob he is selecting for a Seremban 2 terrace house kitchen. On 2026-11-04 Lim Wei Jie reiterated that his criteria are stated dimensions in mm (W x D x H) plus cut-out dimensions, warranty length and coverage, installation included by a qualified installer, and after-sales service coverage in the Seremban / Nilai area; he also sought to be added to Seremban / Nilai groups covering kitchen appliance specifications, renovation contractor reviews, or gas appliance safety.

nodes.name: hand-woven stool
nodes.summary: A hand-woven stool is a rattan piece that adds warmth to a room, weighs little to shift when moving, and requires no nails in a landlord's wall, making it suited to renters who cannot drill or paint.

nodes.name: ir account
nodes.summary: An ir account allows photos to be uploaded, and uploaded photos expire automatically.

nodes.name: aircond replacement
nodes.summary: Faizal Rahim is looking to replace his 9-year-old 1.5HP aircond in the master bedroom in Shah Alam, prioritising cooling capacity, energy efficiency, good installation, and clear warranty covering parts, compressor, and labour. He asked for a trusted installer around Shah Alam and for a quote stating whether standard installation, piping, brackets, and labour are included, and whether warranty stays valid if a third-party installer is used. Joanne Sia, in Miri, Sarawak, added the concern of whether an installer covers East Malaysia at all, since many quote only for Peninsular and then charge extra for labour and brackets; she advised asking for a written quote covering standard installation, piping, brackets, labour, and disposal of the old unit, and confirming the compressor/parts warranty in writing if a third-party installer does the work, sebab some brands void it.

nodes.name: Puchong
nodes.summary: Sinar Home Marketplace is an online-only Malaysian home goods seller based in Puchong, running mostly on Shopee. It compares portal leads against its current Shopee advertising return and treats cost per qualified lead (real WhatsApp enquiries and showroom visits) as the only metric that survives scrutiny; it has offered to share its Shopee ROAS baseline and to act as a voluntary test client for a 30-day protocol. It asks that any paid Partner or commission slot be labelled as iklan before the click, that "Best offer" badges never be buyable and reflect total landed cost (unit + delivery + installation + after-sales), and that lead verification separate genuine buyers from bots, with full data purge before customer photos are collected. It also seeks per-class accuracy and labelled test-set publication before "92% match" claims are treated as fact.

nodes.name: Xiaohongshu
nodes.summary: Xiaohongshu hosts renovation groups that people use when trying to identify where an item is from.
