People also ask "where is this from?" in comments there, alongside Google Lens, image search inside Shopee and Taobao, Facebook renovation groups, interior designers, contractors, showrooms and neighbourhood shops. Cheah Xin Yi, 26, in Kuala Lumpur, reads Xiaohongshu daily and compares results with links shared in comments there.

nodes.name: computer-vision match accuracy
nodes.summary: Computer-vision match accuracy is the claim that a room photo maps to a SKU, which Grace Chin argues must be measured with a defined metric: top-1 category accuracy versus retrieval precision@1 on the exact model code are different numbers. She requires the labelled test set construction to be stated and the false-match rate between near-identical units published, citing a 2019 "beats Google Lens" claim that collapsed when the test set turned out weighted toward the vendor's own training data. Ah Boon Fix It, testing the Casella beta, found match accuracy hit-or-miss and showed failures where a kitchen photo suggested a cabinet that did not fit and a sofa that did not fit, and asks for a benchmark before trusting a "92% match" claim, including false-match rates between near-identical units such as 1.0HP vs 1.5HP and NR-BX418VS vs a lookalike. Nadia Home Diary notes a "92% match" is a similarity score, not a model code, and checks it herself before recommending.

nodes.name: My Home
nodes.summary: My Home is a feature where users save items into rooms of a renovation project, grouped as Considering, Decided or Bought.

nodes.name: Muhammad Hazim
nodes.summary: Muhammad Hazim is 35 and lives in Johor Bahru; he shops for home appliances on both sides of the Causeway, comparing JB prices against Singapore stores including Courts, Harvey Norman, Gain City, Best Denki and Mustafa, and finds the scan app's coverage limited because it shows either JB listings or Singapore listings rather than both. On 2026-11-04 he wrote that "92% match" is not a model code and that he photographs the indoor and outdoor stickers side by side and records the full model number in a spreadsheet before comparing.

nodes.name: solid rubberwood
nodes.summary: Solid rubberwood is named as one of the distinct material specifications that "kayu" fails to capture; MDF, solid rubberwood, and veneer on ply are three totally different sofas that can share the same photo.

nodes.name: Syafiq Hamdan
nodes.summary: Syafiq Hamdan is 32, lives in Sungai Petani, Kedah, in a terraced house with a young child, and has a modest budget and a family home to refresh. He keeps a Google Sheet called "Rumah SP Bajet" with columns for item, shop, price, shipping, voucher, total and delivery days, plus screenshots of promised dates and chat logs; the kitchen cabinet refresh is the second item under an RM5,000 plan (local seller, 4.8 rating, 1.2k sold, RM289 total including shipping to Sungai Petani, 7-day delivery against a listing that said 2-4 days, 14-day return window, RM12 voucher plus free shipping). He scans on Casella but then opens Shopee manually, retypes the model code and compares the total, not trusting match badges or "92% match"; a hidden RM15 shipping charge once appeared only at checkout, and a TV cabinet arrived with a damaged corner and was replaced under the 14-day return policy.

nodes.name: Casella app
nodes.summary: Casella app opened a public beta in Malaysia on 2026-11-04, announced by Malaysia Reno Kaki along with an admin guide warning users to CHECK PRICE for total landed cost (delivery + installation + import tax, not sticker price), noting the app earns affiliate commission from Shopee/Taobao links (acceptable if disclosed but requiring self-verification), distrusting the "Best offer" badge unless verified against units at local stores, and stating it is a non-official consumer mutual-aid platform that stays neutral in disputes and fact-checks before posting. Malaysia Reno Kaki requires paid Partner slots to be labelled clearly as iklan and asks members to report undisclosed ads to admin for fact-checking, calling transparency non-negotiable.

nodes.name: Cyberjaya studio unit
nodes.summary: Amirah Zulkifli is a 27-year-old setting up a small studio unit in Cyberjaya, her first studio unit, at Unit 12-3, where a rattan reading corner is her whole Pinterest board (Tiny Unit Ideas). She keeps her Unit 12-3 Wishlist in her Notes. She searches by cane type, size in cm (L x D x T), seat height, self-collect or delivery, and the real total cost sampai rumah including delivery and any installation. She asked whether she could come and sit first and whether a compact chair fitting a 1-bedroom could be offered, saying cute is still expensive for her and honest prices are needed. One scan app quoted a "compact sofa" at RM899 sticker, but delivery to her poskod plus "installation included *conditions apply*" pushed it past RM1,100. For her bed and wardrobe at Unit 12-3 she wants pasang included, since once installed it stays and she is not strong enough to handle a flat-pack alone.

nodes.name: small-space renting
nodes.summary: Rina Kecil Living addressed small-space renters on 2026-11-04, saying documentation protects renters from "2-4 hari jadi 12" the same way it protects creators from content theft — same skill, different battlefield. She urged every small-space renter and creator to keep receipts and screenshots and to ask for the total landed cost of a purchase and of their worth, under hashtags #CreditCreators, #CheckPrice, and #smallspaceliving.

nodes.name: BUDGET ROOM MAKEOVER UNTUK B40
nodes.summary: BUDGET ROOM MAKEOVER UNTUK B40 is a new series announced by Nadia Home Diary, based in Shah Alam, covering rented rooms and small condos with budgets under RM500. Nadia asked followers to share real total landed costs, especially for Sabah, Sarawak, Kelantan and Perlis, so comparisons can be made apple-to-apple, with contributors credited. The series follows Nadia's stated rule of total landed cost first and sticker price later, and she is building a small Linktree/website to organize recommendations with full details such as model code, dimensions and price delivered to the home.

nodes.name: Klang shop
nodes.summary: Kedai Perabot Seri Jaya operates a furniture shop in Klang. The shop quotes the price it states with no buried markup, and it is careful with any platform or "featured" placement. It asks that paid reviews or paid slots be labeled clearly with the numbers shown, and as a small business it needs to see ROI rather than ambiguity. The shop's message to furniture buyers is to ask what they are really paying for, under the tagline "Quality You Can Trust" and a call to support local.

nodes.name: No proof, no ringgit
nodes.summary: Rumah Bajet MY is the admin of a group with 50k+ members and uses "No proof, no ringgit" as the group's motto, stating it backs a 30-day protocol 100%. The admin pairs the motto with the discipline of screenshotting full model codes, calculating total landed cost, checking delivery days by postcode, and keeping chats and tracking. In a benchmark context the admin states "No benchmark, no trust; no proof, no ringgit." The admin asks that cost per qualified lead be broken down by postcode/state because leads in Kuching or Kangar differ from Klang Valley leads once shipping and delivery days are counted, and that a full delete test be a prerequisite before any house photos are collected. The admin requires provenance on how much training data came from creator or user images with consent, credit and compensation, and while no benchmark is out, buyer discipline stays unchanged.

nodes.name: Dr. Salina Rahmat
nodes.summary: Dr. Salina Rahmat researches commission disclosure and trust in Malaysia. She endorsed three standards for platforms: creator credit and compensation when images are used for listings, demos or AI training; a clear retention period and a real permanent delete stated before upload in plain language rather than buried in a T&C; and commission disclosed on every link before the click. She holds that disclosure is not a disclaimer but a relationship, and that the same standard demanded of sellers should apply to the platform. She identified finding out only when a follower tagged you as the trust break seen in her interviews, and summarized the principles as credit where it's due, consent before use, and label before the click. She conducted a survey of 120 Klang Valley consumers and interviews with buyers in Klang Valley, Penang and East Malaysia, finding that early, plain disclosure usually holds conversion and trust better, not worse.

nodes.name: User 37
nodes.summary: User 37 authored the Sabah Sarawak Home Group weekend check-in post for homeowners and renovators in Sabah and Sarawak, advising them to check local suppliers first and compare total landed cost (unit price, shipping to their postcode, installation, warranty coverage). The post warns that a "2-4 day" delivery from a KL warehouse routinely becomes 1-2 weeks once it crosses the South China Sea, and asks for realistic transit days and courier coverage for KK, Kuching, Sandakan, Sibu, Tawau, Miri, and rural postcodes. It also advises knowing which authorised service centre services the item locally, requiring documentation (invoices, dates, photos, messages) for contractor warnings since unverified accusations are removed, and sharing before-and-after photos, supplier recommendations, and group-buy interest to cut shipping costs. Malaysia Reno Kaki amplified the post and added its own admin voice to User 37's list.

nodes.name: actual unit inspection
nodes.summary: Hafiz Ismail will not proceed if the seller does not let him see the actual unit, because photos can hide flattened foam, the real smell, and the true colour; if you don't sit in it, you don't know.

nodes.name: kitchen cabinet refresh
nodes.summary: The kitchen cabinet refresh is the second item under Syafiq Hamdan's Rumah SP Bajet plan, which is capped at RM5,000. Syafiq reported a local seller with a 4.8 rating and 1.2k sold, a total of RM289 including shipping to Sungai Petani, delivery in 7 days rather than the 2-4 days stated in the listing, a 14-day return window, and a stacked RM12 voucher plus free shipping. He advised writing out total RM, shipping, delivery days, and warranty, and skipping listings that hide RM15 shipping until checkout, and asked for links to cabinet sellers that ship to Kedah.

nodes.name: Budget Reno Bro
nodes.summary: Budget Reno Bro works at a hardware store and posts in the Malaysia Reno Kaki community. Budget Reno Bro's weekend check-in post for Sabah and Sarawak homeowners advised checking local suppliers first, comparing total landed cost (unit price + shipping to the buyer's postcode + installation + warranty coverage), asking for realistic transit days and courier coverage for KK, Kuching, Sandakan, Sibu, Tawau, Miri and rural postcodes, confirming who services the warranty locally, requiring documentation (invoices, dates, photos, messages) for contractor warnings, and sharing before-and-after photos, supplier recommendations and group-buy interest to cut shipping costs.

nodes.name: Taobao Kaki Malaysia
nodes.summary: Taobao Kaki Malaysia is a Twitter community where members discuss Taobao purchases and shipping, centered on comparing total landed cost rather than listed price. Melissa Anak Jimbun asked the group whether RM800 to ship a 3-seater sofa from Taobao to Kuching was normal, thanked Melvin Pang and others who replied, and posted a final decision on 2026-11-04: for bulky items, buy local. The Taobao sofa unit at RM1,450 plus RM800 shipping with no local warranty service came to RM2,250, versus RM2,680 from a local Kuching supplier delivered, installed and with walk-in service, a difference of RM430; she inspected the sofa at the warehouse in person before deciding. Taobao was judged fine for small items such as beadwork and kitchen tools but not for a sofa, with the shipping quote called the hidden tax nobody shows West Malaysia.

nodes.name: Cheah Xin Yi's spreadsheet
nodes.summary: Cheah Xin Yi keeps a spreadsheet for tracking purchases and adds genuine landed-cost numbers from the Malaysia Reno Kaki East Malaysia check-in thread to it. After a 2022 viral air fryer purchase in which the top comment's affiliate code was expired and "2-4 hari" shipping took 11 days, the spreadsheet records total landed cost (unit + postage to her postcode + installation + local warranty service). For rental-friendly items requiring no drilling, the Google Sheet holds price, review count and whether the poster replied in comments; she screenshots every promised date and the chat before paying. Before clicking any link she requires written cut-out/full dimensions (W x D x H in mm), the total landed cost, and the local warranty servicer, and she does not trust a comment link unless multiple users confirm it.

nodes.name: Budget Reno Bro
nodes.summary: Budget Reno Bro commented on Rumah Lengkap Marketing's post about a new home-furnishing portal, agreeing that zero users, zero traction and zero measured match accuracy means zero numbers to check, and that a channel unable to show figures is not a deal but a marketing line. Budget Reno Bro endorsed the 30-day beta test measuring cost per qualified lead against Facebook and marketplace baselines, publishing the numbers, and telling clients to spend elsewhere if it fails, with the rule "No proof, no ringgit." Budget Reno Bro highlighted the requirement that quotes include delivery and installation, including for Sabah and Sarawak postcodes, noting that a RM299 shelf with RM180 courier to KK plus RM300 install is actually RM779.

nodes.name: Suruhanjaya Tenaga
nodes.summary: Suruhanjaya Tenaga is named by Aisyah Rahman as the body whose certified personnel must perform installation of cooker hoods and gas hobs. Aisyah Rahman, a first-time buyer in Shah Alam, listed certified installation by Suruhanjaya Tenaga personnel as a non-negotiable safety requirement in her checklist for cooker hood and gas hob purchases.

nodes.name: Sandakan
nodes.summary: Sandakan is an East Malaysian destination named in Budget Reno Bro's weekend check-in post, which advises asking for realistic transit days and courier coverage for KK, Kuching, Sandakan, Sibu, Tawau, Miri, and rural postcodes. Malaysia Reno Kaki's admin pin repeated the warning that "2-4 hari" from a KL warehouse routinely becomes 1-2 weeks once it crosses the South China Sea, urging checks on realistic transit days for Sandakan and the other listed areas; that check-in post drew 40+ shares.

nodes.name: Check local first
nodes.summary: Rumah Bajet MY, admin of the 50k+ member group, calls "check local first" part of the group's DNA since the 2021 viral incident, in which a post exposed a Shopee seller using misleading images and the warning saved many members. The admin closes posts with "Check local first, guys!" and pairs the principle with point 5 of a shared checklist.

nodes.name: Klang Valley
nodes.summary: Sinar Home Marketplace is an online-only home goods seller based in Puchong that runs mostly on Shopee and identifies total landed cost — delivery plus installation plus import tax, not sticker price alone — as the only number that matters to a buyer in the Klang Valley or East Malaysia. It asks that any slot earning affiliate commission or paid Partner placement be labeled clearly as iklan, and it compares portal leads against its Shopee advertising return, finding verifiable leads win every time; it directs inquiries to a Shopee link and DMs. Dr. Salina Rahmat, drawing on what 120 Klang Valley consumers told her about when they notice paid recommendations, holds that a paid Partner slot is fine and the problem is ambiguity: the "ad" label must sit before the click in plain language rather than buried in a hashtag or bio, since learning of payment only after tapping through is the trust gap.

nodes.name: privacy-first app evaluation
nodes.summary: Chua Li Ting, a Kajang (Semenanjung) mum, applies the same rule to apps that she applies to sellers: unit price and features are the listing price, while the real cost is what data they collect, how long they keep it, and whether the delete button actually works. She advises testing an app with a dummy photo first, deleting before deciding, and asking for the retention period in writing the same way one asks for a warranty in writing. Her stated rule is "No documentation, no warning. No retention period, no upload."

nodes.name: visual accuracy benchmark
nodes.summary: The visual accuracy benchmark requires publishing measured visual accuracy, not just cost per lead, since the load-bearing claim is that a room photo maps to the correct SKU. The metric must be defined — top-1 category accuracy versus retrieval precision@1 on the exact model code are not the same — along with how the labelled test set was built and the false-match rate between near-identical units (1.0HP vs 1.5HP aircond; NR-BX418VS vs a lookalike; fabric codes for sofas). A "92% match" badge without a confidence score and a test set is decoration, not validation, and a confident wrong match costs more than no match; per-class and per-region accuracy is where aggregate numbers fall apart. Dr. Salina Rahmat frames it as a question of numbers, not cost, and Rina Kecil Living calls "3 free scans" a demo, not validation.

nodes.name: computer-vision SKU matching
nodes.summary: Grace Chin argued that a saving only exists if the two compared columns are the same item: the app did not just quote a price but made a claim that a room photo maps to a SKU, and RM89.90 shelf vs RM299 console is a fair price comparison only if both are genuinely the same object class. That is a computer-vision claim with measurable accuracy — define the metric (top-1 category accuracy vs retrieval precision@1 on the exact model code are different numbers), say how the labelled test set was built, and publish the false-match rate between near-identical units. A confident wrong match does not save RM237; it costs the item plus the return. Grace Chin cited a 2019 "beats Google Lens" claim that collapsed when the test set turned out weighted toward the vendor's own training data, so test-set construction is the first thing she inspects.

nodes.name: warranty terms
nodes.summary: Warranty terms must be confirmed in writing before payment, per Lim Wei Jie. For a 1.5HP aircond replacement in Shah Alam, Wong Kar Fai advises that many brands drop the compressor warranty if a non-authorised installer does the gas work, so that must be obtained in writing, and the quote should clearly state unit, standard installation (piping up to how many feet), brackets, labour, and old unit trade-in, with extra piping usually charged per foot. For a built-in oven and gas stove, Wong Kar Fai advises asking whether the warranty covers parts, labour, and gas valve. Malaysia Reno Kaki's PSA lists warranty (original versus parallel import) as part of total landed cost.

nodes.name: content theft documentation
nodes.summary: Content theft documentation is the practice of keeping screenshots as proof whenever apps or brands use someone's before/after photos without credit or pay. It protects creators from content theft, just as documentation protects renters from delivery promises of "2-4 hari" that become 12. The practice was framed alongside the #CheckPrice and #CreditCreators tags in the context of a 600 sq ft rental.

nodes.name: Azlan Musa's 1.5HP aircond
nodes.summary: Azlan Musa is looking to replace a 9-year-old 1.5HP aircond in the master bedroom in Shah Alam. His priorities are cooling capacity, energy efficiency, good installation, and clear warranty covering parts, compressor and labour. He asked for a trusted installer around Shah Alam and for quotes stating whether standard installation, piping, brackets and labour are included, and whether warranty stays valid if a third-party installer is used.

nodes.name: Joanne Sia
nodes.summary: Joanne Sia is 38 and lives in Miri, Sarawak, where she has few local stores and treats shopping and lifestyle apps as a window into what she cannot find locally. She asks sellers for the total landed cost to Miri in writing: unit price, postage to Sarawak postcodes, import tax, installation, and who services the warranty locally, and she wants delivery days shown by postcode for Sarawak rather than a "nationwide" label. After a pendant light arrived cracked from poor packaging, she asks sellers for extra protection before shipping to Sarawak, screenshots promised dates and keeps chat logs, and keeps a small notebook of measurements before buying anything for the house; for gas and electrical work she checks reviews and a proper installer rather than app badges. She tested Casella's three free scans, said most such apps show only Peninsular offers with postage excluded, and checks the app nightly; she is willing to join group buys with Miri neighbours to split shipping.

nodes.name: Sibu
nodes.summary: Sibu is a city in Sarawak, East Malaysia, and the home city of Justin Ling, 22, a CS student there who posts from Sibu. Justin installs and deletes apps quickly, gives each app a single attempt, judges apps in about 10 seconds, and prizes minimal, fast, honest design over splash-screen lag, ads, forced sign-ups and permission grabs; he paid RM60 to ship a RM45 item to Sibu. He holds that "total landed" for Sibu must mean real postcode shipping to Sarawak plus import tax and installation in the same line items (not a Klang Valley number with "nationwide" slapped on), that a room-photo app's "92% match" is a demo rather than a validation set until per-class accuracy and a false-match rate between near-identical units are published, and that delivery latency must hold on the hardware and connections East Malaysians actually use. He tests app deletion with a plant photo first and uninstalls on any ad or sign-up wall mid-scan.

nodes.name: Melvin
nodes.summary: Melvin is a cross-border agent through whom Vanessa Goh has brought in samples; after shipping, duties and the lack of local servicing, the lookalike items stopped looking cheap.

attributes.name: Melissa Anak Jimbun's sofa shipping quote

nodes.name: Melissa Anak Jimbun's sofa shipping quote
nodes.summary: Melissa Anak Jimbun, commenting from Kuching, holds a quote of RM800 just to ship a 3-seater sofa from Taobao to Kuching, before import tax and installation. Melissa previously ordered a wardrobe online where West Malaysia got a much cheaper rate while Sarawak had to pay more. Melissa asks sellers to provide written line items: unit + shipping to Sarawak + import tax + installation + after-sales, and to state whether a "Best offer" total follows the poskod or is a Klang Valley number labeled "nationwide". Melissa also holds that paid Partner slots must be labeled "iklan" before the click.

nodes.name: Kuala Lumpur
nodes.summary: Kuala Lumpur is the home city of Hafiz Ismail, a 34-year-old new homeowner who sees large items in person before buying and compares total landed cost rather than listing price. Other Kuala Lumpur residents include Vanessa Goh, an independent interior designer; Cheah Xin Yi, 26, who reads Xiaohongshu daily; Lau Kok Wai, 42, who refuses to sign in for most apps and uses 3 guest scans before leaving; and Dr. Salina Rahmat, a marketing lecturer who watches how people respond to commission disclosure. Hafiz Ismail confirmed his KL postcodes behave well for delivery and applies four checks: unit price, shipping to the buyer's own postcode rather than a "Peninsular rate", whether installation is included, and who services the warranty locally; for sofas he adds seat height, seat depth and door/lift clearance.

nodes.name: Budget Reno Bro
nodes.summary: Budget Reno Bro responded to Faizal Rahim's request for advice on replacing a 9-year-old 1.5HP aircond in a Shah Alam master bedroom, framing the decision around total landed cost rather than unit choice. For a Shah Alam 1.5HP swap, Budget Reno Bro gave Daikin/Panasonic inverter unit prices of RM1,450–1,900 depending on where bought, standard installation of RM300–450 (usually including 3m copper piping, drainage, bracket, vacuum and test run), extra piping at RM18–25 per foot beyond 3m, old copper pipe replacement at RM150–250, and a separately charged electrical point/isolator at RM80–150 if not existing. On warranty, Budget Reno Bro advised that standard installation normally keeps the manufacturer warranty valid, but many brands honour full warranty only with their authorised installer, so a third-party installer can void the labour portion even when compressor/parts coverage is 5–7 years; the dealer should be asked in writing what is voided.

nodes.name: Hannah Lau
nodes.summary: Hannah Lau is hunting for a bed, wardrobe, compact sofa, and study desk, all rental-friendly and suited to small spaces at honest prices. She keeps saving inspiration for these items and has not yet checked out. She endorsed the idea that "the cheapest item is not the cheapest item," and she posted about the hunt under #smallspaceliving.

nodes.name: Kamala Devi's brother
nodes.summary: Kamala Devi suggests asking her brother to check for you if you are not sure.

nodes.name: data purge
nodes.summary: Sinar Home Marketplace states that a full data purge before any customer photos are collected is non-negotiable, tied to the principle "No proof, no ringgit."

nodes.name: Kedah
nodes.summary: Syafiq Hamdan is based in Sungai Petani, Kedah, where he uses Casella's room-scanning app, then manually reopens Shopee to compare prices. He advises not trusting the match badge and instead checking total RM, shipping to Kedah, delivery days, the return window and seller rating; he considers the 3 free scans fine for trying the app. He recalled an app showing a "best offer" that only revealed RM15 of hidden shipping at checkout. His 30k-adjacent practice involves scanning, closing the app, retyping the model code, and comparing the landed total including delivery to Kedah; he presses sellers on full model code, total cost including installation, and warranty coverage. He keeps the "Rumah SP Bajet" Google Sheet and has shared kitchen-cabinet-refresh updates such as a local seller rated 4.8 with 1.2k sold, total RM 289, 7-day delivery and a 14-day return window.

nodes.name: tenant rights
nodes.summary: Priya Nair, a renter in Petaling Jaya, seeks a tenant or small-space living community and named tenant rights, deposits withheld without reason, and apps that hide data practices as the topics she wants to hear stories about, saying she is ready to learn and share. Her routine is to scan as a guest first, check permissions, and reject location access without reason, under the principle "Check before you click." Her fuller posted checklist adds checking language options (she requested Tamil for one furniture app), ensuring scan history and data can be deleted, and screenshotting privacy policies as reference. She refers to her cat Milo resting on a foldable side table.

nodes.name: reliable-seller list
nodes.summary: Farah Zainal's tip is to save a reliable-seller list of sellers who give flat-rate or free shipping to Sabah, and to share the bad ones too as honest pro-consumer reviews without defamation.

nodes.name: Seremban/Nilai area
nodes.summary: Lim Wei Jie asked for a genuine review with actual dimensions from anyone in the Seremban/Nilai area who had completed a kitchen appliance purchase recently with full specs and installation included.

nodes.name: Chan Mei Fong
nodes.summary: Chan Mei Fong is a 56-year-old homemaker in Klang who usually buys appliances from one trusted local shop whose owner remembers her name, and uses apps only to check a price before visiting. She keeps a small notebook recording app prices on one page and shop prices on the other, and her rule since the 1998 financial crisis is "must touch first, then buy": see the display unit, check the full model code and warranty, ask whether delivery, installation and old-unit removal are included, then ask the shop to match the app price. She never clicks buy online for big items, and insists the total landed cost (unit + delivery + installation + warranty + trade-in) be given in writing with parts and labour cover. She screenshots prices and dates, checks postcode-based delivery promises, and distrusts "92% match" badges and hidden fees.

nodes.name: merchant portal
nodes.summary: The merchant portal has been announced. Local merchants and retailers react to it through verification, listing products, local-first matching, leads, dashboards, quotes, and the Partner slot. Kedai Perabot Seri Jaya, a family-owned furniture shop in Klang operating since 1985, joined the merchant portal and found the CSV upload a headache; after listing full prices (item plus delivery plus installation) and clear materials (solid rubberwood, MDF, veneer), repetitive questions fell and cost per lead dropped without added spend. The shop also stressed the importance of a lead tracker to justify ROI and compare channels.

nodes.name: SIRIM
nodes.summary: SIRIM certification is required for gas appliances before purchase, per Budget Reno Bro's advice to a Seremban/Nilai renovator. Budget Reno Bro advised confirming SIRIM and BOMBA certification and ensuring the installer is a registered gas contractor rather than any wireman, and to walk away from sellers who cannot provide the certificate. Azlan Musa's appliance specification table adds a column for SIRIM and standard hose and regulator for gas appliances, with a certified installer. Azlan Musa also advised confirming SIRIM and standard parts for gas and air-conditioning units, without which warranty may be voided.

nodes.name: Johor Bahru
nodes.summary: Johor Bahru is the home base of Muhammad Hazim, 35, who cross-shopped in Singapore (Courts, Harvey Norman, Gain City, Best Denki, Mustafa) and asks the app to compare both sides of the Causeway on total landed cost, GST, exchange rate and Malaysia-versus-Singapore warranty. Halim Yaakob, an air-conditioning installer, is based in Johor Bahru and asks for total installed price, model code on the sticker, and who services the local warranty. Sri Mutiara Home Centre is a family-owned furniture store in Johor Bahru operating since 2005, offering living room sets, dining tables, bedroom furniture and home decor, with delivery and assembly; it is minutes from the Causeway, open 10am–8pm, quotes total cost (unit price + delivery + assembly), asks Singaporean customers across the border, and requires verified leads before committing to any pay-per-lead model. Bintang Elektrik in Seremban and others in the threads discuss JB alongside the Johor market.

nodes.name: rental-friendly decor
nodes.summary: Priya Nair, posting from Petaling Jaya, is a renter, small-space living enthusiast, and privacy-settings enthusiast seeking a renter or small-space living community; she offered to share rental-friendly decor tips and app privacy guidance. She wants conversation especially about tenant rights, deposits withheld without cause, and apps that hide data practices. Her stated routine is to scan as a guest first, check permissions, and reject location access without reason; she also checks language settings and ensures data can be deleted. Her rental-friendly decor principle is small items that can be moved rather than drilled. She plans to read and understand a group before joining rather than joining blindly. Milo, her cat, is comfortable on the foldable side table.

nodes.name: Google
nodes.summary: Google is one of the sign-in options offered to guests, alongside Apple, phone OTP and email, when saving items or performing a 4th scan. Guests get 3 free scans without an account; saving items or a 4th scan requires signing in with Google, Apple, phone OTP or email. Grace Chin holds that Google's lead in general image search rests on billions of labeled images, years of refinement, and infrastructure most startups cannot touch, and that a startup can win in a niche with a specialized, well-curated dataset without beating Google at general search. She frames the gap between a startup and Google as almost never the model but the data pipeline and evaluation discipline, and cites a fashion visual-search startup that could not close the gap with Google Lens. Google's lead is real, but Chin argues a team need not beat Google — only be undeniably right in a domain Google does not care about.

nodes.name: gas stove installation safety
nodes.summary: Lim Wei Jie's engineering checklist for gas stoves: confirm the gas type (LPG vs piped), the hose/regulator standard, and that installation is done by a certified person, since cheap upfront plus DIY installation is a safety risk rather than a saving. For any built-in appliance, cut-out dimensions (cabinet opening width, depth and airflow clearances) matter more than external ones, as a unit can look like a "92% match" and still not fit a cabinet.

nodes.name: Faizal Rahim's spreadsheet
nodes.summary: Faizal Rahim's spreadsheet has total cost as column #1: unit price plus installation (piping, brackets, labour) plus warranty coverage, never the sticker price. Faizal Rahim is replacing a 1.5HP aircond in Shah Alam.

nodes.name: 3-seater sofa
nodes.summary: Hafiz Ismail considered buying a 3-seater sofa last month but had not yet bought it, not wanting to pay for style without substance. A Klang Valley local store: unit RM1,890 + RM80 two-storey delivery within the valley + RM0 assembly (included) + RM0 lift booking = RM1,970, with the option to sit, measure seat height (45cm) and seat depth (58cm), and see fabric swatches. An online-only model that looks premium in photos: unit RM1,690 + RM180 shipping + RM150 white-glove assembly + RM60 lift booking = RM2,080, more expensive with no way to inspect cushion density, frame, or smell. For B40 rental units on a tight budget, self-assembly plus self-collect (own van rental) can save RM150–250, provided there is a frame warranty and removable cover.

nodes.name: customer photo reviews
nodes.summary: Rumah Bajet MY's tip of the day is to always open the reviews with photos rather than just the 5-star text ones, because real customer pics tell you the true size, colour, and finishing, especially for furniture and lighting; a listing with only studio shots is a red flag, and some items look very different in real life. Lim Wei Jie agreed that real customer photos are the only reliable reference when listings omit specifications, with the rule that before buying any furniture or appliance the photo must show the item next to a measurable reference (tape measure, A4 paper, standard tile) and the listing must state actual dimensions in mm, not just "large" or "slim"; studio shots alone are meaningless.

nodes.name: small space furniture selection
nodes.summary: Rina Kecil Living's guidance for choosing furniture for a small space, specifically a 600 sq ft rental, is that the sofa is the biggest commitment, so frame wood and foam density matter more than the pretty photo. The advice is to measure twice, sit before buying, and support local makers who tell you what is inside, since honest materials plus local after-sales equal real value; a sofa that sinks in 6 months is not affordable but expensive. The guidance was shared in response to Vista Sofa Factory Outlet's four-point sofa checklist covering frame wood, foam density, fabric and stitching, and delivery plus warranty.

nodes.name: false-match rate
nodes.summary: Grace Chin requires the false-match rate to be published before a "92% match" badge can be trusted, because in retail a confident wrong match costs more than no match. She frames this as a computer-vision accuracy claim: a room photo must map to the correct SKU, and that has a measurable accuracy. She asks for three things to be published: the metric itself defined (top-1 category accuracy versus retrieval precision@1 on the exact model code, which she states are not the same number); how the labelled test set was built, including whether near-identical units such as 1.0HP vs 1.5HP aircons or NR-BX418VS vs NR-BX418XSB were included (citing a 2019 "beats Google Lens" claim that collapsed when the test set turned out weighted toward the vendor's own training data); and the false-match rate between near-identical units.

attributes.name: Azlan Musa's terrace house in Kuantan

nodes.name: Azlan Musa's terrace house in Kuantan
nodes.summary: Azlan Musa is renovating a terrace house in Kuantan stage by stage, one room at a time, buying items on a schedule that can lag two to three months after saving them in an app. He said the "92% match" tag is dangerous for this reason: by the time he installs, the tagged unit may be a different series. Before paying he requires the full model code on the indoor and outdoor stickers, an itemised total through installation and testing (unit, delivery to his Kuantan postcode, piping, bracket, vacuum, breaker, labour), and warranty terms for parts, compressor and labour, local authorised versus parallel import, plus whether warranty starts at purchase or installation. He does not compromise on water heaters and gas hobs, requiring a trained installer, leak test, and regulator/hose to standard.

nodes.name: PJ
nodes.summary: PJ is where Priya Nair rents a two-bedroom flat in which she is not allowed to drill or paint, so her approach to furnishing is versatile, movable pieces such as rattan.

nodes.name: Tiny Unit Ideas
nodes.summary: Tiny Unit Ideas is a Pinterest board that Amirah Zulkifli follows, centered on a rattan reading corner for the small studio unit she is setting up in Cyberjaya.

nodes.name: verified listing
nodes.summary: Rosli Ahmad supports verified listings combined with local-first matching if they require sellers to state real delivery days by postcode/state, such as "Perlis, add 2-3 days", before checkout, rather than promising 2-4 days for all of Malaysia.

nodes.name: slow renovation
nodes.summary: Hafiz Ismail's rule is that a saved room is inspiration, not a purchase trigger: he saves rooms as a shortlist, then sees the big stuff in person. For sofas he does not buy from photos only; he measures, sits, checks fabric, then decides, under the tag #SlowReno. His standing questions are whether there is ready stock or made-to-order lead time, seat height and seat depth in cm, whether installation is included or self-collect, and whether the actual unit can be viewed and sat on.

nodes.name: Check Local First
nodes.summary: Rumah Bajet MY's three points are total landed price (shipping to Sabah/Sarawak plus import tax plus installation, not sticker price), paid Partner slots labelled "iklan" before the click, and checking local first by comparing with trusted shops in KK, Kuching, Perlis and Kelantan. Rumah Bajet MY asked commenters to drop their landed totals to compare apple-to-apple, using #CheckLocalFirst. Sarah Thevi said to check local first but also make the app recognise local items.

nodes.name: Rimbun Rattan Crafts
nodes.summary: Rimbun Rattan Crafts is a small family workshop in Melaka making handmade rattan furniture and home decor since 2015, describing itself as a humble collective of artisans; it questions whether handmade items can ever match a similarity search. It states that every woven piece has small variations — a hand-tied knot, a sun-deepened shade, a cane-following curve — so no two baskets or chairs are identical and a photo lookalike is never the same piece in hand. The workshop invites customers to see, touch and feel the weave before deciding, and says it quotes total cost openly: material, hand-weaving time, delivery to the buyer's postcode (including Sabah and Sarawak rates), and who repairs it later. It asks that any paid Partner slot be labelled clearly as iklan front and centre, that the "Best offer" badge stay based on total cost and seller trust rather than paid placement, and that verified listings and transparent cost-per-lead be provided; it would be glad to test small.

nodes.name: Midea/Xiaomi rice cooker
nodes.summary: Kevin Lim searched for a 1.8L Midea/Xiaomi rice cooker last week, but the first result was a mismatched Taobao electric kettle with a voltage plug issue and no clear RM total. He deleted the app in 2 minutes, saying the first result must be correct or he deletes; he would reinstall if match badges improve, but for now goes back to Shopee, image-searching one item at a time and checking seller ratings, delivery days, and warranty.

nodes.name: plant-photo habit
nodes.summary: Rajesh Pillai endorses testing the delete button with a plant photo first, on the basis that photos of one's home are not free data, and summarises the rule as "No proof, no ringgit." Dr. Salina Rahmat likewise backs keeping the plant-photo habit, adding that users should ask for the retention period in writing and not scan if it is unclear.

nodes.name: Sabah
nodes.summary: Sabah and Sarawak are the East Malaysian states at the center of a landed-cost discussion. Hafiz Ismail asked friends in Sabah and Sarawak to share their total landed costs, citing logistics as a real factor rather than a slogan. The Sabah Sarawak Home Group weekend check-in post advised checking local East Malaysian suppliers first and comparing total landed cost (unit price + shipping to postcode + installation + warranty coverage), noting that a "2-4 day" delivery from a KL warehouse routinely becomes 1-2 weeks once it crosses the South China Sea, that warranty service must be reachable locally, and that contractor warnings require documentation (invoices, dates, photos, messages) with unverified accusations removed.

nodes.name: per-class accuracy benchmark
nodes.summary: The per-class accuracy benchmark is the sixth showroom-checklist item that Grace Chin said a vendor, not a buyer, should publish. It must define the metric — top-1 category accuracy versus retrieval precision@1 on the exact model code are different numbers — state how the labelled test set was built, and publish the false-match rate between near-identical units such as NR-BX418VS versus a lookalike and 1.0HP versus 1.5HP. Grace Chin said she inspects test-set construction first, recalling a "beats Google Lens" claim that collapsed in 2019 when the test set proved weighted toward the vendor's own training data. Farah Zainal and Justin Ling likewise demanded per-class accuracy instead of a bare "92% match", with Justin Ling deciding only after the benchmark.

nodes.name: Ariff Danial
nodes.summary: Ariff Danial is a budget renter in the Klang Valley who was interviewed by Dr. Salina Rahmat. He screenshots every price, a habit that saved him from surprises.

nodes.name: registered gas fitter
nodes.summary: For a built-in oven and gas stove purchase, Wong Kar Fai advises confirming the installer is a registered gas fitter, not just the shop's delivery man, as a gas safety check. Lim Wei Jie's requirement for a Seremban 2 terrace house kitchen renovation is that installation be included in the price, with proper gas fitting non-negotiable for safety.

nodes.name: delete button
nodes.summary: Justin Ling's checklist asks whether the delete button actually deletes rather than hides. Sarah Thevi asked where room photos go, how long they are kept, and whether delete is permanent.

nodes.name: 2021 viral Shopee seller post
nodes.summary: A 2021 viral post exposed a Shopee seller using misleading images; Rumah Bajet MY states the warning saved many of its members and that the incident shaped the group's "check local first" and total landed cost principles.

nodes.name: Klang Valley
nodes.summary: The RM 28 shipping quoted for a TV console is a Klang Valley number; per the Sabah Sarawak Home Group admin, the same console can cost RM 80-150 to ship to Sabah/Sarawak with import tax, and "installation included *conditions apply*" often means not for East Malaysia.

nodes.name: KK suppliers
nodes.summary: KK suppliers are local suppliers in KK (Kota Kinabalu) that the Sabah Sarawak Home Group advises members to compare against before committing to a purchase.

attributes.name: Aisyah Rahman's condo in Shah Alam

nodes.name: Aisyah Rahman's condo in Shah Alam
nodes.summary: Aisyah Rahman bought a 750sqft condo in Shah Alam that is due to be completed in two years. She is working to a tight budget of RM30,000 and scans, compares prices, and saves screenshots before buying anything. She dislikes non-transparent pricing and confusing labels, and buys only from shops that are honest, easy to ask questions of, and support local brands. Her advice is to request written quotations, compare total landed cost, and not be shy about asking. In November 2026 she shared this home journey publicly, saying she is a first-time condo owner, and added that she will now also check the full model code on the sticker (indoor and outdoor), capacity against the room, and total cost through installation and testing, so as not to be misled by "92% match" claims.

nodes.name: Budget Reno Bro
nodes.summary: Budget Reno Bro posted a weekend check-in on Twitter addressed to homeowners and renovators in Sabah and Sarawak, advising them to get quotes from local East Malaysian suppliers and compare total landed cost: unit price plus shipping to their own postcode, installation, and warranty coverage. The post warned that a "2-4 day" delivery from a KL warehouse routinely becomes 1-2 weeks once it crosses the South China Sea, and asked for realistic transit days and courier coverage for KK, Kuching, Sandakan, Sibu, Tawau, Miri, and rural postcodes. It also advised confirming who services the warranty locally, since an authorised service centre within reach beats a longer warranty paper covering only Semenanjung. Contractor warnings must come with documentation such as invoices, dates, photos, and messages, and unverified accusations are removed. The post invited before-and-after photos, supplier recommendations, and group-buy interest to cut shipping costs.

nodes.name: SenQ
nodes.summary: SenQ is a retailer that Wong Kar Fai includes among the places to check the same appliance model against, alongside Shopee, Lazada, Mudah, Courts, Harvey Norman and smaller Penang shops, before deciding on a purchase. Wong Kar Fai checks Shopee, Lazada, Mudah, Courts, SenQ and two small Penang shops before signing, and advises Penang buyers this month to compare unit, delivery, installation, warranty and trade-in at Shopee, Lazada, Mudah, Harvey Norman, SenQ and one neighbourhood shop. He cites a fridge advertised as a "Best offer" where delivery was extra, old unit removal was not included, and the warranty card was a parallel import.

nodes.name: Kuching suppliers
nodes.summary: Kuching suppliers are local suppliers in Kuching that the Sabah Sarawak Home Group advises members to compare against before committing to a purchase.

nodes.name: Lim Wei Jie's appliance
nodes.summary: Lim Wei Jie, a Seremban homeowner renovating his home, requires that any appliance listing publish the full model code and cut-out/clearance dimensions (W x D x H), not just a photo, and state whether installation is included and by whom; for gas appliances he treats this as a safety issue rather than a pricing issue. A contractor built a cabinet without checking his appliance dimensions, and the mismatch cost him far more than any "saving".

nodes.name: compact chair
nodes.summary: Amirah Zulkifli asked whether a small-space size could be offered — a compact chair that fits a 1-bedroom — for her Cyberjaya studio unit, noting that cute is still expensive for her and asking for honest prices.

attributes.name: Rina Kecil Living's 600 sq ft rental

nodes.name: Rina Kecil Living's 600 sq ft rental
nodes.summary: Rina Kecil Living's 600 sq ft rental is a small apartment near KK or Kuching. Rina Kecil Living's rule for it is total landed cost, whether an item fits, who services it locally, and whether the seller can be reached if something breaks; a paper warranty that cannot be reached counts as zero. Rina Kecil Living applies the "check local first" advice to small spaces, noting that a tiny apartment near KK or Kuching faces the same "2-4 days becomes 2 minggu" trap. On 2026-11-04, Rina Kecil Living's small-space checklist is: does it fit ("measure twice, angkat sekali"), unit plus delivery plus installation as the real number rather than the listing price, who services it locally, and whether the seller can be reached if something breaks. Rina Kecil Living adds that for creators the "total landed cost" of their work is permission plus credit plus fair pay, and that a repost skipping all three means footing the bill for someone else's profit.

nodes.name: labelled test set
nodes.summary: Grace Chin requires the labelled test set to be published before she would trust the beta, including how it was built and whether near-identical units were included. She cites a 2019 "beats Google Lens" claim that collapsed once the test set turned out to be biased toward the vendor's own training data, and states that test-set construction is the first thing she inspects, not the last. She also asks for the false-match rate between near-identical units such as 1.0HP vs 1.5HP aircond and NR-BX418VS vs a lookalike.

nodes.name: Dr. Salina Rahmat
nodes.summary: Dr. Salina Rahmat posted that disclosure is not a disclaimer but a relationship, urging buyers to ask who paid for a recommendation and whether they would still trust it if they knew. She holds that commission is legitimate while hidden commission is not, and that a plain label before the click — not buried in a hashtag or a bio — keeps trust intact. She framed the position as not anti-creator but anti-ambiguity, and called on Malaysian brands to test better disclosure before claiming it kills conversion. Her post carried the hashtags #CommissionDisclosure, #InfluencerEthics and #ConsumerTrust.

nodes.name: match-quality threshold
nodes.summary: The "Partner" slot at position 2 of a list must pass a match-quality threshold; a slot that passes can never receive the Best offer badge.

nodes.name: Seremban
nodes.summary: Seremban is a Malaysian city that is home to Lim Wei Jie, 39, an engineer renovating a Seremban 2 terrace house kitchen and selecting a built-in oven and gas hob. He requires stated W x D x H dimensions and cut-out dimensions, warranty length and coverage, installation included by a qualified installer, and after-sales coverage in Seremban/Nilai; a contractor once built him a cabinet without checking his appliance dimensions and the mismatch cost more than any saving. Seremban is the base of Bintang Elektrik, an independent, small family-run appliance retailer operating since 2015 that competes on installation and after-sales service, fears price-only comparison, and invites customers to its showroom for demos.

nodes.name: Grace Chin
nodes.summary: Grace Chin authored a 9-item "listing hygiene" checklist for home sellers to fix before spending on ads or boost, with client names removed: full price versus displayed price (including delivery and installation costs, or a "from" price with installation explained); sizes in both cm and inches; exact material (MDF, solid rubberwood, veneer rather than just "wood"); delivery time by postcode zone ("3-5 days" is wrong for Kuching); actual stock status; three photos (full shot, material close-up, real-room shot); FAQs answered in the listing rather than in DMs; a single CTA (WhatsApp or form, not both); and a tracker showing where leads come from so cost per qualified lead can be calculated and channels compared. Grace Chin audits these items for clients before they touch an ad budget, and each time cost per lead drops without added spend because sellers stop paying for questions the listing can answer itself.

nodes.name: Uploaded photos
nodes.summary: Uploaded photos expire automatically.

nodes.name: IKLAN label
nodes.summary: The IKLAN label is a disclosure requirement for paid Partner slots and affiliate links in scan-and-link shopping apps, to be shown in plain BM and English before the click, not in a hashtag or after the tap. Dr. Salina Rahmat, citing user 17's point, argued the problem is never the commission but finding out late, and that in her survey of 120 Klang Valley consumers and interviews with Klang Valley and East Malaysian buyers, early disclosure usually holds conversion better, not worse. Farah Zainal called the IKLAN label before the click a point she will never compromise on, and Ah Boon Fix It listed it as one of three non-negotiable items.

nodes.name: Casella photo deletion feature
nodes.summary: Ah Boon Fix It tested the Casella app's photo deletion feature after Chua Li Ting raised a data privacy concern. Photos can be deleted, but the delete option is buried three menus deep and there is no "delete all" option. Ah Boon also beta-tested Casella's side-by-side match: in one test 3 out of 5 suggestions were decent, but a photo of Ah Boon's kitchen still suggested a cabinet 20cm too wide, and a sofa match did not fit. Ah Boon earns a small affiliate commission when the buy button opens Shopee/Taobao and states this on every link before the click, in BM and English, and has turned down paid deals for untested products. Ah Boon asks that creator and small-shop images, such as those of Rimbun and the Muar sofa makers, get credit, consent and compensation before use, and that retention periods be stated before upload with a delete that really deletes.

nodes.name: Casella Partner slot
nodes.summary: Casella's later merchant phase for Malaysian stores includes one paid Partner slot per list, and that slot cannot receive the Best offer badge. The merchant phase is not available during the beta.

nodes.name: computer vision
nodes.summary: Grace Chin frames the claim that a photo maps to the correct SKU as a computer-vision problem with a measurable accuracy: per-category precision and recall for tagging, how the labelled test set was constructed, and the false-match rate between near-identical units such as 1.0HP versus 1.5HP ACs or the same sofa in a different fabric code. She holds that a 92% "match" badge without a confidence score and a benchmark is decoration — a similarity score, not a SKU identifier — and cites 2019 as showing how fast a "beats Google Lens" claim collapses under test-set inspection. The required publication items are the metric itself (top-1 category accuracy or retrieval precision@1 on the exact model code), the test-set construction including near-identical units (1.0HP vs 1.5HP; NR-BX418VS vs NR-BX418XSB), and the false-match rate, since a confident wrong match costs more than no match.

nodes.name: Processing
nodes.summary: Processing fills the photo across the screen and shows tags appearing one by one. The target is first tags in under 5 seconds, and after 30 seconds the app says it will notify the user.

nodes.name: Klang Valley
nodes.summary: Hafiz Ismail stopped by a shop in Klang Valley and found a salesperson who gave honest specifications: seat depth 58cm, foam 32 density, kiln-dried frame, and removable covers. Hafiz noted that most listings give a pretty render and zero numbers. He also compared East Malaysia versus KL sellers, cautioning that a "2-4 hari" delivery from a KL warehouse means nothing until it clears the sea.

nodes.name: Priya Nair
nodes.summary: Priya Nair is a 28-year-old renter in Petaling Jaya (a three-year tenant in an older building) whose landlord forbids drilling or painting; she buys only small, movable items such as foldable shelves, roll-up carpets, screwless stick-on mirrors and clip-on lamps, and has a cat, Milo, who sits on her foldable side table. Her rule is "Check before you click": test guest scan before signing in, deny unnecessary permissions (especially location), check language options and privacy controls, confirm scan history can be deleted, and screenshot the privacy policy. Testing a furniture app's guest scan for a small side table in AR, she denied location access (the scan still worked), tested deletion on a dummy photo of a plant, verified she could delete her scan history, and submitted feedback asking for Tamil because only English and Malay were offered; she did not sign in, needing only to look rather than give data.

nodes.name: data retention period
nodes.summary: Syafiq Hamdan of Sungai Petani, Kedah holds that a retention period must be stated before upload, with a delete that truly deletes, when a platform uses people's images for listings, demos or AI training. He also requires consent and credit before images are used, and affiliate commission labelled on every link before the click.

nodes.name: RumahBajetMY
nodes.summary: RumahBajetMY is a Malaysian online community focused on budget renovation, whose members discuss pricing, delivery, and buying discipline. Members include Budget Reno Bro, who uses the #RumahBajetMY hashtag, and commenters from Kuching, Kuantan, Kota Kinabalu, Klang, Kangar, and Kota Bharu. Recurring member demands are written line-item landed totals by poskod, "iklan" labels on paid Partner slots before the click, an unbuyable "Best offer" badge based on total landed cost, and published benchmark metrics. The community's stated principle is "no proof, no ringgit."

nodes.name: model code
nodes.summary: Full model code is a required disclosure for verified listings, alongside cut-out dimensions (W x D x H). Dr. Salina Rahmat noted a photo cannot read a model code and that near-identical units such as 1.0HP versus 1.5HP AC look the same in a photo. Ah Boon Fix It advised screenshotting the full model code on both indoor and outdoor stickers side by side before tapping buy, and said a "match" that does not state who installs and how much clearance there is is advertising, not comparison.

nodes.name: Dr. Salina Rahmat
nodes.summary: Dr. Salina Rahmat studies disclosure timing for a living. She conducted a survey of 120 Klang Valley consumers and interviews with Klang Valley and East Malaysian buyers, finding that the trust break is almost never the commission itself but discovering it late, and that when the paid-slot label comes first the same recommendation often converts better. She advocates labeling paid slots IKLAN in plain BM and English before the click, not in a hashtag, bio, or after the tap. She proposed testing early-disclosure versus late-disclosure rather than only disclosed versus undisclosed, and flagged fair delivery dates by poskod, noting that a "2–4 hari" promise becoming day 12 is also a disclosure failure. She framed disclosure as a relationship rather than a disclaimer and used the tags #CheckLocalFirst and #CreditCreators.

nodes.name: Budget Reno Bro
nodes.summary: Budget Reno Bro posted a weekend check-in addressed to homeowners and renovators in Sabah and Sarawak, with reminders from the admin team: check local East Malaysian suppliers first and compare total landed cost (unit price + shipping to your postcode + installation + warranty coverage); a "2-4 day" delivery from a KL warehouse routinely becomes 1-2 weeks once it crosses the South China Sea, so ask for realistic transit days and courier coverage for KK, Kuching, Sandakan, Sibu, Tawau, Miri, and rural postcodes; know who services the warranty locally, since an authorised service centre you can reach beats a longer warranty paper covering only Semenanjung; contractor warnings must come with documentation (invoices, dates, photos, messages) and unverified accusations get removed; and members should share before-and-after photos, supplier recommendations, and group-buy interest to cut shipping costs.

nodes.name: Seremban 2
nodes.summary: Seremban 2 is the location of a terrace house whose owner shared a kitchen appliance buying checklist: get full dimensions (W x D x H, mm) and cut-out dimensions before confirming cabinet work, confirm installation is included in the price, check warranty length, coverage, and local servicing (Seremban/Nilai coverage), and verify after-sales support in writing before payment. The owner recounted that a contractor once built a cabinet without checking appliance dimensions and the result did not fit. Rumah Bajet MY endorsed the checklist, noting the decor-side pain that "10cm salah, seluruh kabinet tak muat." Lim Wei Jie, a Seremban 2 resident, sought recommendations for a built-in oven and gas stove for the house's kitchen renovation, requiring full and cut-out dimensions, warranty period and coverage, installation included in the price (proper gas fitting non-negotiable for safety), and after-sales service in the Seremban/Nilai area, refusing price-only replies.

nodes.name: Mustafa
nodes.summary: Mustafa is one of the Singapore retailers Muhammad Hazim of Johor Bahru compares against Johor Bahru options when shopping for electrical goods, alongside Courts, Harvey Norman, Gain City, and Best Denki. His comparison method weighs Johor Bahru versus Singapore listings, and he notes Singapore prices are sometimes cheaper even after exchange rate and transport, though warranty logistics usually lead him to buy in Johor Bahru.

nodes.name: WhatsApp
nodes.summary: WhatsApp leads are billable and appear in the merchant inbox.

nodes.name: sea freight
nodes.summary: Sea freight rates for tiles and long items are charged by volume, not weight, according to Ah Boon Fix It, a contractor commenting on the Sabah Sarawak Home Group's weekend check-in post. He advised East Malaysian buyers to group-buy with neighbours and split the container, stating he has saved clients thousands this way. The same post noted that a "2-4 day" delivery from a KL warehouse routinely becomes 1-2 weeks once it crosses the South China Sea, and Ah Boon Fix It said budgeting for that delay is the default rather than bad luck.

nodes.name: Tiffany Yeoh's 3-seater sofa
nodes.summary: Tiffany Yeoh's 3-seater sofa decision followed her question in Taobao Kaki Malaysia about whether RM800 to ship a 3-seater from Taobao to Kuching was normal; Melvin Pang and others replied. The Taobao option totaled RM2,250 (RM1,450 unit plus RM800 shipping) with no local warranty service. A local Kuching supplier offered RM2,680 delivered, installed, and backed by a warranty covering Sarawak. The difference was RM430. Tiffany drove to the warehouse to inspect the sofa in person before deciding. Her verdict: for bulky items, buy local, since the shipping quote is a hidden tax not shown to West Malaysia; Taobao is fine for small items such as beadwork and kitchen tools. In follow-up commentary on the sofa story, she added resale and repair as a comparison column: bulky Taobao pieces are hard to service, and replacement covers and foam almost never match once the listing disappears, while a local supplier means a new seat cushion is obtainable in three years.

nodes.name: Kamala Devi's late husband
nodes.summary: Kamala Devi's late husband said to get everything in writing, with parts, compressor and labour listed separately, and that anything not listed is not included.

nodes.name: TV console
nodes.summary: Justin Ling cited a TV console whose RM28 shipping is a Klang Valley rate; shipped across the South China Sea to Sarawak, the same TV console jumps to RM80–150 plus import tax, and "installation included *conditions apply*" almost always excludes East Malaysia. He advised screenshotting the total landed cost by postcode — item + delivery by postcode + assembly + tax — rather than the peninsula rate, and said buying local is cheaper. He also noted the app's "compact TV console" versus a shop's shelf plus bracket are different objects, so the comparison is fair only if both columns are the same item.

nodes.name: guest scan
nodes.summary: Priya Nair used guest scan in a furniture app to view a side table in AR without logging in. She checked permissions (denying location access; the scan still worked), language settings (only English and Malay offered, so feedback requesting Tamil was submitted), and privacy controls (confirming scan history could be deleted, testing the control on a dummy photo of a plant rather than her actual unit); all passed, but she did not sign in because she only needed to "tengok", not "bagi data". On 2026-11-04 she posted recommendations for friends: test guest mode before registering, read the permission list one by one and decline unnecessary ones, check language and privacy settings before trusting, screenshot the privacy policy as evidence, and commit to sign-in only if the retention period is stated plainly; she also holds that an undisclosed affiliate link is where trust leaks, so the "iklan"/"ad" label must appear before the click.

nodes.name: sofa buying
nodes.summary: Sofa buying guidance advises checking four things before buying a lookalike sofa online: frame wood (solid kiln-dried or thin plywood), foam density (soft seat that sinks in 6 months versus firm foam that holds its shape), fabric and stitching, and delivery plus warranty including who fixes a dented corner. The same sofa can carry a very different total cost, and customers are invited to sit on samples, WhatsApp for a quote, or visit the outlet where samples are available for testing. Vista Sofa Factory Outlet makes sofas in Muar and sells direct from its Muar outlet without hidden middleman markup; it states it discloses what is inside the sofa — frame wood, foam density, fabric — and what changes the quote, and asks buyers to compare specs rather than photos.

nodes.name: gas appliance safety
nodes.summary: Gas appliance safety is a check Bintang Elektrik adds beyond model-code verification: for aircond and gas stoves alike, installation must be done by a trained installer with proper vacuum, correct piping and a leak test, since a cheap install can void the warranty and create a safety risk. Bintang Elektrik, speaking from its Seremban showroom, advises asking for the total cost until installed and tested rather than the sticker price, and in a November 2026 post asked the Malaysia Reno Kaki community to add "certified installer + leak test" to its total-landed-cost checklist as the safety line rather than the price line, and to ask for the installer's name before payment.

nodes.name: batik cushion
nodes.summary: A batik cushion was among the items Sarah Thevi uploaded to a shopping app to test its recognition, alongside a teak mandir cabinet, a thali set, and a kolam rug. The app returned only generic labels such as "wooden cabinet" and "bohemian rug" and missed every cultural cue. Sarah Thevi, based in Klang, later cited the same test again, asking whether an app recognises Indian-Malaysian items and styles or just Western decor, whether it can explain its recognition logic, and whether the full deletion path can be tested before photos are handed over; pictures of her prayer corner and her parents' room are private.

nodes.name: Grace Chin
nodes.summary: Grace Chin argued that three questions in the thread should be answered in writing by the vendor rather than by the community: retention period, whether delete truly erases data, and whether the service can be used as a guest without a phone number, calling these policy questions rather than hard technical ones and holding that if they go unanswered before upload, users should not scan, with "delete first, then decide" as the correct rule and testing the delete button with a tree photo as methodology rather than a weakness. Grace endorsed "No proof, no ringgit," reasoning that one confident wrong match costs more than no match, and that for large furniture "Best offer" must mean total landed cost (unit + delivery by postcode + installation + after-sales), not a sticker price. Grace held that commission is not the problem but that buyers learn too late, and that ads must be labeled before the click in BM and English, since disclosure is a relationship, not a disclaimer.

nodes.name: Chua Li Ting's plant
nodes.summary: Chua Li Ting used a dummy photo of her plant to test the delete button of a home-organisation app that scans room photos before deciding whether to use it. The deletion worked, but the app's FAQ never stated the photo retention period.

nodes.name: Kamala Devi's son
nodes.summary: Kamala Devi's son told her about the Casella app. Kamala Devi, a 58-year-old homemaker in Taiping who says she is not good with technology and was cheated once online, will have her son show her the Casella app next month; she will not try it alone and will proceed only if it is easy to understand. She has raised concerns about where her room photos go, how long they are kept, and hidden fees, and wants the price shown to be the full total including delivery, installation and tax.

nodes.name: Casella
nodes.summary: Casella is a Malaysian home-item scanning app in public beta that tags room photos or screenshots with furniture and appliances, prices them, and links to offers on Shopee and Taobao. It offers 3 free scans without an account, and its Best offer badge is stated to be based on total cost including delivery, installation and import charges rather than sticker price. Beta testers reported that the Best offer badge does not appear for cheap items below a certain threshold, and Budget Reno Bro and Ah Boon Fix It reported a kitchen photo suggesting a cabinet that did not fit and a sofa match that did not fit. Sarah Thevi tested it with screenshots from local Indian-Malaysian home pages: a teak mandir cabinet returned as just "wooden cabinet", a kolam-patterned rug as "bohemian rug", a batik-inspired cushion and a stainless steel thali set missed, with the cultural cues missed; she also found the app only offers English and Malay, though her mother and grandmother read Tamil.

nodes.name: handmade rattan furniture
nodes.summary: Handmade rattan furniture and home decor is produced by Rimbun Rattan Crafts, a small family workshop in Melaka operating since 2015, positioned as locally crafted, sustainable rattan and Melaka heritage. Each piece has small variations — a knot tied by hand, a shade that deepens with the sun, a curve that follows the cane rather than a mould — character that cannot be captured by a photo or an algorithm. Customers can come see, touch and feel the weave before deciding. The workshop publicly questioned whether a handmade rattan piece can ever truly match a similarity search, asking how people discover local handmade pieces online and what words, tags or descriptions help find a small workshop. Rimbun echoed other local shops that any paid Partner slot must be labelled clearly as iklan front and centre, and that the

nodes.name: harga app
nodes.summary: Harga app is referenced by Melissa Anak Jimbun in a reply to Budget Reno Bro's East Malaysia weekend check-in, advising buyers to compare harga app against harga kedai for a fair comparison.

nodes.name: room photo credit and consent
nodes.summary: Room photos used by the app require credit and prior consent, with retention and real delete stated before upload. Farah Zainal stated her room photo is not free data, full stop, under #CreditCreators, and that the app using people's home photos must credit and ask permission first.

nodes.name: Facebook
nodes.summary: Facebook hosts renovation and home-decor groups used by people trying to identify where items are from and to share renovation advice, contractor warnings, price checks and shopping finds. Named Facebook groups include Malaysia Reno Kaki, described as a large renovation group, Rumah Bajet MY, a budget home-decor community that shares Shopee finds and warns about items differing from their photos, and Sabah Sarawak Home Group, a group on renovating in East Malaysia. Malaysia Reno Kaki pinned a spec-first quote template from Lim Wei Jie as an example, updated a trusted contractor list monthly from member feedback, and held a monthly live Q&A with industry experts from 8-11 PM on weekends; its East Malaysia check-in post drew 40+ shares.

nodes.name: sofa
nodes.summary: Sofas made in Muar are sold direct from Vista Sofa Factory Outlet, which advises checking four things before buying a lookalike online: frame wood (solid kiln-dried versus thin plywood), foam density (soft seat that sinks in 6 months versus firm foam that holds its shape), fabric and stitching, and delivery plus warranty covering who fixes a dented corner. For Sabah and Sarawak buyers, Vista Sofa Factory Outlet lists five total-cost items: unit price compared between app and local outlet, shipping to the buyer's postcode (a "2-4 day" KL warehouse delivery becomes 1-2 weeks once it crosses the South China Sea, and bulky freight is not cheap), installation (most outstation sellers do not carry it up), warranty (a paper covering only Semenanjung is worth zero), and frame, foam, fabric and stitching.

nodes.name: Klang Valley
nodes.summary: Klang Valley is the delivery and installation area served by Kedai Perabot Seri Jaya, a local family furniture business based in Klang since 1985 that stands behind the furniture it builds, invites customers to sit on its samples in Klang before deciding, and quotes openly. In November 2026 the shop applied a "total landed cost" principle to the area: before comparing with a cheap import, customers should add unit price, delivery to their own postcode, installation and who services the warranty. Hafiz Ismail asked whether there is a Klang Valley showroom or only a Muar outlet. Home decor creator Nadia Home Diary, based in Shah Alam, fields questions about posting to KK and Sibu, and Hannah Lau and Justin Ling in Sibu also endorsed the total landed cost checklist.

nodes.name: electrical load and earthing
nodes.summary: Faizal Rahim, replacing a 9-year-old 1.5HP unit in the master bedroom of an older Shah Alam house, asks about electrical load and proper earthing as part of his aircond purchase checklist. He requires written confirmation on installation and warranty before any deal, and will share landed totals once both quotes come in.

nodes.name: sofas
nodes.summary: Vista Sofa Factory Outlet, a sofa maker in Muar, advised East Malaysian buyers that sofas are bulky, so the total landed cost logic applies strongly: compare a local quote against an online listing on total landed cost rather than sticker price, and check shipping to the buyer's own postcode, since a "2-4 day" sofa delivery from a KL warehouse can become 2 weeks once it crosses the South China Sea and bulky freight is not cheap. Most outstation sellers do not cover installation, leaving that as extra cost and risk, and a paper warranty covering only Semenanjung is worth zero to East Malaysian buyers. Buyers should ask any seller, including Vista, for real delivery days, how the sofa is packed, and who services it if something goes wrong, and should compare specs — frame, foam, fabric, stitching — not just the photo, because local after-sales matters.

nodes.name: Daikin
nodes.summary: Daikin is one of the 1.5HP inverter aircond brands, alongside Panasonic and Midea, that Budget Reno Bro names in hardware-store price breakdowns. Budget Reno Bro's figures put 1.5HP Daikin/Panasonic/Midea inverter app pricing at RM1,500–1,900, with hardware or appliance shops at RM1,450–1,700, and a later quote placed Daikin/Panasonic 1.5HP inverter units at RM1,450–1,900 depending on where they are bought, advising buyers to check both app and kedai hardware prices. The brand appears in a Shah Alam replacement context for a 9-year-old 1.5HP master-bedroom aircond, where the quoted total landed cost covers unit, installation, piping, bracket, isolator, labour and warranty status.

nodes.name: content creation
nodes.summary: Rina Kecil Living keeps a folder of screenshots and receipts as a creator, used as proof when apps and brands use her before/after photos without credit or pay. On 2026-11-04 she framed this documentation as the same skill that protects renters from delivery delays, and urged creators to keep receipts and screenshots and to ask for the total landed cost of their worth, under #CreditCreators, #CheckPrice, and #smallspaceliving.

nodes.name: merchant inbox
nodes.summary: The merchant inbox is part of a merchant phase in which verified Malaysian stores can list products by form, CSV, or Shopee shop import; the inbox holds billable WhatsApp, quote, and showroom leads. Merchants also get a dashboard of impressions, clicks, leads, and missed demand, and users can request a quote from up to 5 stores when no exact match exists, with local stores that deliver to the user matched first in a Local stores tab.

nodes.name: Tawau
nodes.summary: Tawau is listed among the East Malaysian destinations for which Budget Reno Bro's weekend check-in post advises asking for realistic transit days and courier coverage, alongside KK, Kuching, Sandakan, Sibu, Miri, and rural postcodes. Malaysia Reno Kaki's admin pin repeated the warning that "2-4 hari" from a KL warehouse routinely becomes 1-2 weeks once it crosses the South China Sea, and urged checking realistic transit days for Tawau and the other listed areas. On 2026-11-04, Farah Zainal cited the claim that a single "delivery: 3-5 days" is wrong for KK, Kuching, Tawau and Sibu, noting the RM40 rate that becomes RM180 once it crosses the South China Sea. Sinar Home Marketplace's weekend post also repeated that "2-4 hari" from a KL warehouse can become 2 weeks crossing the South China Sea.

nodes.name: landed cost
nodes.summary: Farah Zainal's rule is that total cost sampai rumah equals item price plus shipping to Sabah plus any import/tax plus installation. She keeps a notebook with app price on one page and checkout total on the other, citing a phone case whose shipping reached RM50. She asked whether the "Best offer" badge shows total landed cost (delivery + installation + import tax) or sticker price only, calling sticker-only a trap, and said she would share her landed totals.

nodes.name: scan app
nodes.summary: The scan app is a photo-based tool for comparing listings against actual units. Chua Li Ting asked where room photos go, how long they are kept, whether they are used for AI training, and whether deletion is permanent or only hidden from view; she asked whether she could try as a guest without signing in with her real name, and said that if the retention period isn't clear she won't scan a single room. Vista Sofa Factory Outlet said a photo scan cannot show frame wood, foam density, fabric quality or stitching, calling a scan app a good starting point, not the final word. Sim Kok Leong said a photo cannot show the full model code on the sticker, citing 1.0HP and 1.5HP units that look identical in a picture.

nodes.name: Azlan Musa's spreadsheet
nodes.summary: Azlan Musa keeps a spreadsheet of receipts, dates and photos as evidence to be used when needed, not for making accusations.

nodes.name: Klang Valley
nodes.summary: Klang Valley is cited as the reference point for a RM28 shipping figure on furniture, a number that does not hold for East Malaysia. Vanessa Goh noted that for buyers in Kuching, shipping can jump to RM80-150 plus import tax, and that "installation included *conditions apply*" usually means not available for East Malaysia. Vista Sofa Factory Outlet, which makes sofas in Muar, said Peninsular delivery is straightforward while Sabah/Sarawak quotes are given honestly by poskod.

nodes.name: Google Sheet Rumah SP Bajet
nodes.summary: Syafiq Hamdan of Sungai Petani, Kedah keeps Google Sheet Rumah SP Bajet, recording every item he buys with columns item, shop, price, shipping, voucher, total, and delivery days, plus screenshots of promised delivery dates and chat logs. Listing "2-4 hari" typically becomes 10-12 days to Sungai Petani, so he demands real dates, not "tarikh syok sendiri."
