His pre-commitment checklist: open Shopee himself instead of trusting match badges, check shipping to his own postcode, confirm whether installation is included, and verify local warranty and return window; total landed cost (unit + shipping + install + warranty) counts over headline price, and he skips sellers who hide RM15 shipping until checkout. After a TV cabinet arrived damaged he used a 14-day return policy to file a claim and received a replacement. He calls the sheet his tracker, holding it to the same principle as cost-per-lead accounting.

nodes.name: vacuum and leak test
nodes.summary: Halim Yaakob advised asking the installer to write "vacuum + leak test included" in the quote, because without vacuuming moisture enters, the compressor fails early, and the warranty becomes a problem afterward. He also advised screenshotting the indoor and outdoor unit stickers, asking the total price through to the test, and measuring first before installing.

nodes.name: Ah Boon Fix It
nodes.summary: Ah Boon Fix It is a Chinese-language DIY YouTube channel run by an ex-contractor turned DIY YouTuber who writes in Malay, disclosing affiliate commission on every link before the click. He beta-tested the Casella app: match accuracy is hit-or-miss, with a kitchen photo suggesting a cabinet 20cm too wide and a sofa match that did not fit; 3 out of 5 side-by-side suggestions were decent; the "Best offer" badge does not appear for items below a certain threshold; photos can be deleted but the option is buried 3 menus deep with no "delete all"; the buy button opens Shopee/Taobao, making seller, courier and warranty holder three different parties. He built a cabinet from a Casella kitchen-inspiration suggestion that did not fit by 20cm, and he shows his failures on camera.

nodes.name: credit and consent
nodes.summary: Credit and consent is a requirement that a matched photo is someone's room or a creator's before/after, so the ad must be labelled, retention stated before upload, delete made genuinely permanent, and the original credited. Grace Chin pairs it with the hashtags #CheckLocalFirst and #CreditCreators. Nadia Home Diary states credit and consent for a maker's photos are non-negotiable for her and that she always labels her affiliate links before the click.

nodes.name: similarity search
nodes.summary: Rimbun Rattan Crafts is a small family workshop in Melaka making handmade rattan furniture and home decor since 2015, describing itself as a humble collective of artisans. It offers customers the chance to see, touch and feel the weave before deciding, and positions its work as locally crafted, sustainable rattan and Melaka heritage. The workshop has publicly asked whether handmade rattan pieces can ever truly match a similarity search, noting each piece carries small variations — a hand-tied knot, a sun-deepened shade, a curve that follows the cane rather than a mould — that no algorithm captures; it also asked how buyers discover local handmade pieces online and what words, tags or descriptions help them find a small workshop.

attributes.name: Rumah Lengkap Marketing's Casella beta post

nodes.name: Rumah Lengkap Marketing's Casella beta post
nodes.summary: Rumah Lengkap Marketing's Casella beta post argued that a photo tag is not a quote and that before trusting it, buyers should ask for the total landed cost: unit price plus delivery fee, installation, warranty (original or parallel import), and old-appliance trade-in. The post stated the delivery estimate must follow the real postcode, noting Georgetown 10200 is not 2-4 days if stock is in KL, and asked what the total price is. Rosli Ahmad agreed, saying the postcode point is the most important line, and cited waiting 12 days for a sprocket set from Shah Alam with tracking stuck in Petaling Jaya while the seller blamed Perlis delays despite a 2-4 day listing.

nodes.name: Apple
nodes.summary: Apple is one of the sign-in options offered to guests, alongside Google, phone OTP and email, when saving items or performing a 4th scan.

nodes.name: Budget Reno Bro
nodes.summary: Budget Reno Bro posts on Reddit about renovation and furniture pricing, emphasizing that "total" cost must be line-itemed: unit price, shipping by poskod, import tax, installation, and after-sales. Budget Reno Bro states that a seller refusing a written quote is the red flag, not the price, and that the best offer badge cannot be bought but must be calculated on total landed cost; during beta-testing the badge did not appear for cheap items below a certain threshold. Budget Reno Bro holds that a Paid Partner slot must be labeled "iklan" before the click, since disclosure is not a disclaimer, and advises buying local if the app's landed total is within 10-15% of the price at a KK/Kuching shop.

nodes.name: home-furnishing portal
nodes.summary: A new home-furnishing portal was the subject of a question put four times in one week to Farah Zainal: whether it should enter a client's budget. The answer was that it could not yet, because the portal had zero users, zero traction, and zero measured match accuracy, so it could not show cost per qualified lead. The draft proposal was a 30-day test with three volunteer clients (one Klang Valley, one Penang, one Kuching), measuring cost per qualified lead against their Facebook and marketplace baselines, with no exclusivity, no upfront payment, and a full deletion test before any customer photos are collected; if the test fails, the numbers are to be published and clients told to spend elsewhere. Privacy requires a testable deletion path for photos of children's rooms, and pricing quotes must include delivery and installation, including for Sabah and Sarawak postcodes.

nodes.name: gas appliance installation
nodes.summary: Gas appliance installation requires a trained installer and a leak test, which Hannah Lau and Kamala Devi both treat as a safety requirement rather than a sales point.

nodes.name: saved rooms
nodes.summary: Hafiz Ismail might use saved rooms as a shortlist but will not buy a sofa from a photo.

nodes.name: hand-tied knot
nodes.summary: Ah Boon Fix It, who fixes and builds things for a living, holds that no algorithm captures a hand-tied knot and it shouldn't try. For discovery, what works is boring, specific detail: cane type, dimensions in cm (L x D x H), seat height, finish, self-collect versus delivery, and the real total cost sampai rumah (item plus delivery plus any installation). Process photos of hands weaving build trust because people trust process, not polish.

nodes.name: Rumah Bajet MY
nodes.summary: Rumah Bajet MY is a Malaysian budget home-decor community with 50,000+ members described as "Kaki" that shares Shopee, Taobao and TikTok Shop finds, compares listings to real customer photos, and warns about items that differ from their photos. In 2021 a viral post exposed a Shopee seller using misleading photos, a warning credited with saving many members. Rumah Bajet MY asks sellers for full model codes on indoor and outdoor stickers (e.g. 1.0HP vs 1.5HP, NR-BX418VS vs lookalike), dimensions and clearance, total landed cost (unit + delivery by postcode + piping/bracket/vacuum/breaker/labour + import tax + after-sales), real delivery days by postcode, and written warranty covering parts, compressor and labour (local authorised vs parallel import).

nodes.name: Chan Mei Fong's washing machine
nodes.summary: Chan Mei Fong bought a washing machine; for that purchase she screenshotted the app price, brought it to a trusted shop, and asked the shop to match the price. She advises not simply believing "free installation" until it is written down.

nodes.name: Joanne Sia's pendant light
nodes.summary: Joanne Sia's pendant light arrived cracked because of poor packaging. Joanne Sia, a Miri, Sarawak homeowner, now always asks sellers for extra protection before shipping to Sarawak. She asks for unit price plus postage to her own postcode, installation, and which party services the warranty locally, all in writing before measuring anything, and she checks the app every night. She is open to group buys with Miri neighbours to split shipping, and supports sellers who reply with real measurements, cut-out sizes and honest postage.

nodes.name: trusted contractor list
nodes.summary: The trusted contractor list is updated monthly based on Malaysia Reno Kaki member feedback, per the admin announcement. A Malaysia Reno Kaki post dated 2026-11-04 repeats this and adds that live Q&A sessions with industry experts run every month, 8-11 PM peak, all weekend long. Kuching Home Appliance Centre's Kuching-based business, 30 years old, does not pay per lead and relies on reputation, face-to-face showroom advice, and reachable after-sales; it advises keeping a WhatsApp trail of quotations, payment receipts, and promised dates.

nodes.name: CreditCreators
nodes.summary: #CreditCreators is a hashtag used by Farah Zainal, a Sabah (Kota Kinabalu) homeowner, in posts about the Casella beta calling for fair rates and honest delivery dates by postcode for Sabah and Sarawak; her listed asks include total landed cost, an IKLAN label on paid Partner slots before the click, an unbuyable "best offer" badge based on total landed cost, clear photo retention with real permanent delete, and checking local suppliers first, plus credit and consent for creators' images. Ah Boon Fix It, a beta tester of Casella who fixes and builds things for a living and earns affiliate commission on links, holds that credit and consent for a maker's images are non-negotiable and that if a scan-and-link app lists a piece, the maker should know where it appears and who earns the commission on it.

nodes.name: Justin Ling's room photo
nodes.summary: Justin Ling's room photo is the test case for his dealbreaker that the delete button must actually delete the room photo rather than hide it; he advises testing with a plant first. He also requires that a single scan not throw an intrusive ad and that the sign-up wall not appear after the teaser demo, or he uninstalls with no retry.

nodes.name: #CreditCreators
nodes.summary: #CreditCreators is a creator-credit and fair-pay call associated with Rina Kecil Living, who urged fellow creators to always ask for credit and fair pay and to keep pushing for #CreditCreators. The hashtag drew support from creators, homeowners, sellers and small shops, including Malaysia Reno Kaki (whose admin stated the group fully backs #CreditCreators), Ah Boon Fix It (a Casella beta tester who tested the app's photo deletion feature), Dr. Salina Rahmat, Farah Zainal, Jason Reno Journal, Sinar Home Marketplace (a Puchong-based, mostly Shopee home goods seller), Bintang Elektrik (a family-run Seremban appliance shop since 2010), Sabah Sarawak Home Group (which pinned the framework for members), Nadia Home Diary, Vanessa Goh, Grace Chin, Chua Li Ting, Lim Wei Jie, Tilam Selesa Bedding (a Kuantan family mattress shop), Hannah Lau, Melissa Anak Jimbun, Amirah Zulkifli, Wong Kar Fai and others.

nodes.name: Chinese
nodes.summary: Chinese is one of the app's languages, alongside English and Bahasa Melayu.

nodes.name: Aisyah Rahman
nodes.summary: Aisyah Rahman is a 31-year-old first-time condo buyer in Shah Alam, buying a 750 sq ft unit due in about two years on a tight RM30,000 budget: Living Room RM10,000, Bedroom RM8,000, Kitchen RM5,000, Bathroom RM4,000, Others RM3,000. Her 'Rumah Impian' list holds a RM1,800 sofa, RM350 coffee table, RM200 rug, RM600 TV console (still considering) and RM150 curtains (decided); she has bought nothing yet and is waiting for the keys. She compares total landed cost (unit + delivery + installation + warranty) before buying, asks for written quotations, screenshots prices and dates, checks local shops before buying online, has compared sofa prices from three local shops, and now also checks full model codes on indoor and outdoor stickers and asks about piping per-foot rates and third-party installer warranty voiding. She has not signed in to the app because she wants to read the privacy policy first; she saves room tours and rarely knows item names.

nodes.name: Aisyah Rahman's rug
nodes.summary: Aisyah Rahman's rug is budgeted at RM200 in her 'Rumah Impian' plan. Nothing has been purchased yet; she is waiting for the house keys.

nodes.name: KL home shopping apps
nodes.summary: Lau Kok Wai tested three KL home shopping apps for a compact fridge during the week of November 4, 2026. Two of the apps asked for a phone number before showing the delivery fee, while one showed the price and delivery terms on the first guest scan without requiring login. Lau Kok Wai kept that no-login tab open, holding that a good deal should not cost your identity and that scanning first should be possible.

nodes.name: 1998 crisis
nodes.summary: Chan Mei Fong, 56, a homemaker in Klang, has followed a rule since the 1998 crisis: must touch first, then buy. She keeps a small notebook for prices, with app price on one page and shop price on the other.

nodes.name: Rumah Impian
nodes.summary: Rumah Impian is a photo album on Aisyah Rahman's phone. Aisyah Rahman is a first-time condo owner in Shah Alam with a tight RM30,000 budget who saves room tours and screenshots of checklists into the album, including a Total Landed Cost checklist (unit price + delivery to her postcode + installation + local warranty service); if a seller cannot give full figures in writing, she skips them. Her stated principle is that the advertised price is not the real price and total landed cost comes first, sticker price after. She checks local shops before buying online and considers affiliate commission labelled as advertising in BM and English before the click as something that increases her trust. She also keeps a Rumah Lengkap Marketing listing-hygiene checklist in the album, citing display prices that exclude delivery and installation as selling disappointment and vague material labels such as "kayu" as a problem.

nodes.name: Jason Reno Journal's gadget/review channel
nodes.summary: Jason Reno Journal runs a gadget/review channel and does a fair bit of DIY carpentry. For a workshop like Rimbun's, he said the tags that convert him are cane type, dimensions in cm (L x D x T), seat height, finish, and a real total cost sampai rumah (item + delivery + any installation), plus process photos rather than product-cantik-saja shots; he also said credit and consent for a maker's images are non-negotiable and buyers should know where a piece appears and who earns the commission.

nodes.name: measured match accuracy
nodes.summary: Jason Reno Journal demands that the measured match accuracy be made public: top-1 versus retrieval precision and the false-match rate, showing a benchmark rather than a "3 free scans" demo, because a confident wrong match costs more than no match.

nodes.name: appliance repair
nodes.summary: Sim Kok Leong spent 30+ years repairing appliances and applies the same rule to purchases: quote the total openly — material, labour, delivery, and who repairs it. He holds that what's inside and who stands behind it matters more than the photo, and that specs don't lie. He advises checking the model number first, then the price, and supporting local sellers where the item can be inspected and the maker spoken to.

nodes.name: Ibu Bapa Rumah Selamat
nodes.summary: Ibu Bapa Rumah Selamat is a group for parents. Ah Boon Fix It addressed a public service announcement to parents in the group, warning against buying cheap gas hoses and regulators from unknown online sellers to save RM20, since a leaking regulator can be fatal and some reviewed units failed basic pressure testing. The guidance was to prioritize safe materials and certified parts.

nodes.name: Seremban/Nilai
nodes.summary: Seremban/Nilai is the area for which Faizal Rahim sought a genuine review, with actual dimensions, from anyone who had recently completed a kitchen appliance purchase with full specs and installation included. Faizal Rahim's specification comparison method for built-in ovens, stoves, and hoods has columns for model number, dimensions (W x D x H in mm), cut-out dimensions for built-in items, power rating or gas type (LPG vs natural gas), warranty period and coverage, whether installation is included and who installs, and the nearest after-sales service location; if a seller cannot fill in even half of these, he moves on. Rina Kecil Living shared the same method and the same Seremban/Nilai area request. Aisyah Rahman endorsed the table method, adding warranty sub-columns (parts/compressor/labour) and installation specifics (piping, bracket, labour), and cited a case where a low price changed once delivery, installation, and extra piping were added.

nodes.name: Panasonic
nodes.summary: Panasonic is one of the appliance brands Sim Kok Leong, a 53-year-old former appliance technician in Muar, is comparing alongside Samsung; he intends to buy from a local shop he can walk into. Panasonic appears in the 1.5HP inverter aircond segment alongside Daikin and Midea: app pricing RM1,500–1,900, with hardware or appliance shops charging RM1,450–1,700. Budget Reno Bro cites Daikin/Panasonic inverter 1.5HP units ranging RM1,450–1,900 depending on where they are bought, and advises checking both app and hardware-store prices.

nodes.name: Jason Reno Journal
nodes.summary: Jason Reno Journal is a Malaysian Chinese YouTube gadget-review and DIY carpentry creator who discloses every affiliate link before the click, in BM and English, and holds that commission is legitimate but hidden commission is not, with "test first, trust later" as his stated rule. He turned down a RM10,000 affiliate deal in 2020 for an untested product ("Why I Said No to RM10,000"), and spent five years as a consumer electronics trainer before going full-time on reviews, a role that covered full model codes, itemised installation costs and written warranty terms. In November 2026 he probed the Casella scan-and-link app beta, asking for total landed cost (delivery, installation, import tax), measured match accuracy and per-link commission labels; he also asks sellers for landed cost to the buyer's postcode, realistic transit days to Sabah, Sarawak and other East Malaysian postcodes, and the name of a reachable local authorised service centre.

nodes.name: top-1 category accuracy
nodes.summary: Top-1 category accuracy is one of two candidate metrics Grace Chin requires the app to define before she would trust the beta, distinguished from retrieval precision@1 on the exact model code. She states the two are different numbers and that only retrieval precision@1 on the exact model code protects a buyer. She also calls for per-class and per-region accuracy, since aggregate numbers fall apart there. In later discussion Grace Chin frames a tester's report of a kitchen photo suggesting a cabinet that did not fit and a sofa match that did not fit as a category-correct, identity-wrong failure that would appear as a high false-match rate rather than a low top-1 score.

nodes.name: Rina Kecil Living's 2021 incident
nodes.summary: Rina Kecil Living's 2021 incident left her feeling violated and undervalued. She keeps a folder of screenshots, as always, in connection with it.

nodes.name: Perlis
nodes.summary: Perlis (postcode 01000, Kangar) is the focus of Rosli Ahmad, 50, of Kangar, who wants marketplace listings to show realistic delivery days for Perlis rather than claimed "2-4 day" delivery that in reality takes up to 12 days, with tracking sometimes stopping at Petaling Jaya. Rosli argues sellers' "nationwide delivery" claims add 2-3 days for Perlis and that Kangar is not a foreign country nor a KL suburb; he asks that real delivery days be shown by postcode before checkout, along with total cost including installation. On 2026-11-04 he commented on Casella's announced later merchant phase for Malaysian stores (verified listings, local stores matched first, a leads inbox, a dashboard, and one paid Partner slot per list that cannot receive the Best offer badge, not available during the beta), supporting local stores being matched first while questioning when the merchant phase arrives and whether Perlis delivery days will follow postcode.

nodes.name: User 6
nodes.summary: User 6's practical, tested advice checklist was added to Malaysia Reno Kaki's pinned library, as announced in a 4 November 2026 post. The checklist covers contractor warnings requiring evidence (invoice, date, photos, chat logs), checking total landed cost rather than listing price, especially for Sabah and Sarawak postcodes, and group-buying with neighbours to cut freight.

nodes.name: 1.5HP aircond
nodes.summary: Faizal Rahim is replacing a 9-year-old 1.5HP aircond in the master bedroom of his Shah Alam home, prioritising cooling capacity, energy efficiency, good installation, and clear warranty covering parts, compressor and labour; he keeps a simple spreadsheet to compare total cost per model rather than sticker prices and asks for quotes listing standard installation, piping, brackets and labour to avoid hidden fees. Azlan Musa advised requesting that quote breakdown, noting the compressor warranty is usually separate from labour and that a third-party installer may void the warranty, so the dealer should be confirmed first. Halim Yaakob added that buyers should check total landed cost (unit, delivery, installation, warranty) and require dimensions, model code and total installed price before comparing.

nodes.name: KLinterior
nodes.summary: KLinterior is a hashtag used by Vanessa Goh alongside #rumahku in her comment endorsing Rumah Lengkap Marketing's 9-point listing hygiene checklist for Malaysian furniture sellers.

nodes.name: rental-friendly furniture
nodes.summary: Rental-friendly furniture is the category Amirah Zulkifli is still hunting for Unit 12-3, alongside small-space and honest prices, covering a bed, wardrobe, compact sofa, and study desk. Hannah Lau shares the same hunt for a bed, wardrobe, compact sofa, and study desk, all rental-friendly, and keeps saving inspiration without checking out.

nodes.name: Kuching
nodes.summary: Kuching is a Sarawak city that recurs as an East Malaysian landed-cost problem. Homeowner Melissa Anak Jimbun, 35, of Kuching keeps a spreadsheet of landed costs and backs Kuching/Miri group buys sharing a container; her benchmarks are an RM800 Taobao quote to ship a 3-seater sofa to Kuching before import tax and installation, versus a local supplier quote of RM2,680 delivered and installed against RM2,250 for the Taobao route, and a 1.5HP air-conditioning unit priced at RM1,300 in Shah Alam landing at RM1,600+ in Sarawak before installation. She asks sellers to quote landed totals in writing by postcode with honest delivery days and to answer "free to WHERE?" Peninsula or Sarawak rate; she also describes an online wardrobe order where the West Malaysia rate was much cheaper and Sarawak buyers paid more.

nodes.name: audience trust
nodes.summary: Jason Reno Journal protects audience trust and is sceptical of products he has not tested.

attributes.content_niche: Home renovation and appliance buying advice
attributes.name: Budget Reno Bro

nodes.name: Budget Reno Bro
nodes.summary: Budget Reno Bro posts on Twitter about home renovation and shopping. Budget Reno Bro announced a new Malaysian app called Casella, which opened a public beta; the app lets users snap a room photo or share a screenshot, tags furniture and appliances with prices, and links to offers on Shopee and Taobao, offering 3 free scans without an account. Budget Reno Bro asked whether anyone had tried it yet. Budget Reno Bro's checklists center on total landed cost: unit price, shipping to your own postcode, installation, piping/brackets, labour, trade-in, and warranty coverage, and on comparing app versus kedai prices. Budget Reno Bro advised Seremban/Nilai renovators to search Malaysia Reno Kaki for contractor warnings and price checks, to confirm SIRIM and BOMBA certification with a registered gas contractor, and to measure cabinet depth and hood ducting before buying.

nodes.name: Casella merchant phase
nodes.summary: Casella announced a later merchant phase for Malaysian stores, not available during the beta. The phase includes verified listings, local stores matched first, a leads inbox, a dashboard, and one paid Partner slot per list that cannot receive the Best offer badge. Casella's Best offer badge is based on total cost including delivery, installation, and import charges, not just sticker price; Taobao delivery is estimated at 10 to 18 days, and the app earns affiliate commission on Shopee and Taobao links. The public beta gives 3 free scans without an account and tags furniture and appliances with prices from a room photo or screenshot. Wong Kar Fai raised questions about unit price, delivery fee, installation, warranty (original or parallel import), old-appliance trade-in, and whether delivery estimates follow the real postcode.

nodes.name: Google Lens
nodes.summary: Google Lens is used for image search, typically one item at a time, alongside the image search inside Shopee and Taobao. Grace Chin, a product manager who works with computer-vision tools, doubts a startup can beat Google Lens on accuracy, arguing Google's lead rests on billions of labeled images, years of refinement, and infrastructure most startups cannot touch, making it a near-insurmountable lead in general image search. She repeatedly cites a 2019 case in which a "beats Google Lens" claim collapsed once the test set turned out to be biased toward the vendor's own training data. She states a startup can win in a niche with a specialized, well-curated dataset—retail inventory, industrial defect detection, medical imaging, fashion—since narrow beats broad, but should not present a niche win as a general one.

nodes.name: YouTube
nodes.summary: YouTube is the platform on which Malaysian Chinese creator Jason Reno Journal publishes content.

attributes.name: Chua Li Ting's notebook and screenshots

nodes.name: Chua Li Ting's notebook and screenshots
nodes.summary: Chua Li Ting keeps a notebook and screenshots for exactly the purpose of evidence-based discussions: invoices, dates, and chat logs saved before she posts anything about a seller. She holds that unverified accusations hurt innocent small businesses and vague claims help nobody, and her rule is "No documentation, no warning."

nodes.name: Melissa Anak Jimbun
nodes.summary: Melissa Anak Jimbun is a 35-year-old homeowner in Kuching, Sarawak, who compares East Malaysia delivery charges and asks whether Taobao is realistic for bulky items. A quote of RM800 just to ship a 3-seater sofa from Taobao to Kuching, before import tax and installation, anchored her landed-cost comparisons; she chose a local Kuching supplier at RM2,680 delivered and installed over the Taobao route (RM1,450 unit + RM800 shipping, no local warranty service, RM2,250 total), accepting the RM430 difference for a physical shop and a Sarawak-covered warranty after inspecting the sofa at the warehouse in person. She keeps a spreadsheet of landed costs (unit + shipping to Kuching postcode + installation + warranty) and asks sellers in writing for full model codes, itemised totals, honest delivery days by postcode, and who services the warranty locally, with paid partner slots labelled "iklan" before the click.

nodes.name: AR side table viewing
nodes.summary: Priya Nair used guest scan in a furniture app to view a side table in AR before logging in. She declined location access, found the app offered only English and Malay and sent feedback requesting Tamil, and confirmed scan history could be deleted; all checks passed but she did not sign in because she only needed to look, not give data.

nodes.name: Malaysia Reno Kaki
nodes.summary: Malaysia Reno Kaki is a Malaysian renovation community whose weekend check-in for Sabah and Sarawak homeowners and renovators advised checking local East Malaysian suppliers first and comparing total landed cost: unit price plus shipping to the buyer's postcode plus installation plus warranty coverage. It warned that a "2-4 day" delivery from a KL warehouse routinely becomes 1-2 weeks once it crosses the South China Sea, and urged buyers to confirm realistic transit days and courier coverage for KK, Kuching, Sandakan, Sibu, Tawau, Miri and rural postcodes. It advised knowing who services a product locally, since a longer warranty covering only Semenanjung is worthless in East Malaysia, and required contractor warnings to come with documentation such as invoices, dates, photos and messages, with unverified accusations removed.

nodes.name: Malaysia
nodes.summary: Malaysia is the target market for Casella (working name), a planned mobile app that turns a photo or screenshot of a room into furniture, decor and appliance offers. The product is at public beta stage, and its details come from the team's planned user stories describing intended behaviour rather than proven results, with no users, traction or measured match accuracy.

nodes.name: Lau Kok Wai
nodes.summary: Lau Kok Wai is 42 and lives in Kuala Lumpur. He refuses to sign in for most apps, uses 3 guest scans, and then leaves unless saving really matters; his stated pattern is to scan first and decide whether a login is worth it. In testing three KL home shopping apps for a compact fridge, two asked for a phone number before showing the delivery fee, while one showed price and delivery terms on the first guest scan with no login. Before scanning a room he requires three answers: the tag must show total landed cost (unit + delivery + installation + import tax) rather than sticker price; clarity on where room photos go, how long they are kept, and whether deletion is permanent; and guest scan access without an account or phone number. If he cannot verify these without signing up, he takes screenshots, notes the model code, and calls the shop instead.

nodes.name: Sim Kok Leong
nodes.summary: Sim Kok Leong is 53 and lives in Muar, where he spent 30+ years as a repair technician and is now retired. He advises checking the full model code on the sticker before price — lookalikes such as NR-BX418VS versus NR-BX418XSB and 1.0HP versus 1.5HP units look identical in photos — then confirming the spec sheet (capacity, inverter type, warranty covering parts, compressor and labour, local authorised versus parallel import), total landed cost including delivery, standard installation (piping, brackets, vacuum, breaker), tax and old-unit disposal, and a reachable local service centre. He reported a Shopee listing that claimed inverter technology while the model number did not match the spec sheet, and caught a seller passing off a refurbished unit as new because the model plate told the truth.

nodes.name: Snap
nodes.summary: Snap lets a user take a photo, pick up to 5 images from the gallery, or share a screenshot straight from another app in 2 taps. It is part of a flow that turns a room into furniture, decor and appliance offers.

nodes.name: marketplace listing boost
nodes.summary: Marketplace listing boost was one of two channels compared in Rumah Lengkap Marketing's lead-tracker figures for the previous month, using two small traders in the same category (bedroom furniture) with near-equal spend. The marketplace listing boost client (Client B) spent RM450, received 210 leads (nearly all only asking "pm harga"), 58 answered WhatsApp, 9 were qualified, and 2 sales closed, at RM50 cost per qualified lead. Rumah Lengkap Marketing's conclusion was that the marketplace wins on lead volume while the group wins on leads that actually become sales, with both depending on listing hygiene.

nodes.name: photo-to-SKU product
nodes.summary: Grace Chin's four-question rubric for evaluating any photo-to-SKU product asks, in order: (1) what the metric is, distinguishing top-1 category accuracy (e.g. "aircond") from retrieval precision@1 on the exact model code (1.0HP vs 1.5HP; NR-BX418VS vs a lookalike), since vendors quote the first and let you hear the second; (2) how the labelled test set was built, including who labelled it, how many classes, and whether near-identical units were included; (3) the false-match rate, because in retail a confident wrong match costs more than no match; and (4) per-class, per-region breakdown, publishing precision/recall by class and by region, with Kuching and Kangar needing their own rows. A "92% match" without a confidence score and a test set is decoration, not validation. In 2019 a "beats Google Lens" claim collapsed once the test set turned out to be weighted toward the vendor's own training data.

nodes.name: small-space content creation
nodes.summary: Rina Kecil Living works as a small-space content creator and said the pieces she loves most are handmade ones, such as a rattan stool her mother bought in Melaka and a hand-tied knot no mould could copy. She stated that no algorithm captures character and that what helps her find workshops is real photos of hands working, stories about the material, maker and kampung, tags like #handmadeMY #rattanfurniture #lokalkraf with specific words such as weave pattern, cane type and dimensions, and creators who name and credit the workshop. In 2021 a home design app used her before/after photos without credit or permission and she only found out when a follower tagged her, which she described as feeling violated and undervalued; she now always links and tags the maker.

nodes.name: video upload
nodes.summary: The video upload is a later-stage feature that users browsing for inspiration would return for, alongside the Explore feed.

nodes.name: photo-to-offer portal
nodes.summary: The photo-to-offer portal opened its beta in the week of 2026-11-04. Rumah Lengkap Marketing declined to recommend it at that stage, not because the product is poor but because no channel can fit small merchants' budgets until it shows a measurable cost per qualified lead. Rumah Lengkap Marketing's test rules for any portal: a 30-day limited trial with three volunteer clients (one in the Klang Valley, one in Penang, one in Kuching), measured on cost per qualified lead against each client's existing Facebook and marketplace baseline, with no exclusivity and no upfront payment, plus a full deletion test before any customer photos are collected. For paid Partner slots, the deciding metric is cost per lead and whether the lead is qualified (a real WhatsApp enquiry or showroom visit, not just a click), and ad labels must be clear.

nodes.name: small-space living
nodes.summary: Small-space living is the theme of a post by Amirah Zulkifli about Unit 12-3, noting that the cheapest item is not the cheapest item but the one that arrives on the promised day with installation included and without needing re-measurement. Amirah Zulkifli's still-hunting list covers a bed, wardrobe, compact sofa, and study desk, all rental-friendly, small-space, and honestly priced. Hannah Lau responded that the same hunt applies to her, that she keeps saving inspiration and never checks out, and used #smallspaceliving.

nodes.name: KK
nodes.summary: KK is listed among the East Malaysian destinations for which Budget Reno Bro's weekend check-in post advises checking realistic transit days and courier coverage, alongside Kuching, Sandakan, Sibu, Tawau, Miri, and rural postcodes. Jason Reno Journal cited a buyer in KK as an example of why a 5-year warranty paper covering only Semenanjung is zero value. Malaysia Reno Kaki's admin pin repeated the warning that "2-4 hari" from a KL warehouse routinely becomes 1-2 weeks once it crosses the South China Sea, and urged checking realistic transit days for KK and the other listed areas. Nadia Home Diary named kedai in KK, alongside Kuching, Perlis, and Kelantan, as deserving a fair comparison under "check local first." Sabah Sarawak Home Group noted that a RM40 Peninsular shipping rate can become RM180+ to KK/Sibu and that KK and Kuching suppliers often match or beat the landed price.

nodes.name: Tilam Selesa Bedding showroom
nodes.summary: Tilam Selesa Bedding operates a showroom in Kuantan that customers are invited to visit to try lying on mattresses before deciding. In a nighttime post addressed to Kuantan, the company said a comfortable mattress is not a luxury but a necessity for sound sleep, and that it is ready to help customers choose the best option for their needs and budget; it encouraged visitors to try the mattresses first, since comfort is for the customer to judge. A follow-up afternoon post stated that the showroom is open as usual for those looking for mattresses, bed frames, or bedding accessories, reiterating the belief that the best mattress is one the customer tries personally — lying down and feeling it before deciding — with no pressure, just friendly service and comfortable prices.

nodes.name: Rimbun Rattan Crafts' chairs
nodes.summary: Rimbun Rattan Crafts, a rattan workshop in Melaka, states that no two of its chairs are ever identical, so a "lookalike" in a photo is never the same piece in a customer's hands. The workshop tells customers to compare total cost rather than advertised price: unit price + delivery to the customer's postcode (Sabah and Sarawak carry different rates, and the workshop has shipped there) + hand-weaving labour + warranty and who does repairs.

nodes.name: Sharifah Nadia
nodes.summary: Sharifah Nadia advises choosing safe materials and ensuring a clear return policy. Her guidance was cited in a post about testing affiliate links honestly and transparently, recommending only products the poster personally uses.

nodes.name: Melissa Anak Jimbun's 3-seater sofa
nodes.summary: Melissa Anak Jimbun considered buying a 3-seater sofa from Taobao shipped to Kuching: unit cost RM1,450 plus RM800 shipping with no local warranty service, totaling RM2,250. A local Kuching supplier offered a sofa at RM2,680 delivered and installed, with a shop she could walk into if anything went wrong — a difference of RM430. She drove to the warehouse to inspect the sofa in person before deciding, and her verdict is to buy local for bulky items, treating the shipping quote as a hidden tax not shown in West Malaysia; Taobao remains fine for small items such as beadwork and kitchen tools. On 4 November 2026 she posted the final decision breakdown and credited Melvin Pang and others in Taobao Kaki Malaysia who replied to her question about whether RM800 to ship a 3-seater to Kuching was normal.

nodes.name: 3-seater sofa from Taobao
nodes.summary: Melissa Anak Jimbun was quoted RM800 for a 3-seater sofa from Taobao shipped to Kuching, before import tax and assembly.

nodes.name: Unit 12-3 Wishlist
nodes.summary: Unit 12-3 Wishlist is Amirah Zulkifli's rule for purchases: measure twice, cry once. It requires checking the total landed cost (unit plus delivery, installation and warranty), asking whether installation is included, and waiting three weeks before buying a RM299 shelf anyway. Amirah is not buying everything, just learning. Amirah is 27 and setting up a small studio unit in Cyberjaya, keeping the wishlist as a Notes list alongside a mental RM-per-square-foot calculator; she tests apps with a photo of her teh tarik before uploading any real photo of her empty unit because house photos are not free data. She treats a badge without a confidence score as "not sure" and favors apps that say "no match."

nodes.name: small-space shopping
nodes.summary: Rina Kecil Living applies a total-landed-cost rule to small-space shopping in a 600 sq ft rental: compare unit price plus delivery, installation, warranty, and whether the item actually fits, rather than sticker prices. A RM99 shelf that arrives dented with no local service is not a bargain by this standard. Rina Kecil Living states that comparing quotes is fine, but quoting someone's original content should always come with credit to the creator, just as one credits the supplier.

nodes.name: Chua Li Ting
nodes.summary: Chua Li Ting, 34, lives in Kajang and is a mother of two small children. Her rule is "delete first, then decide" (先删，再决定): she tests an app's delete button with a plant photo before scanning real rooms, after once uploading a photo of her children's room to a "scan and suggest" app that showed bunk beds, school bags, a window and part of the hallway, then deleting it within seconds. Before trusting any scan app she asks how long room photos and scan history are kept, whether deletion is permanent or only hidden from her view, whether photos are used for AI training, and whether she can use it as a guest without signing in with her real name; if the retention period is unclear she will not scan a room, and she tests the delete button with a small table or dummy photo before scanning real items.

nodes.name: Lim Wei Jie
nodes.summary: Lim Wei Jie is a 39-year-old engineer renovating a terrace house in Seremban 2, comparing offers for a new stove and built-in oven. A previous contractor built a cabinet without checking his appliance dimensions and the appliance did not fit, which grounded his fixed written criteria: full dimensions (W x D x H in mm) plus cut-out and clearance dimensions; model code; gas type confirmed (LPG vs natural gas) with hose/regulator standard, certified installer and proper leak test; installation included by a qualified or registered gas fitter; warranty length and coverage (parts vs labour, local authorised vs parallel import); itemised total landed cost including delivery by postcode, piping/brackets/labour and import tax; after-sales coverage in Seremban/Nilai; and photos showing a tape measure, A4 paper or floor tile for scale. He states he bought the house for his family and will not cut corners on gas appliances, and that value, quality and after-sales support come before price.

nodes.name: Indian-Malaysian home pages
nodes.summary: Indian-Malaysian home pages are followed by Sarah Thevi, 29, of Klang, who asks whether the app recognises the items and styles she likes from them.

nodes.name: Malaysia Reno Kaki
nodes.summary: Malaysia Reno Kaki is a large Facebook renovation group where members share contractor warnings, price checks and shopping finds. Admins issue PSAs urging members to compute total landed cost (unit + delivery + installation + warranty, original vs parallel import, plus trade-in), verify delivery lead times against their own postcodes (Georgetown 10200, Penang mainland, Sabah, Sarawak), screenshot promised dates and keep chat logs, and report genuine experiences both good and bad. Disputes go through moderator mediation and fact-checking; no politics, race, religion or unverified personal attacks, and contractor blacklists require invoices, dates, photos and messages. The group keeps a trusted contractor list updated monthly from member feedback and holds monthly live Q&A with industry experts, 8-11 PM, all weekend.

attributes.name: drawing a box around one item

nodes.name: drawing a box around one item
nodes.summary: Drawing a box around one item is planned for the next phase and is not available at beta.

nodes.name: stainless thali set
nodes.summary: Sarah Thevi, a user in Klang, tested an app using screenshots that included a stainless thali set, a teak mandir cabinet, a batik cushion, and a kolam-patterned rug; the app returned generic labels such as "wooden cabinet" and "bohemian rug" and missed every cultural cue. She asks whether an app recognises Indian-Malaysian items and styles or only Western decor, and whether it can explain its recognition logic.

nodes.name: scan-and-link app
nodes.summary: Casella is a scan-and-link app that tags items by appearance and carries "Best offer" badges. Sabah Sarawak Home Group's admin said such a tool is fine for discovery but is not a landed-cost calculator for East Malaysia, and that tags should be treated as a starting point until Casella can show postcode-based delivery days to Sabah, Sarawak, Kelantan, and Perlis. The group stated no measured match accuracy has been published, so nobody should quote a "92% match" as fact, and raised top-1 versus retrieval precision and false-match rate as accuracy concerns. Tiffany Yeoh called an app that matches by photo basically a lookalike generator, and Halim Yaakob asked the app to publish its false-match rate and show total installed price before a buy click.

nodes.name: computer-vision tools in retail
nodes.summary: Grace Chin has been building a rubric for evaluating computer-vision tools in retail, with Casella as a clean test case. The pattern across discussions on Reddit, LinkedIn, and Slack groups is that the commercial layer (landed cost, iklan labels, retention, affiliate disclosure) is scrutinised thoroughly while the technical layer stays dark, even though the commercial layer only works if the item on the screen is the right item. Her four questions for any photo-to-SKU product cover the metric (top-1 category accuracy versus retrieval precision@1 on exact model code), how the labelled test set was built, the false-match rate, and per-class, per-region breakdown. Aggregate accuracy hides the long tail: a teak mandir labelled "wooden cabinet" and a kolam rug labelled "bohemian rug" (tested by a Klang commenter) are coverage gaps, not cultural niceties.

nodes.name: Kuantan showroom
nodes.summary: Tilam Selesa Bedding's Kuantan showroom drew many visitors during a week in which people stopped by to ask about mattresses and bedding, the company thanking Kuantan and noting it loves sharing tips and hearing customers' stories. The showroom is open every day, and visitors can try lying on mattresses and have coffee. Tilam Selesa Bedding is a small family mattress shop operating since 2010; its staff add that mattresses, sofas and other large items cannot be judged from photos or scans, since firmness, foam density and spring quality only become clear by lying down and trying them. The shop installs and sets up what it sells and advises comparing total cost through delivery and installation rather than sticker price, and states it will promote sellers whose prices are honest.

nodes.name: Vanessa Goh
nodes.summary: Vanessa Goh is an independent interior designer in Kuala Lumpur who works in a warm-minimalism style (#KLinterior, #warmminimalism, #rumahku). Her stated rule is "Let me touch it first": a photo cannot reveal foam density, joinery, fabric weave, stitching, proportions or how a cushion sits after six months in Malaysian humidity, and she will not recommend an appliance she has not seen switched on. She tells clients to compare total landed cost — unit + delivery + installation + import tax — rather than sticker price, to check the full model code on both stickers, to demand a trained installer and a proper leak test, and calls cheap installation with a voided warranty the most expensive deal. For risky items (aircond, water heater, gas hob) she insists on seeing the physical sticker, plug type and warranty card, and puts a safety checklist in every handover pack for clients including Haslinda Omar and Balakrishnan Nair.

nodes.name: Melissa Anak Jimbun's sofa decision
nodes.summary: Melissa Anak Jimbun, a Kuching homeowner, closed her sofa decision after doing total landed cost math, with a local Kuching quote of RM2,680 covering delivery, installation, and walk-in service. She asked Vista Sofa Factory Outlet, a Muar sofa maker, for the realistic shipping and delivery cost to a Kuching terrace house postcode rather than the Peninsular rate, and who services the warranty in Sarawak, since a frame warranty claimable only in Semenanjung is worth zero to her. She said she would test duduk a Muar sofa if the landed number to her door beats RM2,680, and asked whether fabric samples could be sent first.

nodes.name: East Malaysia thread
nodes.summary: Sim Kok Leong endorsed the East Malaysia thread as good advice and added a line for appliances: for gas stoves and regulators, never buy from a seller with no physical address, since a faulty regulator caused a leak in a client's home years ago. The added guidance is to ask for the model number, check it against the manufacturer's spec sheet, confirm a certified installer, and weigh total landed cost plus who services it locally.

nodes.name: Merchants
nodes.summary: Merchants get a dashboard of impressions, clicks, leads, and missed demand, and an inbox of billable WhatsApp, quote, and showroom leads. Verified Malaysian stores can list products by form, CSV, or Shopee shop import.

nodes.name: Klang kitchen renovation
nodes.summary: Rajesh Pillai is renovating a kitchen in Klang, with a hob, hood and built-in oven on his list. His non-negotiables are full dimensions and cut-out dimensions in mm (sellers who don't provide them are a red flag), installation included with proper gas fitting by a certified worker (after a friend's bad stove experience, he avoids unknown sellers for gas appliances), warranty terms covering how many years, what is covered, parts or labour, and who services it (Semajun or not), a physical shop plus recent buyer photos (twelve reviews and no history means he skips; earlier he cited five reviews), and declaration of all hidden charges for delivery, hacking and disposal. He cites having once been hit by a RM600 hidden delivery charge. He also accepts Seremban/Nilai offers provided the same information is given, and compares specs, dimensions and after-sales service before buying, asking sellers to show dimensions and warranty before talking.

nodes.name: home renovation
nodes.summary: Home renovation guidance in the Malaysia Reno Kaki KAKI CORNER weekly tips: get at least 3 quotes before booking any contractor and compare scope, not just price ("Murah belum tentu selamat"); check price for big-ticket items (aircon, kitchen cabinet, tiles) and ask for total landed cost including delivery, installation, and warranty; keep a WhatsApp trail of quotations, payment receipts, and promised dates as protection in disputes; insist on certified workers for electrical and plumbing; and share genuine good and bad experiences, with disputes handled through moderator mediation and fact-checking. A trusted contractor list is updated monthly from feedback, and a live Q&A with industry experts is held every month.

nodes.name: third-party installer
nodes.summary: A third-party installer usually voids the aircond warranty, so the dealer should be confirmed first. Kevin Lim and Amirah Zulkifli both advised confirming with the dealer whether warranty stays valid with a third-party installer, and Wong Kar Fai asked that it be confirmed in writing whether labour warranty dies with a third-party installer. Kevin Lim repeated on 2026-11-04 that using a third-party installer usually voids the warranty. Faizal Rahim, replacing a 9-year-old 1.5HP unit in Shah Alam, asked whether using his own third-party installer keeps the warranty valid or voids it, citing a past cheap install with a gas leak that voided the warranty. On 2026-11-04, Halim Yaakob, an aircond installer in Johor Bahru, stated that using a third-party installer voids many warranties when a gas leak occurs. Azlan Musa called the third-party point important, noting cheap-first installs lead to gas leaks and voided warranties.

nodes.name: Amirah Zulkifli's RM299 shelf
nodes.summary: Amirah Zulkifli is a 27-year-old setting up a small studio unit in Cyberjaya, with a wishlist for Unit 12-3. She has been comparing a RM299 shelf for three weeks before buying; she describes herself as careful with money on a budget that is not formal. She has not uploaded a single real photo of her empty unit, testing apps with a picture of her teh tarik first and then checking that the delete button actually deletes, holding that home photos are not free data. She treats a badge without a confidence score as "not sure," since a confident wrong match means ordering the wrong plug type and paying for a return. She is beta-testing a room-scanning app; scanning her parents' living room, the app gave a clean number but missed local equivalents and installation cost.

nodes.name: Georgetown
nodes.summary: Georgetown is the home location of Wong Kar Fai, 48, a careful price checker.

nodes.name: Aisyah Rahman's coffee table
nodes.summary: Aisyah Rahman's coffee table is budgeted at RM350 in her 'Rumah Impian' plan. Nothing has been purchased yet; she is waiting for the house keys.

nodes.name: Penang mainland
nodes.summary: Penang mainland is one of the delivery zones Syafiq Hamdan of Sungai Petani, Kedah distinguishes by postcode: "2-4 hari" to Penang mainland differs from the estimate to Kedah. On 4 November 2026, Hafiz Ismail included Penang mainland among the zones whose lead times differ, alongside Georgetown 10200, Sabah and Sarawak, warning that "2-4 hari" can become 12 days. Rumah Bajet MY and Malaysia Reno Kaki posts on the same date listed KK, Kuching, Sandakan, Sibu, Tawau, Miri and rural East Malaysia as postcodes needing their own shipping rates rather than a "Semenanjung" rate.

nodes.name: new home-furnishing portal
nodes.summary: Rumah Lengkap Marketing addressed the new home-furnishing portal in its "Ringgit dan Reach" weekly note, answering the same question four times in one week: whether the portal should enter a client's budget. Its answer remained no, because the portal has zero users, zero traction and zero measured matching accuracy, so it cannot show cost per qualified lead; a channel that cannot show numbers is a candidate for a neutral test, not a budget line for small traders. The draft test is 30 days with three volunteer clients (one Klang Valley, one Penang, one Kuching), measured on cost per qualified lead against their Facebook and marketplace baselines, with no exclusivity, no upfront payment, and a full deletion test before any customer photos are collected; if it fails, the numbers will be published and clients told to spend elsewhere. Until the test runs, the page stays openly neutral about the portal and every question about it is answered with the same line: what is the cost per lead?

nodes.name: Rumah Lengkap Marketing
nodes.summary: Rumah Lengkap Marketing is a small agency that audits listings for home retailers and manages their advertising, auditing clients' listings before any ad budget is spent. Its "listing hygiene" checklist fixes nine items before any money is spent on ads or boost: display price vs real price including delivery and installation; size in both cm and inches; exact material (MDF, solid rubberwood, veneer); delivery time by postcode; actual stock; three photos (full shot, material close-up, in-room shot); FAQs answered in the listing rather than DMs; a single CTA (WhatsApp or form); and a lead-source tracker. It does not treat reach or total lead count as a KPI, measuring instead cost per qualified lead and cost per closed sale.

nodes.name: data privacy column
nodes.summary: Chua Li Ting adds a data privacy column to her purchase-comparison notebook before buying anything, alongside the specification table columns for model number, dimensions, cut-out dimensions, power rating or gas type, warranty, installation, and after-sales service location. The column records what information a seller collects (name, address, warranty form, even photos), how long they keep it, and whether it can be deleted after upload. For anything that asks her to upload a photo of her home, that column decides the purchase: if there is no stated retention period and no obvious delete button, she does not upload, and she tests the delete button with a plant photo first before deciding. She frames the standard as fit, safety, warranty, and privacy, with price alone telling you nothing.

nodes.name: Rimbun
nodes.summary: Rimbun is a rattan furniture workshop whose work drew extensive response in a Reddit thread on 4 November 2026. Hafiz Ismail asked for honest tags covering rattan type, dimensions in cm (width x depth x height), whether cushions are thick or the seat height, self-collect versus delivery to Klang Valley, and whether customers can view and sit on pieces before buying, closing with well wishes for Rimbun. Chua Li Ting asked whether she could see and sit on pieces before buying, citing honest tags, dimensions in cm, seat height and self-collect or delivery to Kajang/Selangor. Rina Kecil Living said what helps her find workshops like Rimbun is real photos of hands working rather than only finished products, stories about the material, maker and kampung, tags such as #handmadeMY #rattanfurniture #lokalkraf and specific words like weave pattern, cane type and dimensions, and creators who name and credit the workshop.

nodes.name: KL
nodes.summary: KL is the location where Hafiz Ismail checks that a sofa's warranty is serviced locally, and he notes that a "2-4 hari" delivery from a KL warehouse is not the same to destinations like KK or Sibu. Wong Kar Fai's Penang-focused guidance contrasts Georgetown 10200 delivery with mainland postcodes, and Budget Reno Bro's East Malaysia check-in warns that a "2-4 day" delivery from a KL warehouse routinely becomes 1-2 weeks once it crosses the South China Sea. Aisyah Rahman, based in Shah Alam rather than East Malaysia, applies the same total landed cost principle.

attributes.name: Justin Ling
attributes.primary_concern: false-match rate and on-device performance at the Sarawak edge case

nodes.name: Justin Ling
nodes.summary: Justin Ling is a 22-year-old computer science student in Sibu, Sarawak who judges apps in 10 seconds and gives each one single attempt, uninstalling on splash-screen lag, ads before the home screen, forced sign-ups, or unnecessary permission grabs; minimal, fast and honest apps get championed for free. His checklist requires a delete button that actually removes data (tested with a plant photo before a real home upload), paid or affiliate labels before the click, and published per-class accuracy and false-match rates before "92% match" claims count as anything but a demo. He prices the same job both ways and asks for total landed cost by his own postcode — item, delivery, installation, tax — citing RM80–150 shipping plus import tax across the South China Sea to Sarawak versus RM28 in the Klang Valley, and noting "installation included" rarely covers East Malaysia.

nodes.name: DIY installation
nodes.summary: Rajesh Pillai holds that DIY installation is fine for a shelf and bracket, but gas hobs, water heaters and air conditioners require a trained installer and a proper leak test, citing a friend's bad stove experience; for electrical and gas work he does not DIY because the warranty can be voided. Kedai Perabot Seri Jaya, a family-owned furniture shop in Klang operating since 1985, delivers and installs itself within the Klang Valley rather than letting customers arrange their own lorry, on the view that a sofa or wardrobe arriving unassembled with nobody to fit it is not a saving. The shop's furniture checklist covers actual dimensions in cm (L x D x H), seat height and material; total sampai pasang (unit + delivery + installation + old-furniture disposal); and written warranty on frame, joints and who does the repair, with black-and-white measurement confirmation before cutting custom-made cabinets.

nodes.name: showrooms
nodes.summary: Showrooms are among the places already used to identify where an item is from.

nodes.name: sofa shortlisting
nodes.summary: Hafiz Ismail's slow reno note #7 covers the sofa shortlist rather than a sofa purchase: he visited three stores after work in one week and sat on eleven sofas, still shortlisting because a saved room is inspiration, not a purchase trigger. In person he checks seat height (whether feet sit flat), seat depth (55cm vs 65cm for a 950 sq ft living room), cushion density (pressing to see if it sinks fast), removable covers and fabric code for washing and future re-cover, frame of kiln-dried wood rather than chipboard (testing the arm and listening for sound), warranty duration and who services it locally in KL, and door and lift clearance measured before delivery day. He rejected one online-only model that week because its photo looked premium but the cushion sank in the showroom in seconds, and he does not do photo-only buys.

nodes.name: lead verification
nodes.summary: Sinar Home Marketplace requires lead verification up front, needing to know a lead is a genuine buyer rather than a bot or a curious scroller, because unverified leads inflate every number downstream. Sinar compares portal leads against its current Shopee advertising return and holds that cost per qualified lead is the only metric that survives scrutiny, since clicks and "92% match" badges do not pay the bills while a real WhatsApp enquiry and a real showroom visit do. Farah Zainal of Kota Kinabalu likewise asks that cost per qualified lead be shown before any small shop commits ringgit, under the principle "No proof, no ringgit."

nodes.name: Budget Reno Bro
nodes.summary: Budget Reno Bro is a Twitter account whose post "WEEKEND CHECK-IN — East Malaysia represent!" was quoted by Malaysia Reno Kaki in round 69 on 2026-11-04. The post, addressed to homeowners and renovators of Sabah and Sarawak, urged checking local suppliers first and comparing total landed cost (unit price + shipping to postcode + installation + warranty coverage), warned that "2-4 day" KL warehouse deliveries routinely become 1-2 weeks crossing the South China Sea, and asked for realistic transit days and courier coverage for KK, Kuching, Sandakan, Sibu, Tawau, Miri and rural postcodes. It also advised confirming a locally reachable authorised service centre over a longer warranty covering only Semenanjung, required documentation (invoices, dates, photos, messages) for contractor warnings with unverified accusations removed, and encouraged before-and-after photos, supplier recommendations and group-buy interest to cut shipping costs.

nodes.name: Borneo Home Tales
nodes.summary: Borneo Home Tales is named among East Malaysian creators and voices that Malaysia Reno Kaki states will receive the same airtime and the same PIN as West Malaysian coverage, alongside local suppliers and KK/Kuching/Sibu/Miri/Tawau members. Malaysia Reno Kaki cited this position as continuing from the Casella beta, with the stated aim of no more West Malaysia-centric coverage.

nodes.name: BOMBA
nodes.summary: BOMBA certification is required for gas appliances before purchase, per Budget Reno Bro's advice to a Seremban/Nilai renovator. Budget Reno Bro advised confirming SIRIM and BOMBA certification and ensuring the installer is a registered gas contractor rather than any wireman, and to walk away from sellers who cannot provide the certificate.

nodes.name: Lookalike or Not?
nodes.summary: Lookalike or Not? is Tiffany Yeoh's comparison series for judging whether a piece captures a style rather than merely resembling it in photos. She calls for close-up fabric weave shots with a measuring tape alongside rather than relying on "gaya nampak sama" (similar-looking style), and holds that photo match is not style match: Casella tags by appearance, but appearance cannot show proportions, fabric quality, or craftsmanship; she cited a sofa with a "92% match" that arrived with the wrong silhouette and cheap fabric. She runs it as screenshot vs actual unit, asking whether a piece captures the style, and adds that a photo-matching app is basically a lookalike generator whose "Best offer" badge cannot show whether a piece captures the style, so model code, silhouette, joinery, and fabric must be checked side-by-side.

nodes.name: 1.5HP air conditioner
nodes.summary: Faizal Rahim in Shah Alam is replacing a 9-year-old 1.5HP air conditioner in the main bedroom; the existing unit is noisy, weak and expensive on electricity. He requires the full indoor and outdoor model code from the sticker, with photos of both units side by side, and a single written quote covering unit, delivery by postcode, piping, brackets, vacuum, breaker and labour, plus confirmation that third-party installation keeps the warranty valid — he previously had a cheap install leak gas and void the warranty. He also requires warranty terms in black and white covering parts, compressor and labour, local authorised versus parallel import, capacity sized to room area, and checks on electrical load and earthing for the old house; as of 4 November 2026 he had received two quotes, was waiting for two more, and planned to decide within a week and share landed totals.

nodes.name: group-buy
nodes.summary: Group-buy interest is encouraged among East Malaysian homeowners and renovators so that shipping costs can be cut together. Members are asked to post group-buy interest alongside before-and-after photos and supplier recommendations, and the push for group-buys is tied to cutting shipping costs collectively. In November 2026 posts, Sabah and Sarawak homeowners and renovators in areas including KK, Kuching, Sandakan, Sibu, Tawau, Miri and rural postcodes were urged to ask for realistic transit days and courier coverage, confirm who services warranties locally, and compare total landed cost: unit price + shipping to their postcode + installation + warranty coverage. Malaysia Reno Kaki, describing itself as a group built in 2015 around contractor warnings, price checks and shopping finds, invited members to group-buy with neighbours to cut freight by dropping "GB" plus their area.

attributes.focus_area: Home renovation tips and contractor recommendations
attributes.name: KAKI CORNER

nodes.name: KAKI CORNER
nodes.summary: KAKI CORNER is a Twitter community focused on home renovation tips and contractor recommendations, publishing a "Weekly Reno Tips" post advising members to get at least 3 contractor quotes and compare scope rather than just price, check total landed cost for big-ticket items (aircon, kitchen cabinet, tiles) including delivery, installation and warranty, keep a WhatsApp trail of quotations, payment receipts and promised dates as protection in disputes, and insist on certified workers for electrical and plumbing. KAKI CORNER states it stays neutral in disputes with everything going through moderator mediation and fact-checking, maintains a trusted contractor list updated monthly from member feedback, and holds a live Q&A with industry experts every month. The post carried the hashtags #MalaysiaRenoKaki, #RenoTips and #CheckPrice.

nodes.name: rental-friendly fixes
nodes.summary: Amirah Zulkifli sought rental-friendly fixes for Unit 12-3 that did not cost RM4k, asking for direct messages with real reviews only and no "just get this" suggestions without prices. The request came in a November 4, 2026 post noting that the bed, wardrobe, compact sofa, and study desk had not yet been bought.

nodes.name: benchmark verification
nodes.summary: Grace Chin holds that "show me the benchmark" is a universal principle, not just a CV thing: a photo tag is not a quote, a demo is not a benchmark, and a pilot is not a product-market fit claim, and in every case the questions are what exactly is being measured, against what baseline and on whose data, and whether it can be reproduced independently. Sellers who publish real dates do not fear scrutiny, startups with real accuracy do not dodge the test set, and those who resist verification are telling you something; precision over hype applies in appliances and in AI. Verified listings, postcode-accurate delivery, and written warranty terms are reproducibility for shopping, and if a seller's claim cannot survive checking against reality it was never a claim, only marketing, which applies to delivery estimates and model accuracy alike. Grace Chin's worldview is to keep the screenshot and keep the test set.

nodes.name: almari
nodes.summary: Melissa Anak Jimbun was once caught out buying an almari online: the price looked cheap, but West Malaysia rates were far better and Sarawak buyers paid more. She asks out-of-state sellers for three things in writing: the full model code for indoor and outdoor units; the total landed cost to her postcode including delivery to Kuching, import tax, installation, and breaker/damage; and honest delivery days by postcode rather than "nationwide".

nodes.name: nationwide delivery
nodes.summary: The Sabah Sarawak Home Group admin team states that for Sabah and Sarawak, "nationwide delivery" is not enough and that real delivery days by postcode should be shown. The group also advises confirming that delivery and installation actually cover Sabah and Sarawak before committing, and comparing app price versus shop price in the same table including unit, shipping to Sabah/Sarawak, import tax, installation, and after-sales/warranty.

nodes.name: Klang Valley
nodes.summary: Hafiz Ismail is a Klang Valley homeowner furnishing a 950 sq ft condo. A local Klang Valley store quoted a 3-seater sofa at RM1,890 for the unit plus RM80 two-storey delivery within the valley, with assembly included and no lift booking fee, totaling RM1,970; the store allows customers to sit on the sofa, measure seat height (45cm) and seat depth (58cm), and view fabric swatches. Justin Ling noted that the RM28 shipping figure is a Klang Valley number, and that across the South China Sea to Sarawak the same TV console jumps to RM80–150 plus import tax.

nodes.name: Amirah Zulkifli's teh tarik photo
nodes.summary: Amirah Zulkifli uses a photo of her teh tarik as a test image before uploading any real photo of her empty studio unit in Cyberjaya, and she checks whether the delete button actually deletes.

nodes.name: photo-to-SKU index
nodes.summary: Rina Kecil Living raised the concern that room photos, reels and screenshots may be quietly feeding a photo-to-SKU index, making any benchmark built on that data rest on uncredited, uncompensated creator labour. She proposed a provenance question: what share of the training/labelled data is creator or user content with explicit consent, credit and compensation attached, published alongside precision and recall.

nodes.name: Kangar 01000
nodes.summary: Kangar 01000 is cited by Rosli Ahmad as an example of a postcode where delivery estimates fail: if stock is in KL, Georgetown 10200 is not 2-4 days, let alone Kangar 01000. Rosli stated Kangar is not overseas and sellers should give real dates rather than wishful ones.

nodes.name: J&T Express
nodes.summary: J&T Express is a courier whose name is used in fake delivery-notice scams sent by WhatsApp and SMS. Thinesh Kumar identified jtexpress.com.my as the official domain, warning that scam links use lookalike or shortened domains instead. Real couriers such as J&T Express never ask for OTP or card details through a link to release a parcel.

nodes.name: Dr. Salina Rahmat
nodes.summary: Dr. Salina Rahmat is a marketing lecturer in Kuala Lumpur who studies how people respond to commission disclosure. Her Klang Valley survey covered 120 consumers; first-time buyer Aisyah Rahman told her that a furniture "haul" she trusted had a commission buried in the comments, saying "Kalau saya tahu, saya fikir dulu." Dr. Rahmat's stated position is that "Disclosure is not a disclaimer; it is a relationship": commission is legitimate but hidden commission is not, and a plain label must sit before the click rather than buried in a hashtag or bio. She argues this is anti-ambiguity rather than anti-creator, urges Malaysian brands to test better disclosure before claiming it kills conversion, and holds that disclosure coming first often makes the same recommendation land better. In a consumer behaviour class case note she contrasted the disclosure-fail example with a Muar sofa maker publishing frame wood, foam density, stitching and after-sales checks.

nodes.name: East Malaysian suppliers
nodes.summary: East Malaysian suppliers are local suppliers in Sabah and Sarawak. Homeowners and renovators are advised to get a quote from a local East Malaysian supplier before committing to any big-ticket item, comparing total landed cost: unit price plus shipping to the buyer's postcode, installation, and warranty coverage. Support for local East Malaysian suppliers is framed around their knowledge of local roads, ports, and prices, and buyers are encouraged to share supplier recommendations. Discussion covers delivery to KK, Kuching, Sandakan, Sibu, Tawau, Miri, and rural postcodes, where a KL warehouse's "2-4 day" delivery routinely becomes 1-2 weeks crossing the South China Sea, and shipping that is RM40 to Peninsular addresses can reach RM180 to KK; most outstation sellers do not cover installation, and a warranty covering only Semenanjung offers no local service.

nodes.name: R410A refrigerant
nodes.summary: R410A is an air-conditioning refrigerant gas. Halim Yaakob, an aircond installer in Johor Bahru, cited it alongside R32 as an example of how visually identical 1.5HP units can differ: units that look the same may use different gas (R32 vs R410A), have different capacity, or be another region's model, so a low price can reflect the wrong model rather than a bargain.

nodes.name: Malaysian stores
nodes.summary: Verified Malaysian stores can list products by form, CSV, or Shopee shop import. Local stores that deliver to the user are matched first and shown in a Local stores tab. Users can request a quote from up to 5 stores when there is no exact match.

nodes.name: offers comparison
nodes.summary: Offers comparison shows each item's offers from Shopee and Taobao, with a match badge and a total price in RM. Users can sort, filter, change colour, material or size chips, and compare 2 or 3 offers side by side.

nodes.name: Jason Reno Journal's review channel
nodes.summary: Jason Reno Journal runs a review channel and discloses every affiliate link in his videos. He endorsed all five points of a checklist, calling points 2 and 4 his red lines, and added two requirements: a measurable benchmark rather than a badge — clear metrics (top-1 category versus precision@1 on full model code), how the labelled test set was built, and the false-match rate between near-identical units (1.0HP vs 1.5HP; same sofa, different fabric code) — since a "92% match" without a confidence score is decoration; and disclosure before the click rather than in a hashtag. He declined a RM10,000 affiliate deal for an untested product.

nodes.name: home decor content creation
nodes.summary: Nadia Home Diary works as a home decor content creator who advises followers not to buy on price alone. For kitchen purchases she emphasizes that gas appliances are a safety matter rather than a cheapness matter, and that buyers should request dimensions and cut-out measurements, confirm installation is included and performed by certified personnel, and ask who services the area (Seremban/Nilai). She frames a price without specifications as a question rather than a deal, and uses the hashtags #CheckPrice and #JomKitaDeco with the sign-off "Jom kita deco dengan amanah."

nodes.name: moderator mediation and fact-checking
nodes.summary: Malaysia Reno Kaki handles disputes through moderator mediation and fact-checking, staying neutral in disputes, per the admin announcement.

nodes.name: Hannah Lau
nodes.summary: Hannah Lau tried Casella for fun and called it her new favourite way to window shop. She scanned her whole rented room, tagged everything, then closed the app without buying a single thing. She finds the 3 free scans dangerous for her "virtual dream home" folder and asked whether anyone else scans and saves but never checks out.

nodes.name: Budget Reno Bro
nodes.summary: Budget Reno Bro authored a weekend check-in post for East Malaysian homeowners and renovators in Sabah and Sarawak, issued under an admin team's voice. The post advises checking local suppliers first and comparing total landed cost (unit price + shipping to the buyer's postcode + installation + warranty coverage), warns that a "2-4 day" delivery from a KL warehouse routinely becomes 1-2 weeks once it crosses the South China Sea, and urges buyers to ask for realistic transit days and courier coverage for KK, Kuching, Sandakan, Sibu, Tawau, Miri, and rural postcodes. It also advises knowing who services a warranty locally, since an authorised service centre within reach beats a longer warranty paper covering only Semenanjung. The post requires contractor warnings to come with documentation (invoices, dates, photos, messages), states unverified accusations get removed, and calls for evidence-based discussion only.

nodes.name: East Malaysian shipping
nodes.summary: Delivery to Sabah is Farah Zainal's main cost, so she checks whether total prices reflect East Malaysian shipping.

nodes.name: Budget Reno Bro
nodes.summary: Budget Reno Bro is a young TikTok renovation creator who reacts quickly and compares app prices to hardware store prices. On 2026-11-04, Budget Reno Bro posted about Casella, a new Malaysian app in public beta that tags furniture and appliances in a room photo or screenshot with prices and links to Shopee and Taobao offers, with 3 free scans without an account. In the beta, Budget Reno Bro found match accuracy hit-or-miss: one kitchen photo suggested a cabinet that did not fit and one sofa match did not fit; scans of his parents' living room and his rented room missed local equivalents and installation cost. He observed the Best offer badge did not appear for cheap items below a certain threshold, and argued the badge must never be buyable, must be based on total cost (unit, delivery, installation, after-sales, trust), and that merchant-phase ads need clear labels and cost per qualified lead. His line: "Harga app vs harga kedai, bro.

nodes.name: Halim Yaakob
nodes.summary: Halim Yaakob is an air-conditioning installer in Johor Bahru with 16 years of installation experience. He advises buyers to check the full model code on indoor and outdoor unit stickers rather than listing photos, because 1.0HP and 1.5HP units can look identical in a photo while differing in series, capacity, gas type (R32 vs R410A), warranty region and price. He asks for an itemised total installed price: unit, copper piping (about 7 feet standard, extra per foot or per meter), bracket, stabiliser, new breaker, vacuum and labour, plus delivery by postcode. He opposes DIY air-conditioning work, since skipping vacuum and leak tests voids warranty and can ruin the compressor; third-party or non-authorised installers can void brand warranty, compressor warranty usually comes from the manufacturer while labour warranty follows the installer, and quotes should state 'vacuum + leak test included'.

attributes.focus_area: Home renovation and appliance buying in Malaysia
attributes.name: Malaysia Reno Kaki

nodes.name: Malaysia Reno Kaki
nodes.summary: Malaysia Reno Kaki is a multi-racial, nationwide renovation community established in 2015 for homeowners, contractors and suppliers, covering contractor warnings, price checks, shopping finds and DIY tips; members are addressed as "Kaki." House rules require spec-first listings (dimensions, warranty, after-sales coverage rather than price-only posts), no politics, race, religion or unverified personal attacks, and disputes handled through moderator mediation and fact-checking; contractor warnings must carry invoices, dates, photos and messages. It maintains a trusted contractor list updated monthly from member feedback and holds monthly live Q&A sessions with industry experts at 8–11 PM peak on weekends.

nodes.name: Malaysia Reno Kaki
