nodes.summary: Malaysia Reno Kaki is a renovation-focused community that issued an admin announcement advising members to check delivery dates against their own postcode, since lead times differ for Georgetown 10200, Penang mainland, Sabah and Sarawak, and warning that a "2-4 hari" promise can become 12. Its CHECK PRICE guidance covers total landed cost: unit price plus delivery, installation, warranty (original vs parallel import) and trade-in. Members are told to screenshot every promised date and keep chat logs, and to report genuine good and bad experiences; the community stays neutral in disputes and handles them via moderator mediation and fact-checking, with no politics, race, religion or unverified personal attacks. A trusted contractor list is updated monthly based on member feedback, and live Q&A with industry experts runs every month during the 8-11 PM peak, all weekend long.

nodes.name: Aisyah Rahman's sofa
nodes.summary: Aisyah Rahman's sofa is budgeted at RM1,800 in her 'Rumah Impian' plan. Nothing has been purchased yet; she is waiting for the house keys.

nodes.name: iklan labelling
nodes.summary: Sinar Home Marketplace asks for the same disclosure standard it applies to itself: if a slot earns commission, it must be labelled iklan before the click, as fair advertising practice with no hidden bias. Farah Zainal of Kota Kinabalu, Sabah, underlines that a Paid Partner slot must be labelled IKLAN up front, before the click, in plain BM and English; learning only after tapping that it was an ad destroys trust, and disclosure is a relationship, not small print.

attributes.name: Azlan Musa
attributes.renovation_stage: renovating in stages over two years

nodes.name: Azlan Musa
nodes.summary: Azlan Musa is a 44-year-old teacher in Kuantan renovating his terrace house in stages, one room at a time, over two years, buying items on a schedule and sometimes only two to three months after saving them. In his renovation update for month 14 he completed the second bedroom's ceiling fan and wiring for RM514 (5-blade DC motor fan RM289 saved since July after a RM20 sale drop, wiring/casing/switch RM145, certified SIRIM electrician labour RM80), taking 3 weeks while waiting for stock, with the master bedroom aircond still in planning for the following month. He keeps receipts, dates, photos and saved items in a renovation spreadsheet and asks sellers for itemised totals: unit price plus delivery to his own Kuantan postcode plus piping, bracket, vacuum, breaker and labour, then warranty covering parts, compressor and labour with a local authorised service centre; he also asks whether warranty starts at purchase or installation and whether third-party installers void it.

nodes.name: Casella side-by-side match
nodes.summary: Ah Boon Fix It tested the Casella app's side-by-side match: 3 out of 5 suggestions were decent, but a photo of his kitchen still suggested a cabinet 20cm too wide. He advised measuring rather than trusting the app to measure.

nodes.name: English
nodes.summary: English is one of the app's languages, alongside Chinese and Bahasa Melayu.

nodes.name: Sinar Home Marketplace
nodes.summary: Sinar Home Marketplace is an online-only Malaysian home goods seller based in Puchong, operating mostly on Shopee, and states it compares its Shopee advertising return against leads from other merchant portals daily. Its stated position is that cost per qualified lead is the only metric that survives scrutiny, that clicks and "92% match" badges do not pay the bills while a real WhatsApp enquiry and showroom visit do, and that unverified leads inflate every number downstream. It calls for paid Partner slots to be labelled "iklan" before the click, for "Best offer" badges to be unbuyable and based on total landed cost (unit + delivery + installation + import tax + after-sales), for lead verification separating genuine buyers from bots, for published match accuracy (top-1 and false-match rate), for consent, credit and compensation before use of creator or shop images, and for retention periods and real deletes stated before upload.

nodes.name: kolam-patterned rug
nodes.summary: Sarah Thevi, an Indian-Malaysian consumer in Klang and a self-described consumer voice rather than a seller or tech expert, tested Casella with screenshots from local Indian-Malaysian home pages; a teak mandir cabinet returned as "wooden cabinet", a kolam-patterned rug as "bohemian rug", and a stainless steel thali set went into a random kitchen category, missing every cultural cue. She asked whether Casella's recognition logic includes Indian-Malaysian items or only English-language Western decor, whether it can tell a prayer-room cabinet from a plain wardrobe and a kolam rug from a generic patterned rug, where room photos go, how long they are kept, whether deletion is permanent, whether the app can be used as a guest without a phone number, and whether affiliate commission is disclosed on every link before the click.

nodes.name: Hafiz Ismail's tape measure
nodes.summary: Hafiz Ismail's tape measure stays on the seat during showroom visits. At a Klang Valley shop he stayed and measured after the salesperson gave honest specifications, and his rule is to measure, sit, and check fabric before deciding on a sofa.

nodes.name: sofa making
nodes.summary: Vista Sofa Factory Outlet runs a sofa factory outlet in Muar and builds each piece slightly differently in frame wood, foam density and hand stitching, which no algorithm captures. It advises honest tags covering material (rotan type or frame wood), dimensions in cm (L x D x H), seat height, foam type and delivery area, plus real photos of hands working rather than only finished products. It holds that customers should come see and sit first, saying "kalau tak duduk, tak tahu" and "sit before you buy", and extends this to Rimbun Team, noting Muar and Melaka local craft can succeed together.

nodes.name: Wong Kar Fai
nodes.summary: Wong Kar Fai, 48, lives in Georgetown, Penang (postcode 10200), and describes himself as an operations guy in Penang, not a technician. He tests whether a "Best offer" is really best against his own search, checking Shopee, Lazada, Mudah, Courts, SenQ and smaller Penang shops himself before trusting any offer. He demands total landed cost: unit price + delivery fee + installation + warranty (original authorised or parallel import) + old-appliance trade-in, with delivery estimates tied to the real postcode (Georgetown 10200, Butterworth, Balik Pulau, Penang mainland and island are not one delivery lane). He requires full model codes (indoor and outdoor stickers screenshotted before deposit), capacity matched to room size, and written terms; from a fridge experience he learned to demand unit + piping + bracket + vacuum + breaker + labour in one number, and he writes the model, price and promised delivery date in his notebook before paying.

nodes.name: image search
nodes.summary: Image search is discussed across Malaysian home-improvement and appliance communities as a feature for finding matching products, with a focus on whether it delivers real, verifiable local leads rather than sticker-price comparisons. Grace Chin, a computer-vision practitioner, rejects claims of beating Google Lens for general image search while holding that niche domains with small, well-curated labeled datasets can outperform generalist models; her standing request is to state the domain, test set, baseline, and published failure slices, framed as "Show me the benchmark" and "no proof, no ringgit." Sinar Home Marketplace, an online-only home goods seller in Puchong operating mainly on Shopee, asks that scan accuracy and false-match rate both be published, that affiliate commission be labeled before the click in BM and English, and that retention and real delete be stated before upload with consent and credit for creator or small-shop images.

nodes.name: scan history
nodes.summary: Chua Li Ting asked how long scan history is kept, whether deletion is permanent, and whether the scanner can be used as a guest without signing in with a real name. She tests the delete button with a dummy photo before trusting any scanner.

nodes.name: B40 families
nodes.summary: B40 families on a budget make up most of Nadia Home Diary's audience, for whom the total landed cost — delivery, installation, and import tax — is the only number that counts.

nodes.name: Rina Kecil Living's before/after photos
nodes.summary: Rina Kecil Living's before/after photos were used in 2021 by a popular home design app without credit or permission; she only found out when a follower tagged her, and she felt violated and undervalued. She raises this in asking whether Casella credits and compensates the creators whose content it uses, under the tag #CreditCreators.

nodes.name: app scan
nodes.summary: Muhammad Hazim of Johor Bahru reports that the app scan's "92% match" is not a model code, and that he photographs the indoor and outdoor stickers side by side and writes the full model in a spreadsheet before comparing. He says the app covers only one side of the border, showing Johor Bahru listings or Singapore listings but not both, and that models seen on shelves sometimes do not appear in the app at all. The Sabah Sarawak Home Group admin team states that a "92% match" is a similarity score, not a model code, and that buyers should screenshot both stickers side by side and confirm the full model code on the indoor and outdoor stickers, capacity matched to room size, and total cost through installation and testing (piping, bracket, vacuum, breaker, labour) before clicking buy.

nodes.name: Casella public beta
nodes.summary: Casella runs a public beta app in Malaysia that tags furniture and appliances from a photo or screenshot and links to Shopee/Taobao listings, earning affiliate commission. One listing slot is a paid Partner slot that cannot receive the "Best offer" badge; the beta includes 3 free scans. Sabah Sarawak Home Group noted there is no measured match accuracy yet and warned East Malaysian buyers that sticker price excludes shipping to Sabah/Sarawak, import tax and installation. Halim Yaakob reported a Mount Austin customer bought a 1.5HP unit on a "92% match" that was a different outdoor unit series and excluded vacuum and breaker, and pressed for total installed price and clear affiliate labelling.

nodes.name: real landed cost sheet
nodes.summary: A shared "real landed cost" sheet is an admin commitment of Malaysia Reno Kaki, using User 6's method: unit price + shipping + installation + warranty. It aligns with the group's advice to compare total landed cost — unit price, shipping to the buyer's postcode, installation, and warranty coverage — before committing to any big-ticket item.

nodes.name: Melvin Pang
nodes.summary: Melvin Pang replied in Taobao Kaki Malaysia to Melissa Anak Jimbun's question about whether RM800 to ship a 3-seater sofa from Taobao to Kuching is normal. Melissa thanked Melvin Pang and the others who replied in her final decision post on the sofa purchase, published November 4, 2026, where she chose a local Kuching supplier at RM2,680 delivered and installed over the Taobao option at RM1,450 plus RM800 shipping with no local warranty service — a RM430 difference — and advised buying bulky items locally while Taobao remains fine for small items like beadwork and kitchen tools.

nodes.name: app privacy settings
nodes.summary: Priya Nair, a renter in Petaling Jaya, follows a routine for every new app: try guest scan or guest mode before registering, review each permission and reject location access without reason, check language options (she requested Tamil for one furniture app), ensure scan history and data can be deleted, and screenshot the privacy policy for reference. She framed this as controlling what can be controlled, since small furniture can be moved but shared data is hard to retract. On 2026-11-04 she shared the checklist publicly, saying she wanted to join tenant groups, small-space living communities, or app-privacy channels, and that she would wait rather than join blindly; she described rental-friendly decor as small items that can be moved, and her cat Milo sits on her folding side table.

nodes.name: Rosli Ahmad's motorcycle workshop
nodes.summary: Rosli Ahmad runs a small motorcycle workshop (bengkel motor) in Kangar, Perlis, and is also an online buyer. In February he ordered a sprocket set from Shah Alam whose listing said 2-4 working days; it arrived on day 12 with tracking stalled at the Petaling Jaya hub, and he lost a customer job because the motorcycle could not be finished on time. The seller replied "Perlis usually slower, boss" with a laughing emoji. He keeps screenshots of chats, tracking and dates in his Pos book and asks sellers for written full model codes, total landed cost by postcode, real delivery days stated upfront ("Perlis, add 2-3 days"), and warranty terms covering parts and labour.

nodes.name: total landed cost
nodes.summary: Total landed cost is the real purchase price: unit price plus delivery to the buyer's own postcode, installation, import tax and shipping for cross-border orders, warranty coverage (original vs parallel import), trade-in, and after-sales. The "Best offer" badge is calculated from total landed cost plus seller trust and cannot be bought; any paid Partner slot must be labelled "iklan" before the click. Full dimensions (W x D x H in mm), cut-out dimensions, gas type (LPG vs natural gas), exact indoor/outdoor model codes, and warranty duration covering parts, compressor and labour must be stated in writing before purchase or cabinet work, along with warranty start date (purchase vs installation) and whether third-party installers void it.

nodes.name: interior design
nodes.summary: Vanessa Goh is a KL-based interior designer who works under #KLinterior and #rumahku and tells homeowners every week to "compare total, not headline." She points to piping per foot, brackets, labour, and whether the compressor warranty survives a third-party installer as things a photo of a unit will never show; she applies the same discipline to furniture and appliances she specs, and holds that if the seller won't put inclusions and warranty in writing, that is the answer — no hidden fees, no surprises on installation day. Her sourcing rule is to check the model number first, then the price, and to buy where she can inspect and talk to the maker; she cites a solid teak sideboard found at an old furniture shop for less than a lookalike veneer piece because she touched it first.

nodes.name: Hafiz Ismail
nodes.summary: Hafiz Ismail is a 34-year-old homeowner in the Klang Valley furnishing a 950 sq ft condo. He compares total landed cost in writing (unit + delivery to his postcode + installation + any tax, plus disposal) rather than listing price: a local Klang Valley store 3-seater at RM1,890 + RM80 delivery + RM0 installation + RM0 lift booking = RM1,970 versus an online-only model at RM1,690 + RM180 shipping + RM150 white-glove installation + RM60 lift booking = RM2,080; the online model's cushion sank in the showroom within seconds. In one week he visited three stores after work and sat on eleven sofas, still shortlisting rather than buying.

nodes.name: Georgetown 10200
nodes.summary: Georgetown 10200 is a Penang postcode used by Wong Kar Fai as the example that delivery estimates must follow the real postcode: Georgetown 10200 is not "2-4 days" if stock is in KL. Wong Kar Fai holds that shipping to "your postcode" is not one lane — Georgetown 10200, Butterworth and Balik Pulau differ — that some KL sellers quote a flat rate then ask for a top-up at the doorstep, and that a Penang test client should be split island versus mainland, since Georgetown 10200 and Seberang Perai are different delivery and installation lanes; a Penang delivery zone must state Georgetown 10200 versus mainland plus an installation rate per item. Malaysia Reno Kaki's PSA and Grace Chin's listing-hygiene checklist name Georgetown 10200 among postcodes where lead times are not the same; Cheah Xin Yi and Rumah Bajet MY repeat that "2-4 hari" to Georgetown 10200 differs from Sabah/Sarawak, and Hafiz Ismail endorses the check-the-date PSA.

nodes.name: Subang Jaya
nodes.summary: Subang Jaya is the home city of Hannah Lau, 24, who saves hundreds of room tours on TikTok but seldom buys and would scan for fun, possibly never reaching an offer. Kevin Lim is based in Subang Jaya; his shopping philosophy is "total landed cost or nothing" — item price plus shipping, installation, and warranty in one clear RM number — and hidden shipping fees and fine print lead him to delete apps after one bad experience, with a rule that the first result must be correct or he deletes, and the total must be honest or he walks. He tests one app promising combined search, finds an electric kettle instead of a 1.8L rice cooker as the first result, and deletes it in 2 minutes. He screenshots, compares delivery days, waits for 6.6, then checks out, and keeps notes rather than carts.

nodes.name: Oyen
nodes.summary: Oyen is a cat belonging to Nadia of Nadia Home Diary, based in Shah Alam. In a November 4, 2026 post, Nadia included "Oyen says hi too" alongside her home decor content. In a later November 4, 2026 post about her plans, including one day having her own home decor line, Nadia wrote "Oyen pun tumpang salam." In a further November 4, 2026 post about quietly testing affiliate links in her bio, her BUDGET ROOM MAKEOVER UNTUK B40 series, and building a Linktree/website for recommendations, Nadia wrote "Oyen pun dah tolong susun bantal."

nodes.name: room-scanning app
nodes.summary: Budget Reno Bro is beta-testing a room-scanning app. Scanning his parents' living room produced a clean number, but the app missed local equivalents and installation cost; he walked to the kedai hardware and the real total differed. He wants any "shop-the-whole-room total" to show which items, which local SKUs, and whether installation and delivery are included — the slice, not the aggregate. He frames this as "harga app ≠ harga kedai," "listing price ≠ landed cost," and "headline accuracy ≠ accuracy on YOUR room," and advises fixing the measurement before trusting the number ("Kita kira dulu, baru cakap").

nodes.name: Rumah Impian album
nodes.summary: Hannah Lau's "Rumah Impian" album is a collection of screenshots she keeps for her planned small KL apartment. She saved a post about total cost through installation rather than sticker price into it.

nodes.name: delete test
nodes.summary: The delete test is a precondition: a customer's room photo is not a data point kept by default. Rina Kecil Living's version requires the retention period to be stated before upload in plain BM and English, with a delete that really deletes, tested first with a plant photo. Jason Reno Journal says to test first and publish the numbers, including the negative result, before making claims.

nodes.name: Budget Reno Bro
nodes.summary: Budget Reno Bro posted a weekend check-in for homeowners and renovators of Sabah and Sarawak on Twitter, advising them to check local suppliers first and compare total landed cost: unit price plus shipping to the buyer's postcode plus installation plus warranty coverage. The post noted that a "2-4 day" delivery from a KL warehouse routinely becomes 1-2 weeks once it crosses the South China Sea, and asked for realistic transit days and courier coverage for KK, Kuching, Sandakan, Sibu, Tawau, Miri and rural postcodes. It also advised confirming who services a warranty locally, required documentation (invoices, dates, photos, messages) for contractor warnings with unverified accusations removed, and encouraged before-and-after photos, supplier recommendations and group-buy interest to cut shipping costs. Malaysia Reno Kaki quoted the post and commented on it.

nodes.name: contractors
nodes.summary: Contractors are among the people already used to identify where an item is from.

nodes.name: Partner slot
nodes.summary: A merchant can pay for one "Partner" slot per list, at position 2; it must pass a match-quality threshold and can never receive the Best offer badge. Casella's merchant phase for Malaysian stores includes a paid Partner slot per list that cannot receive the Best offer badge, and it is not available during the beta. Retailers and commenters including Hafiz Ismail, Azlan Musa, Wong Kar Fai, Vista Sofa Factory Outlet, Kedai Perabot Seri Jaya, Bintang Elektrik, Sri Mutiara Home Centre, Rumah Lengkap Marketing, Tilam Selesa Bedding, Rimbun Rattan Crafts, Sinar Home Marketplace, Rumah Bajet MY, Sabah Sarawak Home Group, Farah Zainal and Ah Boon Fix It require the slot be labelled clearly as advertising (iklan) before the click in BM and English, and that cost per qualified lead be shown in writing before small shops commit.

attributes.name: Lim Wei Jie's kitchen appliance checklist

nodes.name: Lim Wei Jie's kitchen appliance checklist
nodes.summary: Lim Wei Jie's checklist for buying kitchen appliances for his Seremban 2 terrace house covers four points: get full dimensions (W x D x H, mm) and cut-out dimensions before confirming any cabinet work, since a contractor once built a cabinet without checking appliance dimensions and the result did not fit; confirm installation is included in the price, as improper installation of gas appliances is a safety hazard; check warranty length, coverage, and who services it locally (Seremban/Nilai coverage); and verify after-sales support in writing before payment. The checklist states a good deal is not the lowest price but value, quality, and after-sales support. Hafiz Ismail endorsed it, agreeing on the order of dimensions first, then installation, warranty and local servicing before price, and noting cut-out dimensions before cabinet work is the step people skip and the one that costs them.

nodes.name: comment 42
nodes.summary: Comment 42, alongside comment 154, raised privacy questions about a scan-and-link app: how long room photos are stored, whether they are used for training, and whether deletion is truly permanent. Grace Chin cited both comments as the same coin's two sides and said that until these points are written clearly, not a single photo should be uploaded, endorsing the instinct to delete first and decide later.

nodes.name: home design app
nodes.summary: In 2021 a home design app used Rina Kecil Living's before/after photos without credit or permission; she found out when a follower tagged her. Rina Kecil Living raised the question of whose images train such models and whether creators were asked, arguing that if room photos, reels and screenshots feed a photo-to-SKU index, the benchmark rests on uncredited, uncompensated creator labour.

nodes.name: Rosli Ahmad
nodes.summary: Rosli Ahmad, 50, lives in Kangar, Perlis (postcode 01000), where he runs a small motorcycle workshop (bengkel motor) and also buys online. A February sprocket set order from Shah Alam, listed at 2-4 working days, arrived on day 12 with tracking stuck at the Petaling Jaya hub and the seller replying "Perlis usually slower, boss" with a laughing emoji; Rosli says he lost a customer job because the motorcycle could not be finished on time.

nodes.name: cut-out dimensions
nodes.summary: Lim Wei Jie requires full dimensions (W x D x H in mm) and cut-out dimensions in any offer for a built-in oven and gas stove for a Seremban 2 terrace house kitchen renovation, and will not consider price-only replies. Lim Wei Jie adds that for built-in appliances the cut-out dimensions (cabinet opening width, depth and airflow clearances) matter more than external ones, and that for gas stoves the gas type (LPG vs piped), hose/regulator standard and certified installation must be confirmed; a full model code, warranty terms covering parts and labour, and total landed cost including installation are also required. Wong Kar Fai advises that cut-out dimensions must match or the installer will charge to enlarge the countertop, a hidden cost, and that the warranty should cover parts, labour and gas valve.

nodes.name: warranty coverage
nodes.summary: Muhammad Hazim asks whether warranty is Malaysia or Singapore; if the set is from Singapore, he questions whether a service centre across the border is practical and whether there are hidden charges such as GST, delivery, installation, vacuum, or breaker. He will only click a badge that shows total landed cost, model, and warranty.

nodes.name: Cheah Xin Yi
nodes.summary: Cheah Xin Yi is 26, lives in Kuala Lumpur, reads Xiaohongshu daily, and is a Setapak condo renter with no drilling allowed. Her checking rules: full cut-out/dimensions (W x D x H, mm) in writing; total landed cost = unit + postage to her postcode + installation + who services the warranty locally; screenshot every promised date and the chat before paying; test delete buttons with a plant photo first; commission labelled on every link before the click; a confidence score on the badge, a "no match" option, and a "Best offer" badge showing delivery and installation. She cites a 2022 viral air fryer purchase where the top comment's affiliate code was expired and shipping took 11 days instead of 3, and she does not trust a comment link unless multiple users confirm it. She keeps a Google Sheet of price, review count and whether the poster replied in comments, plus an "XHS links to check" folder, and re-screenshots total landed cost after a week to catch fake sale prices.

nodes.name: rattan workshop
nodes.summary: The rattan workshop is a small handmade rattan business in Melaka whose team signs off as "The Rimbun Team." Its lesson is that the listing price is never the real price: for a handmade piece, total landed cost also includes the weaver's hours, the honesty of the material, and who will repair it years from now. Unlike a warehouse SKU, no two of its baskets or chairs are identical, so "similar" in a photo means almost nothing for handmade goods.

nodes.name: sofa and furniture buying
nodes.summary: Hafiz Ismail's guidance on sofa and furniture buying, given in response to Malaysia Reno Kaki's CHECK PRICE announcement, holds that for big items the "date vs postcode" rule saves the most trouble, and that buyers should measure door, corridor and lift clearance before delivery day because an item that fits the room but not the lobby is the worst surprise. Buyers should get seat height, seat depth and foam density in cm, in writing, plus confirmation of local warranty service, and should screenshot the promised delivery window. Sellers who refuse a viewing or hide shipping costs are ones to walk away from; the approach is to view the actual unit first before shortlisting, since "kalau tak duduk, tak tahu."

nodes.name: rak lipat
nodes.summary: Priya Nair chose a rak lipat as one of the small, movable items for a rental where the landlord does not allow drilling or painting; it can be lifted and taken along when moving.

nodes.name: project budgets
nodes.summary: Project budgets are planned for the next phase and are not available at beta.

nodes.name: built-in oven
nodes.summary: Lim Wei Jie's specification comparison method for home appliances covers built-in ovens, stoves, and hoods, with columns for model number, dimensions (W x D x H in mm), cut-out dimensions (built-in items only), power rating or gas type (LPG vs natural gas, to be confirmed rather than assumed), warranty period and coverage, whether installation is included and who installs, and the nearest after-sales service location; if a seller cannot fill in even half the columns, Wei Jie moves on. Wei Jie sought built-in oven and gas stove recommendations for a Seremban 2 terrace house kitchen renovation, requiring full dimensions and cut-out dimensions, warranty period and coverage, confirmation that installation is included in the price (proper gas fitting is non-negotiable for safety), and after-sales service coverage in the Seremban/Nilai area, and would not accept price-only replies.

nodes.name: Aisyah Rahman's TV console
nodes.summary: Aisyah Rahman's TV console is budgeted at RM600 in her 'Rumah Impian' plan and is still under consideration. Nothing has been purchased yet; she is waiting for the house keys.

nodes.name: creator credit and consent
nodes.summary: Jason Reno Journal holds that creator photos are their work, just like a retailer's catalogue shot, and that any scan-and-link app listing a piece, using before/after shots, or feeding images into training must have consent first and credit after. He demands credit plus compensation with explicit consent before creator content is used for listings, demos, or AI training, and requires affiliate commission to be labelled on every link before the click in BM and English ("disclosure is not a disclaimer"). He also demands publicly measured match accuracy — per-category precision/recall, how the labelled test set was built, and the false-match rate between near-identical units — rather than "92% match" claims, and presses for full model code, cut-out/clearance dimensions, total landed cost including East Malaysia, and written warranty covering parts and labour. He turned down a RM10,000 affiliate deal for an untested product.

nodes.name: precision@1
nodes.summary: precision@1 is a benchmark metric cited by Vanessa Goh as proving whether an app put the right item on screen, but not whether that item will look right in the room or last a Malaysian year. She proposed adding proportion and texture, since a 92% match on the correct SKU can still fail on depth, pilling, or veneer swelling, and provenance, publishing the consent/credit/compensation share next to precision and recall. She argued a 92%-accurate pipeline on 0% consenting data is a liability, not a benchmark.

nodes.name: B40 & small-space kakis
nodes.summary: B40 & small-space kakis is the audience Nadia Home Diary addressed when adding tips to a home-buying checklist. Nadia Home Diary, a home decor creator in Shah Alam, advised them to screenshot the total cost to the door (unit + shipping + import tax + installation + after-sales) and compare side-by-side, noting that for rentals and condos the difference is often hundreds of ringgit. She also advised that room photos and before/after shots are not free data and require credit, consent and real delete stated before upload.

nodes.name: Hannah Lau's KL apartment
nodes.summary: Hannah Lau is planning a small apartment in KL someday; it is not yet acquired or renovated.

nodes.name: XHS links to check folder
nodes.summary: A personal folder used by Cheah Xin Yi, a KL renter, to save links to check, including a checklist she called "damn solid."

nodes.name: Miri kaki's pendant light
nodes.summary: A Miri kaki's pendant light arrived cracked, which Nadia Home Diary cited as an example of the real shipping experiences that protect people, and Melissa Anak Jimbun cited alongside her own chipped wardrobe corner as evidence that thin packaging fails across the South China Sea.

nodes.name: gas hob
nodes.summary: A gas hob is one of two appliances Lim Wei Jie is finalizing for a Seremban 2 terrace house kitchen, alongside a built-in oven. His fixed criteria are stated dimensions in mm (W x D x H) plus cut-out dimensions, warranty length and exactly what it covers, installation included in the price and done by a qualified installer, and after-sales service coverage in the Seremban / Nilai area. Azlan Musa, renovating a Kuantan terrace house stage by stage one room at a time, buys items on schedule sometimes 2-3 months after saving and will not compromise on water heaters and gas hobs: a trained installer plus leak test and a regulator/hose to LPG or piped standard are required. Grace Chin's buyer checklist requires the warranty start date (purchase vs install) and parts, compressor and labour terms in writing, and states that for gas a trained installer plus leak test is safety, not upsell.

nodes.name: Facebook group
nodes.summary: In a lead-tracker comparison of two small bedroom-furniture sellers with near-identical spend, the Facebook group placement (Client A) spent RM420 and produced 96 leads, 41 WhatsApp replies, 14 qualified leads (budget, location and timing clear) and 5 closed sales, at RM30 cost per qualified lead. The marketplace listing boost (Client B) spent RM450 and produced 210 leads, 58 WhatsApp replies, 9 qualified leads and 2 closed sales, at RM50 cost per qualified lead. The conclusion was that the marketplace wins on lead volume while the group wins on leads that become sales, with both depending on listing hygiene covering price, size, material and delivery time. Nadia Home Diary attributed the group's advantage to trust, which converts leads into customers.

nodes.name: Facebook renovation groups
nodes.summary: Facebook renovation groups are a community on Facebook focused on renovation. People already use them as a way to find out where an item is from.

nodes.name: CHECK PRICE
nodes.summary: CHECK PRICE is a total-landed-cost check advocated in Malaysia Reno Kaki posts and echoed by commenters. Malaysia Reno Kaki's admin announcement defines it as unit + delivery + installation + warranty (original vs parallel import) + trade-in, and warns that fast-delivery promises must be checked against the buyer's postcode, since "2-4 hari" from a KL warehouse is not the same to Georgetown 10200, Penang mainland, Sabah, or Sarawak. Sabah Sarawak Home Group added that landed cost in East Malaysia must include the sea crossing (RM40 Peninsular shipping can become RM180+ to KK/Sibu, and "2-4 days" can become 2 weeks), to check local KK and Kuching suppliers first, and to pool group-buy orders with neighbours. Hafiz Ismail's version adds delivery to the buyer's postcode, whether installation is included, who services the warranty locally, trade-in, and seat height, seat depth, and door/lift clearance in writing.

nodes.name: teak sideboard
nodes.summary: Vanessa Goh's favourite sourcing story is a solid teak sideboard she found at an old furniture shop for less than a lookalike veneer piece, because she touched it first.

nodes.name: #KLinterior
nodes.summary: #KLinterior is a hashtag used by Vanessa Goh, who identifies herself as the design voice in a thread, alongside #CheckLocalFirst and #warmminimalism in one post and #CreditCreators in another. Her posts under it argue that a designer look is not a filter but proportion, light, texture, and how a room lives, and that buyers should ask for landed totals in writing, credit makers, and set retention periods before any scan.

nodes.name: reporting a wrong tag
nodes.summary: Reporting a wrong tag is planned for the next phase and is not available at beta.

nodes.name: Rimbun Rattan Crafts' baskets
nodes.summary: Rimbun Rattan Crafts, a rattan workshop in Melaka, states that no two of its baskets are ever identical, so a "lookalike" in a photo is never the same piece in a customer's hands. The workshop tells customers to compare total cost rather than advertised price: unit price + delivery to the customer's postcode (Sabah and Sarawak carry different rates, and the workshop has shipped there) + hand-weaving labour + warranty and who does repairs.

nodes.name: Philips screwdriver
nodes.summary: The single tool Budget Reno Bro used to install a shelf and bracket bought at Mr DIY Puchong in 40 minutes.

nodes.name: Gain City
nodes.summary: Gain City is one of the Singapore retailers Muhammad Hazim of Johor Bahru compares against Johor Bahru options when shopping for electrical goods, alongside Courts, Harvey Norman, Best Denki, and Mustafa. His comparison method weighs Johor Bahru versus Singapore listings, and he notes Singapore prices are sometimes cheaper even after exchange rate and transport, though warranty logistics usually lead him to buy in Johor Bahru.

nodes.name: Kajang
nodes.summary: Kajang is a city in Selangor, Malaysia, and the home city of Chua Li Ting, 34, a mother based there. Chua Li Ting asks sellers whether installation is included and whether the installer is a certified gas installer, the warranty length and what it covers, who services appliances in Kajang/Selangor, whether everything is confirmed in writing (hitam putih) before payment, and whether anyone has actually checked the seller. She keeps a notebook and screenshots of invoices, dates and chat logs before posting anything about a seller, and for apps asks about the data retention period and tests photo deletion with a dummy photo before uploading more. In November 2026 she engaged with posts on appliance buying, saying value means clear costs, clear warranty and clear after-sales rather than the lowest price.

nodes.name: Kelantan
nodes.summary: Kelantan is the east-coast state whose access problems Zarina Yusof, based in Kota Bharu (postcode 15200), raises repeatedly: sellers advertising "nationwide delivery" or "whole Malaysia" often do not reach Kota Bharu, or add surcharges and delays, so she asks whether offers reach Kelantan before price matters — "Kalau tak boleh hantar ke Kota Bharu, tak payah cakap pasal harga." She groups Kelantan with Sabah, Sarawak and the East Coast (Pantai Timur) as treated as "outstation," noting the same checklist applies across them: postcode first, then total landed cost (unit + delivery to postcode + installation + tax + a reachable warranty service centre).

nodes.name: gas stove
nodes.summary: Azlan Musa advises that for a gas stove, proper gas fitting is non-negotiable, and that the hose and regulator should carry SIRIM or an equivalent standard. He recommends asking whether the warranty covers the valve and burner, using a certified installer rather than self-installation, and measuring cut-out dimensions twice before purchase. He checks dimensions, warranty and after-sales before committing, and stores items for months ahead of his own renovation.

nodes.name: Samsung
nodes.summary: Samsung is one of the appliance brands Sim Kok Leong is comparing, alongside Panasonic, before buying from a local shop he can walk into.

nodes.name: Budget Reno Bro
nodes.summary: Budget Reno Bro is a content creator who posts videos on home renovation pricing and repeats the same points in each video. Budget Reno Bro argues that a "total" must be line-itemed as unit + shipping by poskod + import tax + installation + after-sales, and that a seller's refusal to quote in writing is the red flag rather than the price. From beta-testing, Budget Reno Bro reports that the "Best offer" badge does not appear for cheap items below a certain threshold, and questions whether that is fair to budget renovators who want best offer even on an RM29 lamp. Budget Reno Bro holds that paid Partner slots must be labeled "iklan" before the click, since disclosure is not a disclaimer, and advises buying local when the app's landed total is within 10-15% of the shop price. Budget Reno Bro uses the hashtag #RumahBajetMY.

nodes.name: pos.com.my
nodes.summary: pos.com.my is the official domain of Pos Malaysia, identified as the legitimate site for parcel delivery matters. Thinesh Kumar warned that a "parcel failed delivery" message should not be acted on by tapping its link, and that the official domain is pos.com.my rather than pos-my.xyz or bit.ly links. The advised steps are to check the domain, open the official app or type the site directly instead of clicking from WhatsApp or SMS, and never enter a bank username or OTP on a page reached from a link.

nodes.name: Semenanjung
nodes.summary: Semenanjung is the region that warranty coverage often covers exclusively. Budget Reno Bro's East Malaysia weekend check-in post advised Sabah and Sarawak homeowners that an authorised service centre they can actually reach beats a longer warranty paper that only covers Semenanjung, and that a "2-4 day" KL warehouse delivery routinely becomes 1-2 weeks once it crosses the South China Sea. Melissa Anak Jimbun, in Kuching, said a 5-year warranty covering only Semenanjung equals zero for Sarawak buyers. Jason Reno Journal and Malaysia Reno Kaki repeated that a 5-year warranty paper covering only Semenanjung is zero value to a buyer in KK or Sibu, and Malaysia Reno Kaki's buyer filter asks whether a local service centre for the warranty is reachable, since paper covering only Semenanjung is zero.

nodes.name: Rimbun Team
nodes.summary: Rimbun Team is the team behind a furniture-scanning app discussed in Reddit threads on 4 November 2026. Aisyah Rahman praised the team's handmade local furniture effort and encouraged them to continue, wishing them success. In the same thread, Lau Kok Wai asked for plain answers before scanning a room: whether tags show total landed cost (unit, delivery, installation, import tax) or sticker price only, where room photos go and how long they are kept, whether deletion is permanent, and whether guest scans work without an account or phone number. Budget Reno Bro pressed that the Best offer badge must never be buyable, that placement may be paid but the badge must still reflect total cost, and that the merchant phase must label ads upfront, rank badges by total cost (unit, delivery, installation, after-sales, trust), and show cost per qualified lead; Budget Reno Bro also beta-tested and found the Best offer badge did not appear for cheap items below a certain threshold. Dr.

nodes.name: Farah Zainal
nodes.summary: Farah Zainal is a 38-year-old homeowner in Kota Kinabalu, Sabah, undertaking a kitchen renovation. She applies a "total landed cost" standard covering unit price, shipping to her postcode, import tax, installation, after-sales and who services the warranty locally, and treats any warranty serviced only in Semenanjung as worth zero in Sabah. Her curtain order from a West Malaysian seller cost more in shipping than the curtains themselves, an RM40 "Peninsular rate" became RM180 across the South China Sea, and a "2-4 days" promise stretched to two weeks. She asks sellers to state full prices including Sabah/Sarawak and rural postcodes, give realistic transit days in writing, label Paid Partner slots IKLAN in plain BM and English before the click, and keep "Best offer" badges unbuyable and based on total landed cost. She backs group-buys to cut shipping and will pay more to a local Sabah/Sarawak supplier than risk a cheap West Malaysian listing.

nodes.name: Klang Valley consumer interviews
nodes.summary: Klang Valley consumer interviews conducted by Dr. Salina Rahmat surfaced two consumer behaviors: appliance shopper Rajesh Pillai learned to ask for the out-the-door number, and safety-conscious Haslinda Omar always asks who installs. Dr. Salina Rahmat cited these as consumers manually doing what Rumah Lengkap Marketing's listing hygiene checklist does by default.

attributes.name: Seremban 2 terrace house
attributes.renovation_stage: comparing offers for a new stove and built-in oven

nodes.name: Seremban 2 terrace house
nodes.summary: Lim Wei Jie owns a terrace house in Seremban 2 bought for his family, where he is renovating the kitchen and comparing offers for a new stove and built-in oven. Before buying any kitchen appliance he requires, in writing: full dimensions in mm (W x D x H) plus cut-out dimensions for built-in items; clearance from combustible surfaces; gas type confirmed (LPG vs natural gas); installation included by a qualified installer; warranty length and coverage; and after-sales service within reach of Seremban/Nilai. A contractor once built a cabinet without checking his appliance dimensions and the result did not fit, and he will not repeat that. For misleading product photos he asks for a tape measure or standard reference (A4 paper, floor tile) beside the unit, and dimensions stated in listing text. He also seeks local Seremban/Nilai home improvement groups that share specifications, dimensions and genuine after-sales experiences.

nodes.name: benchmark
nodes.summary: Ah Boon Fix It, a Casella beta-tester who showed his failures on camera, backs a published benchmark for the app's computer-vision matching, calling a confident wrong match more costly than "no match" and urging "NO MATCH" on screen when unsure. His acid test is near-identical units such as 1.0HP vs 1.5HP aircond and NR-BX418VS vs a lookalike, since a photo cannot read the sticker; if the labelled set has no near-identical pairs, the number is borrowed confidence. He wants per-region rows including a POSKOD row, not just state, citing Kuching, Sibu, Kangar, Kota Bharu and Sandakan logistics, and advises buyers to count total landed cost to the house (unit, delivery, installation, import tax) rather than sticker price. He also requires affiliate commission labelled on every link before the click in BM and English, and says credit and price both assume the app put the right item on screen, a measurable accuracy claim.

nodes.name: Rumah Ideas folder
nodes.summary: Sarah Thevi, an Indian-Malaysian consumer voice from Klang, keeps a "Rumah Ideas" folder of local Indian-Malaysian home pages and of useful home-decor checklists. She tested Casella and found the app only in English and Malay, and that screenshots from local Indian-Malaysian home pages were misrecognised: a teak mandir cabinet came back as "wooden cabinet", a kolam-patterned rug as "bohemian rug", and a stainless steel thali set went into a random kitchen bin. Before uploading photos of her parents' home she wants to know where photos go, how long they are kept, whether deletion is permanent, and whether guest use without a phone number is possible; she tested with a plant photo first. If Casella adds Tamil and recognises that style, she will tell her family and friends in Klang; if not, she will keep the folder and ask local shops instead.

nodes.name: Chan Mei Fong's small notebook
nodes.summary: Chan Mei Fong keeps a small notebook in which she writes down everything, then goes to a shop to see the display unit. She uses it when shopping, including for appliance purchases such as her washing machine.

nodes.name: room renovation
nodes.summary: Azlan Musa is renovating his terraced house stage by stage, one room at a time, buying items according to schedule and sometimes 2–3 months after saving. He keeps the checklist in his renovation spreadsheet and asks whether warranty starts on the purchase date or the installation date when a unit is bought now but installed the following month, wanting it in black and white. He asks shops for the full model code on the sticker (indoor and outdoor for aircond), an itemised total (unit + delivery + piping + bracket + vacuum + breaker + labour), and warranty covering parts, compressor, and labour from a local authorised source, holding that value comes from correct installation and after-sales. Melissa Anak Jimbun screenshotted the checklist for her renovation comparison in Kuching.

nodes.name: total-landed-cost PSA
nodes.summary: The total-landed-cost PSA was posted by the MalaysiaRenoKaki admins on 2026-11-04, warning that fast-delivery promises must be checked against the buyer's postcode because lead times differ across Georgetown 10200, Penang mainland, Sabah, and Sarawak, and "2-4 hari" can become 12. Its checklist covers unit + delivery + installation + warranty (original vs parallel import) + trade-in, and it advises screenshotting every promised date and keeping chat logs as protection. Jason Reno Journal praised the checklist as the discipline every gadget listing should have, adding that a warranty is only worth what a reachable service centre will honour and that "5 years, Semenanjung only" is a poster, not a warranty. Rina Kecil Living highlighted the screenshot-and-keep-chat-logs advice as the same folder she keeps as a creator to prove ownership when apps and brands use her before/after photos without credit or pay.

nodes.name: MalaysiaRenoKaki admins
nodes.summary: The MalaysiaRenoKaki admins posted a total-landed-cost PSA on 2026-11-04 warning members to check delivery dates against their own postcode (Georgetown 10200, Penang mainland, Sabah, Sarawak) because lead times differ and "2-4 hari" can become 12. The PSA advises checking total landed cost — unit + delivery + installation + warranty (original vs parallel import) + trade-in — and screenshotting every promised date and keeping chat logs. The admins state the group stays neutral in disputes and handles them via moderator mediation and fact-checking, with no politics, race, religion, or unverified personal attacks. The trusted contractor list is updated monthly based on member feedback, and live Q&A with industry experts runs every month, 8-11 PM peak, all weekend long.

nodes.name: BUDGET ROOM MAKEOVER
nodes.summary: BUDGET ROOM MAKEOVER is a series on rental-friendly room makeovers under RM500. Amirah Zulkifli, 27, in a first studio unit in Cyberjaya, called it her genre and said the under-RM500 rental-friendly corner is very worth it. Aisyah Rahman, working with a tight RM30k budget for her first condo in Shah Alam, said the series is exactly right for her.

attributes.name: Rina Kecil Living's balcony garden reel

nodes.name: Rina Kecil Living's balcony garden reel
nodes.summary: Rina Kecil Living's balcony garden reel was used by another home app without credit. Rina Kecil Living keeps a folder of screenshots as evidence and characterized the reuse as theft of labor rather than flattery, urging creators to document everything and apps to credit creators, since crediting takes 5 seconds and fair pay is not a favor.

nodes.name: Muar-made sofa
nodes.summary: Muar-made sofas are produced in Muar and sold direct from the Vista Sofa Factory Outlet. The outlet does not claim the absolute cheapest sticker price and instead asks buyers to compare the real number: total cost, correct dimensions, visible materials, delivery days, and after-sales. Buyers are invited to sit on the samples before buying and to WhatsApp for a quote. Rumah Bajet MY endorsed the outlet's breakdown, calling a Muar-made sofa you can sit on and talk to better than a mystery-box lookalike.

nodes.name: Sri Mutiara Home Centre
nodes.summary: Sri Mutiara Home Centre is a family-owned furniture store and Johor Bahru showroom operating since 2005, open 10am–8pm and located just across the Causeway from Singapore. Its offer includes living room sets, dining tables, bedroom furniture and home decor, with delivery and assembly services and quotes that include the total cost upfront (unit price + delivery + assembly). The store requires evidence that a lead is real before committing to any pay-per-lead model, having previously been disappointed by lead providers' lack of proof of authenticity, and it backs clearly labelled paid Partner slots (marked as iklan) and a "Best offer" badge based on total cost, seller trust and after-sales service rather than paid placement. It welcomes the portal's local-first matching and leads inbox, and markets to Singaporean shoppers with exclusive weekend deals.

nodes.name: Bintang Elektrik
nodes.summary: Bintang Elektrik is a local merchant thanked by the Sabah Sarawak Home Group admin in a post addressing East Malaysia buyers. The group's guidance holds that big-ticket electrical and gas purchases should be bought locally where warranty and installation are handled by the same shop, so there is someone to call if the unit leaks or fails, and that "total sampai pasang" must be quoted ikut poskod including import tax and real delivery days rather than a peninsula rate.

attributes.focus_area: East Malaysia home buying and total landed cost
attributes.name: Sabah Sarawak Home Group

nodes.name: Sabah Sarawak Home Group
nodes.summary: Sabah Sarawak Home Group is a Reddit community for homeowners and renovators in Sabah and Sarawak, admin-run with a firm "check local first" stance, the house motto "logistics is real", and repeated "East Malaysia represent" messaging. Its pinned WEEKEND CHECK-IN post tells members to get local East Malaysian quotes and compare TOTAL landed cost (unit + shipping to the member's postcode + installation + warranty), warning that a KL warehouse's "2-4 day" delivery routinely becomes 1-2 weeks crossing the South China Sea for KK, Kuching, Sandakan, Sibu, Tawau, Miri and rural postcodes; it also asks for warranty serviced by a reachable local authorised centre, evidence-documented contractor warnings (invoices, dates, photos, messages) with unverified accusations removed and no politics, race, religion or personal attacks, and group-buy interest to cut shipping.

attributes.name: total cost until installed and tested

nodes.name: total cost until installed and tested
nodes.summary: Bintang Elektrik advises customers to always ask for the total cost until installed and tested, not the sticker price. It states that a "Best offer" genuinely including delivery, installation and import charges is the only fair comparison, and that buyers should confirm in writing the full model code, that standard installation (piping, brackets, vacuum, breaker, labour) is included, and the warranty terms — local authorised versus parallel import, and whether parts, compressor and labour are all covered.

nodes.name: Hannah Lau
nodes.summary: Hannah Lau is 24 years old and lives in Subang Jaya, in Peninsular Malaysia. She saves room tours on TikTok (including hundreds of them) and scans furniture from room tours for fun, but has never clicked buy. Her stated interests center on aesthetic, handmade and sustainable pieces, and she treats the difference between sticker price and total landed cost as her recurring pitfall while browsing toward "one day" buying. She asks for honest delivery days, retention terms stated before upload, and the "delete first, then decide" rule: if retention is unclear she uploads no photo, and she treats her room photo as not free data. She keeps a 500+ video room-tour folder and saves checklists into a "dream home" folder.

attributes.name: Hannah Lau's saved room tour folder

nodes.name: Hannah Lau's saved room tour folder
nodes.summary: Hannah Lau's saved room tour folder holds 500+ saved room tour videos, and she said the checklist in the thread rose to the top of it. She browses and never buys, and found points 1 and 4 (full model code on indoor and outdoor stickers, and black-and-white warranty covering parts, compressor and labour) the most relevant, calling total landed cost always the trap and stating that her room photo is not free data.

nodes.name: affiliate disclosure
nodes.summary: Affiliate disclosure rules across these discussions converge on labelling paid links and Partner slots before the click, not after or buried in a bio. Justin Ling's checklist requires the affiliate label to be shown before he clicks, and he asks whether the delete button actually deletes rather than hides and whether apps request unneeded permissions. Rumah Bajet MY holds that a paid Partner slot must be labelled "iklan" before the click, alongside total landed pricing and check-local-first. Nadia Home Diary committed to labelling every link or recommendation honestly as "Link affiliate — aku dapat komisen kecil, tapi aku dah guna & percaya barang ni" before the click, outside the bio, tied to #AffiliateDisclosure and #NadiaHomeDiary. Dr.

nodes.name: local after-sales
nodes.summary: Vista Sofa Factory Outlet offers local after-sales as part of its direct factory offer, and Rina Kecil Living describes honest materials plus local after-sales as real value. Lim Wei Jie requires after-sales service coverage in the Seremban/Nilai area for a built-in oven and gas stove, and Wong Kar Fai advises getting the service centre's number in writing.

nodes.name: Wong Kar Fai
nodes.summary: Wong Kar Fai is a Penang-based buyer. He endorsed Rumah Lengkap Marketing's "Ringgit dan Reach" note on a new home-furnishing portal, framing the portal trial's core question "Berapa kos per lead?" as the same question he asks sellers: "What is the total price?" From a Penang buyer's notebook he added that the Penang test client should be split island versus mainland, since Georgetown 10200 and Seberang Perai are different delivery and installation lanes; that quotes must state the warranty path (original import or parallel) and who services it locally, not just delivery and install fees; and that a failed trial must be published with no hiding of bad results. He proposed a tenth listing-hygiene point: warranty path written, with local service centre, and delivery zones and per-item installation rates stated for Penang. His pre-payment notebook records the model number, quote, promised date and salesperson's name.

nodes.name: commission labelling
nodes.summary: Priya Nair asked that commission be labelled on every link before the click, and Jason Reno Journal said buyers should know where a listed piece appears and who earns the commission on it.

nodes.name: Rumah Ideas
nodes.summary: Rumah Ideas is a source of home ideas that Sarah Thevi keeps a folder of screenshots for. Sarah Thevi asked, regarding gas appliances, whether the warranty states who services them in the Klang area rather than just Seremban, and whether the app or store recognises cut-out dimensions when a spec sheet photo is snapped or whether they must still be typed manually.

nodes.name: renovation
nodes.summary: Azlan Musa saves items for months for his renovation, and stable, honest pricing matters to him for that purpose.

nodes.name: Kucing Milo
nodes.summary: Kucing Milo appears as a hashtag (#KucingMilo) in Priya Nair's post about testing a furniture app in guest mode before signing in. The post covers checking permissions (declining location access), language settings (only English and Malay, with feedback sent requesting Tamil), and privacy controls (ensuring scan history can be deleted), and is tagged #RentalLife #PrivacyMatters #PetalingJaya #SmallSpaceLiving #KucingMilo.

nodes.name: Midea rice cooker
nodes.summary: Kevin Lim has a 1.8L Midea rice cooker sitting in his online cart since the previous month, alongside a 1.8L Xiaomi rice cooker, awaiting the 6.6 sale to see which one drops to a lower total price. He confirmed the seller rating, delivery days, and warranty for the items before deciding.

nodes.name: Rimbun Rattan Crafts workshop
nodes.summary: Rimbun Rattan Crafts is a rattan craft business based in Melaka, run by a team that signs off as The Rimbun Team. Its handmade products include sofas and rattan baskets, each woven by hand and never identical to mould-made pieces; the workshop invites customers to visit in Melaka. Commenting under Vista Sofa Factory Outlet's post about checking frame wood, foam density, fabric and stitching, and delivery and warranty before buying a lookalike sofa online, Rimbun Rattan Crafts agreed with the advice and asked whether handmade goods can truly be matched by 'similarity search', urging support for local traders and handcraft.

nodes.name: local-first matching
nodes.summary: Rosli Ahmad, a small-business owner (motorcycle workshop) and online buyer in Kangar, Perlis, supports verified listings plus local-first matching if they force sellers to state delivery realities such as "Perlis, add 2-3 days" upfront before checkout, since logistics outside the Klang Valley are real rather than an excuse.

nodes.name: warranty in writing
nodes.summary: Warranty in writing, covering parts and labour on a local unit, is one of the checklist points Kamala Devi, a 58-year-old homemaker in Taiping, Perak, holds on to.

nodes.name: group buys
nodes.summary: Group buys are proposed as a way to cut shipping costs for homeowners and renovators in Sabah and Sarawak. The Sabah Sarawak Home Group admin team asks members to post group-buy interest alongside before-and-after photos and supplier recommendations so shipping costs can be cut together. Sabah Sarawak Home Group advises pooling orders with neighbours in the same area and negotiating a single bulk shipment, which it says slashes the per-unit logistics cost.

nodes.name: Miri
nodes.summary: Miri is a city in Sarawak, East Malaysia, with postcode 98xxx, where Joanne Sia lives as a homeowner. Joanne asks sellers for the total landed cost to Miri — shipping to Sarawak plus import tax plus installation, written down — because the total changes once an item crosses to East Malaysia, and she asks whether Casella's tag shows delivery days by postcode for Sarawak or only "nationwide." She stresses confirming that delivery and installation are actually included, since Sarawak logistics can quietly change the real price, and she wants real landed totals to Sarawak shared for comparison; she checks the app nightly because the listing price is never the real price. A pendant light Joanne ordered arrived cracked from poor packaging, so she now asks sellers for extra protection before shipping to Sarawak, and she is open to group buys with Miri neighbours to split shipping. Sellers who reply with real measurements, cut-out sizes and honest postage earn her support.

nodes.name: 92% match score
nodes.summary: The "92% match" score is a similarity score, not a model code, and is decoration until the tool publishes per-category precision, how the labelled test set was built, and the false-match rate between near-identical units such as 1.0HP versus 1.5HP AC or the same sofa in a different fabric code. Dr. Salina Rahmat argued a photo cannot read a model code and a confident wrong match costs more than no match. Ah Boon Fix It, a Casella beta tester, backed this, citing his own on-camera failures where a kitchen photo suggested a cabinet that did not fit and a sofa match that did not fit.

nodes.name: Ninja Van
nodes.summary: Ninja Van is a courier whose name is used in fake delivery-notice scams sent by WhatsApp and SMS. Thinesh Kumar identified ninjavan.co as the official domain, warning that scam links use lookalike or shortened domains instead. Real couriers such as Ninja Van never ask for OTP or card details through a link to release a parcel.

nodes.name: Penang shops
nodes.summary: Penang shops are part of Wong Kar Fai's price comparison process for furniture and appliances: he checks Shopee, Lazada, Mudah, and the Penang shops before believing any offer. In a later post he added Shopee, Lazada, Courts, SenQ, and smaller Penang shops as the places to check before trusting a sticker price, saying a photo cannot tell model number, warranty terms, or whether delivery and installation are included. He also asks whether a local shop listing shows total cost including delivery and installation and whether he can see the actual unit before deciding, noting that if not, he still goes to the shop and asks.

nodes.name: Kamala Devi
nodes.summary: Kamala Devi is a 58-year-old homemaker in Taiping, Perak, a Tamil speaker comfortable in English who is not good with technology and was cheated once online, so she is very careful. Her son mentioned the Casella app to her; she will try it only when he visits next month to show her, and only if it is easy to understand — she will not try it alone and will not buy alone. She insists the price be the full total (unit + delivery + installation + tax, plus piping and brackets) with no hidden fees, and that before upload the company state plainly where room photos go, how long they are kept, and that delete truly deletes, testing delete properly before collecting photos. Her late husband said to get everything in writing, with parts, compressor and labour listed separately; she also holds to warranty in writing, local unit, trained installer and safety first for gas. Her stated motto is "Better safe than sorry."

nodes.name: commission disclosure
nodes.summary: Dr. Salina Rahmat researches commission disclosure and trust in Malaysia. Her position is that disclosure is a relationship, not a disclaimer: buyers should ask who paid for a recommendation and whether they would still trust it if they knew. Commission is legitimate but hidden commission is not; a plain label before the click, not buried in a hashtag or bio, keeps trust intact. The stance is not anti-creator but anti-ambiguity, and Malaysian brands were urged to test better disclosure before claiming it kills conversion. Her Klang Valley interviews found the same practice works for both hidden costs and hidden commissions: screenshot the promised price and ask who pays whom. She applies the standard to platforms as well as sellers, supporting creator credit and compensation when images are used for listings, demos or AI training, a clear retention period and a real permanent delete stated before upload in plain language, and commission disclosed on every link before the click.

nodes.name: poskod-based delivery
nodes.summary: Poskod-based delivery means delivery days and totals quoted by postcode rather than a "nationwide delivery" slogan. Farah Zainal, a KK homeowner, asked whether Casella's total landed cost really covers Sabah/Sarawak or is a Klang Valley number with nationwide delivery slapped on, citing a West Malaysian curtain order where shipping cost more than the curtains. She said Pantai Timur and Perlis also need to "ikut poskod", that 2-4 days becoming day 12 is a disclosure failure, and that "nationwide delivery" is a slogan, not a number.

nodes.name: published benchmark methodology
nodes.summary: Grace Chin demands a published benchmark methodology from the vendor: define the metric (top-1 category accuracy versus retrieval precision@1 on the exact model code), state how the labelled test set was built (who labelled it, how many classes, whether near-identical units were included), and publish the false-match rate per category plus the failure set, not just the failure rate. Grace cited a 2019 case where a "beats Google Lens" claim collapsed once the test set turned out to be weighted toward the vendor's own training data, and said test-set construction is the first thing Grace inspects.

nodes.name: Balik Pulau
nodes.summary: Balik Pulau is a Penang location that Wong Kar Fai cited alongside Georgetown 10200 and Butterworth as distinct delivery lanes, noting that some KL sellers quote a flat shipping rate and then ask for a top-up at the doorstep.

nodes.name: Kaki
nodes.summary: Kaki is a Reddit community where members discuss consumer-protection concerns around the Casella app, including affiliate disclosure, total landed cost, and photo-tagging accuracy. Nadia Home Diary thanked Kaki for the honest talk.

nodes.name: sofa specifications
nodes.summary: Hafiz Ismail lists the sofa specs to ask for after total cost: seat height, seat depth, cushion density, frame material, whether the cover is removable, and warranty length.

nodes.name: small space living
nodes.summary: #smallspaceliving appears in Amirah Zulkifli's November 4, 2026 post about Unit 12-3, where the bed, wardrobe, compact sofa, and study desk had not yet been bought; the post asked for rental-friendly fixes that did not cost RM4k, with real reviews and prices only. On the same day, Rina Kecil Living used #smallspaceliving in a post about her 600 sq ft rental, where the real cost of any item is unit price plus delivery to her postcode, installation, warranty, and whether it fits, alongside #TotalLandedCost and #CreditCreators; she also framed the total landed cost of creators' work as permission, credit, and fair pay, and signed off "Small space, big standards." Rina Kecil Living separately cited Jason Reno Journal's post on total landed cost, endorsing labelled affiliate links and #CreditCreators.

nodes.name: Sabah Sarawak Home Group
nodes.summary: Sabah Sarawak Home Group is a Facebook group on renovating in East Malaysia, run by an admin team. Its "WEEKEND CHECK-IN — East Malaysia represent!" post advises checking local suppliers first and comparing total landed cost (unit price + shipping to one's own postcode + installation + warranty coverage), noting that KL warehouse "2-4 day" deliveries routinely become 1-2 weeks once they cross the South China Sea, covering KK (88xxx), Kuching (93xxx), Sandakan (90xxx), Sibu (96xxx), Tawau (91xxx), Miri (98xxx) and rural postcodes. Contractor warnings require documentation — invoices, dates, photos and messages — with unverified accusations removed, and members are invited to post before-and-after photos, supplier recommendations and group-buy interest to cut shipping costs.

nodes.name: Tamil
nodes.summary: Tamil was not offered as a language in the Casella app, which offered only English and Malay. Priya Nair and many others sent feedback asking for Tamil to be added. Priya Nair repeated this in November 2026, saying the app still offered only English and Malay and that many people had submitted feedback requesting Tamil, arguing that a platform wanting the community's rooms should carry its languages.

nodes.name: Total Landed Cost method
nodes.summary: The Total Landed Cost method is a checklist promoted in the Malaysia Reno Kaki community for evaluating purchases, especially for Sabah and Sarawak buyers. It comprises: unit price (comparing app/TikTok Shop listings against local kedai hardware, printing both); shipping to the buyer's own postcode (RM40 can become RM180 to KK or Sibu; a KL warehouse's "2-4 hari" routinely becomes 1-2 weeks once it crosses the South China Sea); installation (outstation sellers usually do not cover it, budget RM150–400); and warranty (confirming an authorised service centre the buyer can reach, since 5-year paper covering only Semenanjung counts as zero). Malaysia Reno Kaki pinned the checklist for the weekend and added a group-play of pooling orders: group-buying with 3-5 neighbours in the same area to split freight, with interested members dropping "GB" plus their area (KK, Kuching, Sibu, Miri, Tawau) for mods to connect them.

nodes.name: Explore feed of tagged rooms
nodes.summary: An Explore feed of tagged rooms is planned for the next phase and is not available at beta.

nodes.name: Lim Wei Jie's cabinet
nodes.summary: Lim Wei Jie, a Seremban homeowner renovating his home, had a contractor build a cabinet without checking his appliance dimensions; the mismatch cost him far more than any "saving". He cited this as the reason listings must publish full model codes and cut-out/clearance dimensions (W x D x H).

nodes.name: tagged view
nodes.summary: The tagged view gives each item a dot and a label such as "Sofa, from RM1,299". Uncertain items show a hollow dot labelled "Similar items". A tray lists items with category filters.

nodes.name: East Malaysia
nodes.summary: East Malaysia (Sabah and Sarawak) is treated across Malaysian home-renovation and home-decor communities as a distinct logistics, pricing and coverage problem from Peninsular Malaysia. Recurring guidance from Malaysia Reno Kaki, Budget Reno Bro, Rumah Bajet MY, Sabah Sarawak Home Group, Sinar Home Marketplace, Bintang Elektrik, Kuching Home Appliance Centre and others directs buyers to compare TOTAL landed cost — unit price + shipping to their own postcode + installation + import/tax + warranty coverage — not sticker price. Lead times differ for Georgetown 10200, Penang mainland, Sabah and Sarawak: a KL warehouse "2-4 hari" routinely becomes 1-2 weeks once it crosses the South China Sea, and rural postcodes add days. Named differing-rate areas include KK, Kuching, Sandakan, Sibu, Tawau, Miri and Igan.

nodes.name: comment 154
nodes.summary: Comment 154, alongside comment 42, raised privacy questions about a scan-and-link app: how long room photos are stored, whether they are used for training, and whether deletion is truly permanent. Grace Chin cited both comments as the same coin's two sides and said that until these points are written clearly, not a single photo should be uploaded, endorsing the instinct to delete first and decide later.

nodes.name: Japandi inspiration
nodes.summary: Japandi inspiration is the design style Amirah Zulkifli has been scanning for weeks. A cozy reading corner with a rattan chair, linen curtain and warm lamp came up over RM4,000, and a small kitchen with a quartz top was out of budget before she started. Amirah's conclusion is that inspiration is free but execution is not.

nodes.name: Farah Zainal's room
nodes.summary: Farah Zainal's room is the basis of her objection that her photos are not free data: she wants credit and consent for creators and a real permanent delete rather than hidden retention. She cited the app mislabelling a teak mandir cabinet as "wooden cabinet" and a kolam rug as "bohemian rug" as erasure rather than a match.

nodes.name: Taiping
nodes.summary: Kamala Devi is a 58-year-old homemaker in Taiping, Perak, who describes herself as not good with technology and as having been cheated once online, so she is very careful. She plans for her son to sit with her before she tries the Casella app, will not try it alone, and will proceed only if it is easy to understand. Her stated concerns are where her room photos go and how long they are kept, and opposition to hidden fees, with the price required to be one full total including delivery, installation and tax; she asked that delivery, piping, brackets or installation costs be stated upfront. She asked for proper testing of the delete function before any photos are collected and for simple wording in plain English or Tamil. She endorses total installed cost rather than sticker price, warranty in writing covering parts and labour for a local unit, and for gas appliances a trained installer with leak test on safety grounds.

nodes.name: Bintang Elektrik
nodes.summary: Bintang Elektrik is an independent, family-run appliance retailer in Seremban, operating since 2015 from a Seremban showroom. Its stated policy is service over price: it competes on professional installation and after-sales service rather than the lowest price, will never publicly criticise a competitor, and will not buy a "Best offer" badge. It advises buyers to verify full model codes (indoor and outdoor stickers for aircond; 1.0HP vs 1.5HP look identical in photos), match capacity to room size, and demand total landed cost through installation and testing — unit plus delivery by postcode, piping, brackets, vacuum, breaker and labour — with warranty in writing covering parts, compressor and labour, local authorised versus parallel import. For gas appliances it promotes trained installers, correct piping and leak tests as safety.

nodes.name: R32 refrigerant
nodes.summary: R32 is an air-conditioning refrigerant gas. Halim Yaakob, an aircond installer in Johor Bahru, cited it as an example of how visually identical 1.5HP units can differ: units that look the same may use different gas (R32 vs R410A), have different capacity, or be another region's model, so a low price can reflect the wrong model rather than a bargain.

nodes.name: teh tarik photo
nodes.summary: Amirah Zulkifli uses a photo of her teh tarik to test an app's deletion function before she dares to scan her actual unit. She lives in Cyberjaya in a small first studio unit, listed as Unit 12-3, and is hunting for a bed, a wardrobe and a compact sofa. She scans, saves, closes the app, then manually checks Shopee and Mr DIY and compares total cost to the home before deciding; one scan app quoted a "compact sofa" at RM899 sticker, which rose past RM1,100 with delivery to her poskod and "installation included *conditions apply*". She wants total landed cost (delivery + installation + import tax) rather than sticker price, and wants to measure before scanning, saying gambar rumah bukan free data and that she would report back if results are realistic. She still wants pasang included for her bed and wardrobe, and finds DIY acceptable for a shelf and bracket.

nodes.name: 3 free scans without an account
nodes.summary: Casella offers 3 free scans without an account. Justin Ling said this earns the app a try, since no forced sign-up already beats 90% of these apps; he would test it with a plant photo first, then delete it, and would leave if a sign-up wall appears after the teaser.

attributes.name: Rina Kecil Living's screenshot evidence folder

nodes.name: Rina Kecil Living's screenshot evidence folder
nodes.summary: Rina Kecil Living keeps a folder of screenshots as evidence documenting uncredited reuse of her content, including another home app's use of her balcony garden reel without credit. In a November 4, 2026 post she reported that another home app had used her balcony garden reel without credit again, calling it theft of labor rather than flattery, urging every creator to document everything and every app to credit creators in seconds, under #CreditCreators and #CreatorRights. She referenced a 2021 incident that made her feel violated and undervalued. After a Reddit thread grew around her case, she locked in three asks for platforms: credit and compensation with explicit consent before her photos are used (listings, demos, AI training), retention periods stated before upload in plain BM and English with a delete that really deletes, and affiliate commission labelled on every link before the click, saying disclosure is a relationship, not a disclaimer.

nodes.name: Muar
nodes.summary: Muar is the base of Vista Sofa Factory Outlet, a sofa maker selling direct from a Muar outlet that invites customers to sit on samples and inspect frame wood (solid kiln-dried vs thin plywood), foam density and firmness, fabric and stitching, and delivery plus warranty; dimensions, seat height, seat depth and door/lift clearance are also raised. Vista Sofa Factory Outlet urges buyers to compare total landed cost (sofa + delivery to postcode + installation + after-sales) rather than sticker price, quotes Sabah/Sarawak honestly by postcode, and in 2026 framed local landed cost as sofa + delivery to poskod + pasang + buang barang lama in one written number, telling customers to skip sellers who cannot give it in writing.

nodes.name: air conditioner installation
nodes.summary: Kuching Home Appliance Centre, a family-owned appliance retailer in Sarawak running a single showroom since 1995, advises that a photo never carries the full model code and that "92% match" is not a model number. Its routine is three checks: full model code on both indoor and outdoor stickers, capacity matched to room size, and total cost sampai pasang dan test covering piping, bracket, vacuum, breaker and labour. For East Malaysia buyers it advises confirming that delivery and installation are included for Sarawak, because logistics there can quietly change the real price, and notes that a cheap install with a voided warranty is the most expensive deal. Balakrishnan Nair likewise asks for total cost through installation and testing and whether using another installer voids the warranty.

nodes.name: affiliate income
nodes.summary: Affiliate income is income earned through links in scan-and-link apps such as Shopee and Taobao links; creators, merchants and consumer advocates in the discussion treat it as legitimate as long as commission is disclosed. Dr. Salina Rahmat requires the label IKLAN in plain BM and English before the click, holds that early disclosure usually holds conversion better, and cites a survey of 120 Klang Valley consumers plus interviews with Klang Valley and East Malaysian buyers. Ah Boon Fix It, a Casella beta tester who reviews gas and electrical appliances, discloses earning affiliate commission on purchases through his links; Nadia Home Diary labels her links before the click and wants credit and consent for a maker's photos; Rina Kecil Living worries that apps profit from her content without crediting her; Jason Reno Journal is sceptical of untested products. Farah Zainal holds that her room photo is not free data and considers disclosure a relationship, not a disclaimer.

nodes.name: measurement hygiene
