nodes.summary: Measurement hygiene is framed as a design skill, not just a marketing one, in a comment on Rumah Lengkap Marketing's nine-point "listing hygiene" checklist. The checklist's measurement-related points require sizes in both cm and inches, exact material specification (MDF, solid rubberwood, or veneer rather than just "kayu"), and delivery times stated by postcode zone, since "3-5 days" is wrong for Kuching. The commenter, an interior designer, said "3–5 days" is wrong for Kuching the way a styled photo is wrong for a Malaysian living room because the aggregate hides the failure mode, and that "kayu tak cukup" is their catchphrase in reverse: touch it first, then spec it. They compared a client showing a viral room and asking to make their house look like it — with no dimensions, material, light direction, or budget line — to a benchmark with hidden test conditions, and said you can't compute cost per qualified lead if you can't attribute it.

nodes.name: Aisyah Rahman's curtains
nodes.summary: Aisyah Rahman's curtains are budgeted at RM150 in her 'Rumah Impian' plan and the decision has been made. Nothing has been purchased yet; she is waiting for the house keys.

nodes.name: Dr. Salina Rahmat
nodes.summary: Dr. Salina Rahmat draws on her own chats with Klang Valley shoppers to identify three things that help people find small workshops: plain, specific tags (cane type, size in cm as L x D x T, seat height, self-collect or delivery, without jargon); proof of the maker such as hands weaving, the kampung, and the story behind the piece, since people trust process over polish; and credit and consent, which she holds as non-negotiable when a platform or reseller uses a creator's images. She asked the Rimbun Team whether, when selling through a scan-and-link app, they know where their listing appears and who earns the commission on it, noting that most small workshops are never told this and that transparency is not just for the big players. She closed with "Selamat maju jaya — real craft deserves to be found."

nodes.name: Taobao foldable table
nodes.summary: Cheah Xin Yi cited a Taobao foldable table as an example of an item whose recognition would require stable 5G, making the model 0% useful on her commute as a KL renter scanning for adhesive shelves and plug-in sconces.

nodes.name: stainless steel thali set
nodes.summary: Sarah Thevi, an Indian-Malaysian consumer from Klang, tested Casella with screenshots from local Indian-Malaysian home pages. A teak mandir cabinet was labelled just "wooden cabinet", a kolam-patterned rug as "bohemian rug", and a stainless steel thali set was placed into a random kitchen category, missing the cultural cues. Sarah asked whether the recognition logic includes Indian-Malaysian items or only English-language Western decor, whether it can distinguish a prayer-room cabinet from a plain wardrobe and a kolam rug from a generic patterned rug, and where room photos go, how long they are kept, whether deletion is permanent, and whether affiliate commission is disclosed on every link. She also raised that Casella supports only English and Malay, while her mother reads Tamil and her grandmother's world is Tamil, and asked whether she could use it as a guest without a phone number.

attributes.name: Rajesh Pillai's terrace house in Klang

nodes.name: Rajesh Pillai's terrace house in Klang
nodes.summary: Rajesh Pillai is renovating the kitchen of his terrace house in Klang; the house is 18 years old and has water damage under the sink. He is based in Klang and compared his renovation situation to that of a Seremban 2 terrace house renovator, noting the shared struggle despite the different postcode. He seeks groups that share real specifications, cut-out dimensions, and after-sales reviews, and asks about installation inclusion, warranty years, physical shop presence, and hidden charges.

nodes.name: Setapak condo
nodes.summary: A condo in Setapak where Cheah Xin Yi rents; no drilling is allowed there.

nodes.name: Melissa Anak Jimbun's wardrobe
nodes.summary: Melissa Anak Jimbun's wardrobe arrived with a chipped corner after crossing the South China Sea in a thin carton. Melissa, a Kuching homeowner, now asks sellers before paying to crate orders (papan plus foam corners) and to send photos of the packed item, a step she considers cheaper than a replacement making the same two-week trip again. On 2026-11-04 she cited her wardrobe's chipped corner, and a Miri buyer's cracked pendant light, as the same packaging problem in East Malaysia shipping. She also received a quote of RM800 just to ship a 3-seater sofa from Taobao to Kuching, before import tax and installation.

nodes.name: wardrobe
nodes.summary: Melissa Anak Jimbun ordered a wardrobe online at a price that looked cheap, but West Malaysia received a much lower rate while Sarawak had to pay more.

nodes.name: Petaling Jaya
nodes.summary: Petaling Jaya is home to Priya Nair, 28, a renter of three years in an old PJ building whose landlord forbids painting or drilling; she buys only small movable items — folding shelves, screw-free stick-on mirrors and clip-on lamps — and large furniture results do not help her. Her cat Milo sits on her foldable side table. She tests guest scans, permissions, languages and privacy controls before signing in, rejects location access, requested Tamil language support from a furniture app, requires that scan history and data be deletable, and screenshots privacy policies. Balakrishnan Nair, 62, also lives in Petaling Jaya; he prefers phone calls to shops and doubts that an app helps with after-sales service. Priya posts under #RentalLife #PrivacyMatters #PetalingJaya #SmallSpaceLiving #TenantRights seeking tenant and small-space living communities.

nodes.name: privacy
nodes.summary: Chua Li Ting's rule for apps and services: no credit, no permission, no deal, and no retention period stated, no upload. Chua Li Ting once uploaded a room photo to a home-organisation app that "scans" your space, then felt uneasy about who sees it, whether it is used for training, and when it is deleted. Chua Li Ting tested the delete button with a plant photo first, deleting before deciding, and applies the same rule as an appliance spec table: if they cannot answer half, walk away.

nodes.name: 30-day test
nodes.summary: The 30-day test is Farah Zainal's draft proposal for evaluating a new home-furnishing portal before it enters a small trader's budget. It involves three volunteer clients (one Klang Valley, one Penang, one Kuching), measures cost per qualified lead against the clients' Facebook and marketplace baselines, has no exclusivity and no upfront payment, and requires a full deletion test before any customer photos are collected. If the test fails, the numbers are published and clients are told to spend elsewhere.

nodes.name: cost per qualified lead
nodes.summary: Malaysia Reno Kaki treats cost per qualified lead — a real WhatsApp contact or a real showroom visit — as the only fair metric for small traders, and if it fails, the numbers should be published and the spend moved elsewhere, under the principle "no proof, no ringgit." The metric is framed as the measurement axis of a proposed bounded 30-day test with a cap and three volunteer clients (one Klang Valley, one Penang, one Kuching), measured against each client's Facebook and marketplace baselines, with no exclusivity and no upfront payment. Sinar Home Marketplace of Puchong, an online-only Shopee-based home goods seller, volunteered as a test client and said cost per qualified lead is the only metric that survives scrutiny, adding that leads must be verified as genuine buyers up front and that commission-earning slots must be labelled iklan before the click.

nodes.name: Ah Boon Fix It
nodes.summary: Ah Boon Fix It is an ex-contractor who fixes and builds things for a living, reviews gas and electrical appliances, and beta-tested Casella. He holds that "92% match" is a similarity score rather than a model code and must be checked, not trusted outright; he has shown his own Casella match failures on camera, including a kitchen photo suggesting a cabinet that did not fit and a sofa match that did not fit, and a cabinet 20cm too wide. His routine: capture the full model code on the indoor and outdoor stickers side by side (1.0HP vs 1.5HP look the same in a photo), size capacity to the room's area rather than the unit's appearance, and compute total cost through installation and testing — unit plus piping, bracket, vacuum, breaker and labour. Without vacuuming, moisture enters, the compressor fails early and warranty becomes a problem; a cheap install with a void warranty is the most expensive deal.

nodes.name: listing hygiene checklist
nodes.summary: Rumah Lengkap Marketing's "listing hygiene" checklist specifies 9 items corrected before any ad or boost spend, with client names removed and the same pattern each time: (1) displayed price vs actual price — full price, or "from" with installation cost explained; (2) size in cm AND inches; (3) exact material (MDF, solid rubberwood, veneer — "kayu" is insufficient); (4) delivery time by postcode/zone, since "3-5 hari" is wrong for Kuching; (5) real stock; (6) three photos — one full shot, one material close-up, one in a real room; (7) FAQs answered in the listing, not in DMs; (8) a single CTA — WhatsApp OR form; (9) a tracker for lead source to calculate cost per qualified lead and compare channels. The audit is done for clients before touching ad budget, and each time cost per lead drops without added spend. The checklist was reshared and endorsed on 2026-11-04 by Syafiq Hamdan, Ah Boon Fix It, Sarah Thevi, and Lau Kok Wai; the closing line is "No proof, no ringgit. Kita kira dulu."

nodes.name: boucle sofa
nodes.summary: Vanessa Goh has seen a viral boucle sofa sag within six months because someone trusted a photo, and cited the case as evidence that cheap things are not always cheap. She also raised the risk that "boucle" fabric pills in Malaysian heat, and argued that a 92% match on the correct SKU can still be a hard no if the sofa is 5cm too deep for a 3.1m wall or the finish does not hold up. She watched a viral lookalike sofa sag in six months where the match was fine but the room was not.

nodes.name: Cheah Xin Yi's Sheet
nodes.summary: Cheah Xin Yi's Sheet is a collection for aircond installation quotes with actual numbers, which she offered to add to after commenting on Faizal Rahim's Shah Alam aircond replacement post. She asked that anyone with a real quote (not "DM for price") share it so she could add it to the Sheet, noting hidden fees for piping, bracket and labour are real when quotes never list them. She advises getting the dealer to confirm in writing whether a third-party installer voids the warranty, since compressor warranty is usually separate from workmanship, and tags such posts #ShahAlam and #RentalFriendly.

nodes.name: Hannah Lau
nodes.summary: Hannah Lau plans to eventually get a small KL apartment and found a shared checklist useful for that purpose, screenshotting it for future reference. Hannah highlighted point 5 as especially important: gas items must be handled by a trained installer with a leak test, which she framed as a safety matter rather than a sales point. Hannah has 500+ saved room tour videos in her folder and said she had not previously thought about where those creators' photos end up; she supports crediting creators, obtaining permission before using their images, deletion that really deletes, and upfront commission labels, and she stated that transparency is not only about price.

nodes.name: Linktree
nodes.summary: Amirah Zulkifli wished the creator good luck with the Linktree.

nodes.name: Nadia Home Diary
nodes.summary: Nadia Home Diary is a Malay-language TikTok home-decor creator based in Shah Alam whose audience is mostly young women and B40 families decorating rentals and condos; she writes in BM and English and signs off with "Jom kita deco!". She has been quietly testing affiliate links in her bio and tracking clicks to prove her influence is genuine rather than "vibes", and refuses to hide commissions: every link gets an "iklan"/"Link affiliate" label before the click, in BM and English, because "disclosure is a relationship, bukan disclaimer." She recommends only items she has used and trusts, asks sellers for dimensions, packaging protection, postcode delivery zones and local service centres, and asks followers to check total landed cost (unit + delivery to their postcode + installation + import tax + warranty). She plans a budget room makeover series for B40 families and is building a Linktree/website listing model codes, dimensions and landed prices.

nodes.name: ceiling fan
nodes.summary: A 5-blade ceiling fan with a DC motor was installed in the second bedroom of Azlan Musa's home, completing that room's ceiling fan and wiring work in the 14th month of renovation. The installation took 3 weeks because of waiting for stock. The fan cost RM289, RM20 less than earlier pricing after a sale, and had been saved for since July. Wiring, casing and switch cost RM145, and labour by a certified electrician with SIRIM certification cost RM80, for a total of RM514, within budget. Azlan Musa advises buying fans or air conditioners through certified installers to keep the warranty valid, especially for the compressor or valve, and getting written quotes covering piping, bracket and labour to avoid hidden fees.

nodes.name: Rajesh Pillai's fridge
nodes.summary: Rajesh Pillai paid RM350 extra to install a fridge he bought online. A recent quote he received hid a RM600 delivery charge until the last minute.

nodes.name: SSM number
nodes.summary: Balakrishnan Nair advises verifying a seller's credentials before any purchase, especially gas appliances, by asking for the SSM number and the trained installer's name in writing; an unlicensed seller means no leak test and no liability.

nodes.name: Penang
nodes.summary: Penang is one of three locations for a proposed 30-day test of a new home-furnishing portal, alongside one Klang Valley client and one Kuching client, as set out in Rumah Lengkap Marketing's draft. The test measures cost per qualified lead against Facebook and marketplace baselines, with no exclusivity, no upfront payment, and a full ablation test before any customer photos are collected; Rumah Lengkap Marketing states the draft remains one unchanged, that a portal with zero users, zero traction and zero measured match accuracy cannot show cost per qualified lead, and that a failed test will have its numbers published. Grace Chin cited this draft on 2026-11-04, comparing it to computer-vision benchmarking.

nodes.name: import tax
nodes.summary: Import tax, along with SST, installation and after-sales, must appear in the same line items as the total landed cost rather than being revealed at checkout. Farah Zainal required this for Sabah/Sarawak buyers, and Ah Boon Fix It defined total landed cost as unit + delivery + installation + import tax + after-sales, plus seller trust.

nodes.name: Local stores tab
nodes.summary: The Local stores tab shows local stores that deliver to the user, matched first ahead of other results.

nodes.name: teak mandir
nodes.summary: A teak mandir was mislabelled as a "wooden cabinet" by the app's local recognition, cited by Grace Chin as an example of a benchmark coverage problem rather than a cultural bug fixable with goodwill.

nodes.name: Nadia's home decor line
nodes.summary: Nadia's home decor line is a future goal Nadia shared in a post: one day she wants to have her own home decor line. She feels it is far off, but the dream is what gets her up in the morning. For now she is taking small steps first, including continuing her budget makeover series for B40 families, tidying her page/Linktree for all her recommendations, and being careful in choosing brands to collaborate with — ones that are honest and transparent. She sometimes feels insecure and fears people will say she has become 'commercial', but reminds herself that if she sincerely helps people, that won't be lost; what matters is being honest, affordable, and community-focused.

nodes.name: hand-woven side table
nodes.summary: A hand-woven side table is a rattan piece that adds warmth to a room, weighs little to shift when moving, and requires no nails in a landlord's wall, making it suited to renters who cannot drill or paint.

nodes.name: Zarina Yusof
nodes.summary: Zarina Yusof is 41 and lives in Kota Bharu, Kelantan (postcode 15200), where few stores deliver. Her recurring first question about any offer is whether it can actually be delivered to Kota Bharu; if it cannot be shipped there, price is irrelevant. She is replacing a rusting gas stove in her kitchen and seeks a seller who delivers to 15200, along with transit days, extra Kelantan charges, installation, and a locally claimable warranty, keeping screenshots of each store's delivery policy before buying. Her mandatory three questions to sellers are whether they deliver to 15200, how many days it takes and whether there is an additional Kelantan charge, and whether installation and warranty can be handled locally.

nodes.name: Kuantan
nodes.summary: Kuantan is the home city of Azlan Musa, a 44-year-old teacher renovating his terrace house stage by stage over two years; he saved a mattress at Tilam Selesa Bedding and found the price had risen by the time he returned to buy, so he asks how long a tagged price stays valid. Tilam Selesa Bedding is a small family mattress retailer in Kuantan operating since 2010, selling mattresses, bed frames and bedding accessories, inviting customers to try beds at its showroom, and asking customers who photograph mattresses in-store whether they are comparing online prices or showing family before buying. On 4 November 2026, Tilam Selesa Bedding posted a night-time message greeting Kuantan, framing a comfortable mattress as a necessity for good sleep rather than a luxury, offering help choosing a mattress to suit needs and budget, and inviting customers to visit the showroom to lie down and decide for themselves.

nodes.name: affiliate commission disclosure
nodes.summary: Affiliate commission disclosure is a condition Cheah Xin Yi, Jason Reno Journal, Syafiq Hamdan, Chua Li Ting and Farah Zainal set for scan-and-link platforms and seller links: commission must be disclosed on every link, and the disclosure must appear before the click. Farah Zainal of Kota Kinabalu holds that a Paid Partner slot must be labelled IKLAN in plain language before the click, in BM plus English, and that finding out it is an ad after tapping ends trust. Jason Reno Journal, a consumer electronics trainer before going full-time on reviews, states affiliate commission on Shopee and Taobao links is acceptable only if labelled clearly on every link before the click in BM plus English; disclosure is not a disclaimer, and he turned down a RM10,000 affiliate deal for an untested product.

nodes.name: Casella
nodes.summary: Casella is a home-design app whose load-bearing claim is a "92% match" between a room photo and the correct SKU, a figure critics call unmeasured; no forced sign-up is offered for three scans, which Justin Ling said earns Casella one attempt from him. Farah Zainal and Justin Ling said Casella should be recommended only if it recognises local Malaysian homes and styles — teak mandir cabinets and kolam rugs, not generic "wooden cabinet" or "bohemian rug" — and protects photos with credit, consent and real permanent delete. Demands include per-class accuracy benchmarks, a plain BM/English privacy policy, "iklan" disclosure before any Paid Partner click, and postcode-specific landed totals for Sarawak such as Sibu and Kuching, where "total landed" must combine real postcode shipping, import tax and installation in the same line items.

nodes.name: NR-BX418VS
nodes.summary: NR-BX418VS is a refrigerator model code used as the standard illustration of photo-matching limits in Malaysian appliance retail. Sim Kok Leong, a 53-year-old ex-appliance technician in Muar, cites NR-BX418VS and a lookalike NR-BX418XSB as near-identical in a photo but not the same unit, since an app tag cannot read the sticker on the unit and so cannot confirm the model. Bintang Elektrik, a Seremban retailer since 2015, likewise uses the pair to show a photo cannot tell an NR-BX418VS from a lookalike, or a 1.0HP from a 1.5HP aircond. Grace Chin repeatedly cites NR-BX418VS versus its lookalike alongside 1.0HP versus 1.5HP airconds as near-identical units that any match benchmark's labelled test set and false-match rate must address. Justin Ling of Sibu also cites the pair, arguing "92% match" cannot be treated as fact until the false-match rate between near-identical units is published.

nodes.name: 30-day protocol
nodes.summary: Malaysia Reno Kaki endorsed a 30-day protocol with a cap, three volunteer clients, and a full blackout test before customer photos are collected, stating it would monitor and update members when results arrive. It added that cost per qualified lead (real WhatsApp contacts, real showroom visits) is the only fair metric, and that failing sellers should publish the numbers and spend elsewhere. Rumah Bajet MY backed the protocol 100% and asked that cost per qualified lead be broken out by postcode/state, since Kuching or Kangar leads differ from Klang Valley leads once shipping and delivery days are counted, and that the full deletion test be a precondition before any home photos are collected, with the delete screenshotted. Dr. Salina Rahmat proposed three additions: time the disclosure and measure cost per qualified lead both before and after the click, publish the failure as promised, and keep the full deletion test as a precondition.

nodes.name: the app
nodes.summary: The app supports sign-in with Google, Apple, phone OTP or email. It is available in English, Chinese and Bahasa Melayu. Users can download or delete their data and delete their account, and uploaded photos expire automatically.

nodes.name: Instagram
nodes.summary: Instagram is the platform on which small-space creator Rina Kecil Living publishes content; Rina Kecil Living worries that apps profit from her content without crediting her. Aisyah Rahman typically finds handmade-furniture shops through Instagram using the hashtags #buatanmalaysia and #rotan, alongside word-of-mouth from friends.

nodes.name: CheckPrice
nodes.summary: CheckPrice is a hashtag used in Malaysian renovation and home-decor discussions on Twitter. Nadia Home Diary endorsed #CheckPrice while stressing that recommenders must protect the people who trust them, including screenshotting delivery promises, checking total landed cost, disclosing affiliate commissions, and recommending only products actually used. Aisyah Rahman used #CheckPrice in a comment on Lim Wei Jie's Seremban 2 kitchen renovation request, adding cooker hood and gas hob suction rates (m³/j), gas type, and certified installation by Suruhanjaya Tenaga personnel to her checklist. Joanne Sia's pinned weekend round-up urged checking price via total landed cost and praised spec-first sellers, and Cheah Xin Yi commented that "the listing price is never the real price" should be printed on every Shopee listing, adding #CheckPrice and #TotalLandedCost.

nodes.name: East Malaysian creators
nodes.summary: East Malaysian creators are supported by Malaysia Reno Kaki, which stated on 2026-11-04 that its coverage is not just West Malaysia-centric and that it is supporting these creators. The support was announced alongside Malaysia Reno Kaki's public-beta guide to the Casella app, in which members were asked to share genuine experiences and tag the community.

nodes.name: Grace Chin
nodes.summary: Grace Chin mentors several startups and identifies as the loudest skeptic of claims that "we beat Google Lens," while not being anti-startup. She rejects the leap from a niche result to a general one without evidence: general image search rests on Google's billions of labeled images, years of refinement, and infrastructure most cannot touch, a near-insurmountable lead, whereas niche domains such as retail inventory, industrial defect detection, medical imaging, and fashion can be beaten outright by a small, well-curated, well-labeled dataset — narrow beats broad. She asks builders to state the domain, the test set, and the baseline, and to publish the slice where they fail, so the number speaks instead of marketing: evidence-based or it's marketing, show the benchmark.

nodes.name: phone OTP
nodes.summary: Phone OTP is one of the sign-in options for the app, alongside Google, Apple and email.

nodes.name: Nadia Home Diary's affiliate links
nodes.summary: Nadia Home Diary is a home decor creator in Shah Alam whose audience is mostly young women and B40 families decorating rental homes. She has been quietly testing affiliate links in her bio and refuses to hide them, holding that disclosure is a relationship, not a disclaimer; transparent affiliate labels should come before the click, in BM and English. She extends the same standard to data: if a model is trained on creators' before/after photos and room tours without consent, credit or compensation, then accuracy on borrowed data is still borrowed, and the consent/credit/compensation share should be published right beside precision and recall. She holds that the metric that matters is precision@1 on the exact model code (e.g. 1.0HP vs 1.5HP, NR-BX418VS vs lookalike), not a generic "92% match", and that per-region rows are needed for Kuching, Sibu, Kangar, Kota Bharu and her own Klang Valley renters.

nodes.name: home-organisation app
nodes.summary: Chua Li Ting has been weighing a home-organisation app that scans room photos, wanting a straight answer on how long the photos are kept and whether deletion is permanent. She tested the app's delete button with a dummy photo of her plant first, and the deletion worked, but the FAQ never stated the retention period. She asked for honest reviews from ordinary users, not affiliate links, on whether anyone had actually checked the seller and whether the privacy note explained storage length. She applies the same rule to such apps: what data is collected, how long it is kept, and whether it can be deleted after upload; "no retention period stated, no upload."

nodes.name: Dr. Salina Rahmat
nodes.summary: Dr. Salina Rahmat commented on Rumah Lengkap Marketing's "listing hygiene" checklist of 9 items to fix before spending on ads or boost, calling it disclosure practice in disguise. She highlighted point 1 on pricing ethics (show the real number or explain the gap) and likened points 4 (delivery by postcode) and 5 (real stock) to a "sponsored-but-not-labelled" review, where the buyer only discovers the truth after committing. From her Klang Valley consumer interviews, appliance shopper Rajesh Pillai learned to ask for the out-the-door number and safety-conscious Haslinda Omar always asks who installs. She advised her students and house sellers to add a line to listing hygiene: if any recommendation or placement is paid, the label goes before the click, not in the fine print, since disclosure is a relationship, not a disclaimer. She closed with "No proof, no ringgit" and the hashtags #CommissionDisclosure and #ConsumerTrust.

nodes.name: screen recordings up to 60 seconds
nodes.summary: Screen recordings up to 60 seconds are planned for the next phase and are not available at beta.

nodes.name: Seremban 2 terrace house kitchen renovation
nodes.summary: Lim Wei Jie is renovating the kitchen of a terrace house in Seremban 2 and is selecting a built-in oven and gas stove. His fixed criteria, posted on 2026-11-04, require full dimensions (W x D x H in mm) and cut-out dimensions, warranty length and exactly what it covers, installation included in the price by a qualified installer with proper gas fitting (non-negotiable for safety), and after-sales service coverage in the Seremban/Nilai area. He stated that price-only replies are not useful and that he compares specs, dimensions and after-sales service before buying: "No dimensions, no trust. Show me the dimensions and the warranty, then we talk." He later asked the renovation crowd for actual models, dimensions, and installer and after-sales experiences, valuing those over discount codes. Malaysia Reno Kaki pinned his post as an example of how to request a quote, citing his four-point spec-first template and noting a Kaki in Seremban 2 doing a kitchen reno.

nodes.name: Google Sheet
nodes.summary: Syafiq Hamdan uses a Google Sheet to track home project purchases one item at a time, recording item, shop, price, shipping, voucher, total, and delivery days before deciding to buy. He applies the same discipline to sellers, skipping any seller who cannot show total price, delivery days and warranty before the buy click, and checking Shopee first rather than trusting match badges. Cheah Xin Yi keeps a Google Sheet recording price, review count, and whether the poster replied in comments.

nodes.name: karpet gulung
nodes.summary: Priya Nair chose a karpet gulung as one of the small, movable items for a rental where the landlord does not allow drilling or painting; it can be rolled up and taken along when moving.

nodes.name: Tilam Selesa Bedding
nodes.summary: Tilam Selesa Bedding is a family-run mattress and bedding shop in Kuantan that has served the city for more than a decade (operating since 2010), selling mattresses, bed frames and bedding accessories from a showroom open daily where customers can lie on and try mattresses before deciding; staff describe it as no-pressure, friendly service at comfortable prices. Its position is that comfort cannot be judged from a photo or a "92% match" — a scan app is a starting point, not the final word, and mattresses are like shoes, with firmness, foam density and spring quality only showing when you lie down. It backs paid Partner slots only if clearly labelled as iklan and backs comparing total landed cost (unit + delivery + installation + import tax + warranty) over sticker price, adding that if an app's landed total is within 10-15% of the shop price, buyers should buy local.

nodes.name: viral air fryer
nodes.summary: Cheah Xin Yi bought a viral air fryer in 2022, after spending two nights in the comments comparing Shopee and Lazada links and finding a lower price with a stackable voucher; the affiliate code in the top comment was expired, however, and shipping ballooned from a promised 3 or 2-4 days to 11 days. Cheah Xin Yi's rules before clicking any link are: dimensions (W x D x H in mm) in writing rather than just a photo, total landed cost of unit plus postage to the buyer's own postcode plus installation plus who services the warranty locally, and screenshots of every promised date and the chat before paying. Cheah Xin Yi does not trust a comment link unless multiple users confirm it, and keeps a Google Sheet for rental-friendly, no-drilling items listing price, review count, and whether the poster replied in comments. Sponsored content should be disclosed; "DM for link" and hidden negative reviews warrant a blacklist.

nodes.name: Causeway
nodes.summary: Muhammad Hazim, based in Johor Bahru, regularly crosses the Causeway and notes that Singapore prices are sometimes cheaper even after transport and exchange rate. He asks whether the app covers both Johor Bahru retailers and the Singapore side, saying an app that shows only one side of the border is of no use to people in Johor.

nodes.name: Casella
nodes.summary: Casella is the scan app under scrutiny in a Reddit thread. Ah Boon Fix It beta-tested Casella and showed the failures on camera: a kitchen photo suggested a cabinet that did not fit, and a sofa match did not fit; Ah Boon Fix It tested the photo deletion feature after Chua Li Ting's concern by uploading, checking where the image went, and testing the delete. Jason Reno Journal, a consumer electronics trainer of five years before going full-time on reviews, asked Casella to show per-class and per-region accuracy, label advertising before the click, and provide a delete function that truly deletes, saying trust would follow only after testing.

nodes.name: XHS CSI group
nodes.summary: Cheah Xin Yi's XHS CSI group is where she would share a published benchmark for photo-to-SKU matching; she asked for the benchmark to be shown before she would share it in the group.

nodes.name: Harvey Norman
nodes.summary: Harvey Norman is one of the Singapore retailers Muhammad Hazim of Johor Bahru compares against Johor Bahru options when shopping for electrical goods, alongside Courts, Gain City, Best Denki, and Mustafa. His comparison method weighs Johor Bahru versus Singapore listings, and he notes Singapore prices are sometimes cheaper even after exchange rate and transport, though warranty logistics usually lead him to buy in Johor Bahru. Wong Kar Fai, buying in Penang, checks Shopee, Lazada, Mudah, Harvey Norman, SenQ, and one neighbourhood shop in his area, comparing unit, delivery, installation, warranty, and trade-in costs.

nodes.name: Kangar
nodes.summary: Kangar, in Perlis (postcode 01000), is home to Rosli Ahmad, 50, a small-business owner who runs a motorcycle workshop (bengkel motor) and also buys online; he posts as a Perlis voice in discussions of the Casella app. Rosli asks that delivery days be shown honestly by postcode, because marketplace delivery to Kangar is slower than in the Klang Valley, and he rejects the standard 2–4 day estimate as unrealistic, saying Kangar is neither overseas nor a KL suburb. He recounts ordering a sprocket set from Shah Alam in February whose listing promised 2–4 working days but which arrived on day 12, with tracking stalled at the Petaling Jaya hub, costing him a customer job; the seller replied that Perlis is usually slower and added a laughing emoji. He wants the merchant phase's verified listings and local-first matching to compel sellers to state “Perlis, add 2-3 days” before checkout, and asks for realistic delivery days for Perlis declared before checkout based on postcode.

nodes.name: Shopee Affiliate
nodes.summary: Shopee Affiliate is an affiliate platform that a home-decor poster asked followers about, seeking tips from anyone who had tried TikTok Shop or Shopee Affiliate.

nodes.name: niche image search
nodes.summary: Niche image search covers domains such as retail inventory, industrial defect detection, medical imaging, and fashion, where a small, well-curated, well-labeled dataset can beat a generalist model outright — narrow beats broad. Grace Chin holds that this niche advantage is real but distinct from general image search, where Google's billions of labeled images, years of refinement, and infrastructure give it a near-insurmountable lead. The mistake she identifies is dressing a niche win in general-search clothing; her ask is to state the domain, the test set, and the baseline, and to publish the slice where the model fails.

nodes.name: Lazada
nodes.summary: Lazada is an online shopping platform in Malaysia. Wong Kar Fai plans to open Lazada (with Shopee and Mudah) and compare total landed costs himself before trusting any Best offer badge; he also names Lazada alongside Shopee, Courts, SenQ and smaller Penang shops when checking the same model after measuring his unit, and in a later note he lists Shopee, Lazada, Mudah, Harvey Norman, SenQ and one neighbourhood shop as the places to compare unit price, delivery, installation, warranty and trade-in. Amirah Zulkifli's routine for furniture pricing is to scan, close the app, open Shopee or Lazada manually, compare the landed total, and only then decide. Rajesh Pillai requires that any Paid Partner slot be clearly labelled as advertising and not quietly sit inside the list.

nodes.name: Casella
nodes.summary: Casella is an app that Ah Boon Fix It tests; the buy button pays Ah Boon Fix It a small commission, which he discloses every time. Ah Boon Fix It states that with apps like Casella the "buy" button drops users into Shopee/Taobao, so the seller, courier and warranty holder become three different people and nobody owns the failure. He also showed his own Casella match failing — a cabinet 20cm too wide — to illustrate that real reviews must show failures.

nodes.name: Best Denki
nodes.summary: Best Denki is one of the Singapore retailers Muhammad Hazim of Johor Bahru compares against Johor Bahru options when shopping for electrical goods, alongside Courts, Harvey Norman, Gain City, and Mustafa. His comparison method weighs Johor Bahru versus Singapore listings, and he notes Singapore prices are sometimes cheaper even after exchange rate and transport, though warranty logistics usually lead him to buy in Johor Bahru.

nodes.name: thali set
nodes.summary: A thali set was mislabelled as a kitchen bin by an app's local recognition, cited by Grace Chin as an example of a benchmark coverage problem rather than a cultural bug fixable with goodwill; the same mislabelling grouped it with "wooden cabinet" for a teak mandir and "bohemian rug" for a kolam-patterned rug. Sarah Thevi uploaded a teak mandir cabinet, a batik cushion, a thali set and a kolam rug to an app and received only generic labels such as "wooden cabinet" and "bohemian rug", and asked whether apps recognise Indian-Malaysian home items, explain their recognition logic, and disclose paid recommendations. Grace Chin argued per-class precision and recall on long-tail regional and cultural classes should be published before any "92% match" claim is quoted as fact.

nodes.name: Kota Bharu
nodes.summary: Kota Bharu (postcode 15200) in Kelantan is where Zarina Yusof, 41, lives; few stores deliver there. Zarina repeatedly asks sellers whether they can ship to Kota Bharu, how many days delivery takes, whether there are extra Kelantan charges, and whether installation and locally claimable warranty are available, stating that if a seller cannot deliver to Kelantan there is no point discussing price and that the East Coast is not a second choice. She requests written confirmation of coverage, delivery days and extra charges by postcode, screenshots each store's delivery policy before buying, treats sellers who answer with promotions instead of delivery questions as a red flag, and collects a list of honest sellers who genuinely deliver to Kota Bharu. She seeks a replacement gas stove for her kitchen in Kota Bharu, whose old stove has rusted at the knob, and wants it settled before raya, prioritising safety and warranty over price.

nodes.name: Vista Sofa Factory Outlet
nodes.summary: Vista Sofa Factory Outlet is a sofa maker and factory outlet in Muar, Johor, selling direct from the outlet and treating Taobao and Shopee as a benchmark rather than an enemy. It builds every sofa itself in Muar, so frame wood, foam density, fabric, stitching and dimensions (including seat height, seat depth and lift/door clearance) vary; its four-point lookalike check covers solid kiln-dried frame wood vs thin plywood, foam density, fabric and stitching, and delivery plus warranty, and it asks buyers to compare five things: unit price (app vs outlet), shipping to the buyer's own postcode, installation, warranty served locally, and materials.

nodes.name: rumahku
nodes.summary: rumahku is a hashtag used by Vanessa Goh alongside #KLinterior in her comment endorsing Rumah Lengkap Marketing's 9-point listing hygiene checklist for Malaysian furniture sellers.

nodes.name: NSRC
nodes.summary: NSRC is the body to which scam victims are directed to report, reachable at 997, according to Thinesh Kumar's guidance on fake courier delivery notices. Victims are also advised to call their bank immediately and screenshot everything for evidence.

nodes.name: Kuching container group-buy
nodes.summary: Melissa Anak Jimbun proposed a group-buy on 4 November 2026 to share a shipping container into Kuching for Sabah and Sarawak renovators. The plan covers bulky items such as tiles, small furniture and kitchen fittings, consolidated at one West Malaysia warehouse and sent in a single shipment to Kuching, with shipping split by weight or volume and each participant receiving their own receipt. Melissa worked out the landed cost for a sofa and asked interested parties to reply, noting enough volume is needed to make the shipment worthwhile. That day she gave the comparison: Taobao RM1,450 plus RM800 shipping with no Sarawak warranty totals RM2,250, versus RM2,680 from a local Kuching supplier delivered, installed and covered by a Sarawak warranty, a RM430 difference; she inspected the warehouse in person and decided for bulky items to buy local, for small items (beadwork, kitchen tools) Taobao still wins, and she will post the full breakdown that week.

nodes.name: CommissionDisclosure
nodes.summary: CommissionDisclosure is a hashtag used by Dr. Salina Rahmat in a comment on Rumah Lengkap Marketing's listing hygiene checklist. Her related point: if any recommendation or placement is paid, the label goes before the click, not in the fine print, because disclosure is a relationship, not a disclaimer.

nodes.name: Bintang Elektrik
nodes.summary: Bintang Elektrik authored a practical checklist for buying electrical appliances that Jason Reno Journal endorsed as the most practical checklist in the thread, adding that its points 1, 2 and 4 were his daily work as a trainer and where customers most often get cheated. The checklist requires the full model code for indoor and outdoor units on the sticker (not "looks the same", since 1.0HP vs 1.5HP and inverter vs non-inverter can look similar in photos), a line-item total through installation and testing (unit + delivery + piping + bracket + vacuum + breaker + labour), and written warranty terms covering parts, compressor and labour, local authorised versus parallel import. Jason Reno Journal added that for Sabah, Sarawak and Kelantan import tax and delivery days by postcode must be added, that third-party installation voiding warranty must be stated before installation, and that gas work requires a trained installer, leak test, and regulator/hose to standard.

nodes.name: Rina Kecil Living
nodes.summary: Rina Kecil Living is an Instagram creator who posts small-space and home-decor content, including a 1.5 sqm reading nook styled with a thrifted rattan chair, lamp and plant, a 600 sq ft rental, and three tiny-apartment hacks under RM50 (command hooks behind the door, stackable thrift baskets, a mirror to double light). In 2021 a home design app used her before/after photos without credit or permission; she only found out when a follower tagged her, and she later found a home app using her balcony garden reel without credit again, keeping a folder of screenshots as evidence. She campaigns under #CreditCreators for creator permission, credit and fair pay, with three asks: credit and compensation with explicit consent before photos are used (listings, demos, AI training), retention periods stated before upload with a delete that verifiably deletes, and affiliate commission labelled on every link before the click.

nodes.name: email
nodes.summary: Email is one of the sign-in options for the app, alongside Google, Apple and phone OTP.

nodes.name: creators' rights
nodes.summary: Rina Kecil Living applies the same "evidence before trust" standard to creators' rights as to appliance purchases: for apps that use your content, no credit, no permission, no deal — document, verify, and ask for the receipts.

nodes.name: Bahasa Melayu
nodes.summary: Bahasa Melayu is one of the app's languages, alongside English and Chinese.

nodes.name: TotalLandedCost
nodes.summary: TotalLandedCost is a hashtag used in Malaysian renovation discussions on Twitter. Joanne Sia's pinned weekend round-up urged checking price the total landed cost way: unit price + shipping to the buyer's postcode + installation + warranty coverage, noting the listing price is not the real number. Cheah Xin Yi commented that "the listing price is never the real price" should be printed on every Shopee listing and that she was adding genuine landed-cost numbers to her sheet, tagging #CheckPrice and #TotalLandedCost.

nodes.name: Kuching local sofa supplier
nodes.summary: A local Kuching sofa supplier quoted RM2,680 for a sofa, delivered and installed, with a shop customers can walk into if anything goes wrong and a warranty that covers Sarawak. Melissa Anak Jimbun compared this against a Taobao sofa at RM2,250 total landed cost and chose the local supplier, a difference of RM430, after driving to the warehouse to inspect the sofa in person. On 4 November 2026 she published her final decision publicly, framing the RM430 as the price of a face she can talk to and a Sarawak-covered warranty, and citing shipping of RM800 on the RM1,450 Taobao unit. The Kuching quote of RM2,680 remained her benchmark when she asked Vista Sofa Factory Outlet of Muar for realistic bulky shipping to a Kuching terrace house postcode and for who services the warranty in Sarawak.

nodes.name: Aisyah Rahman's budget notebook
nodes.summary: Aisyah Rahman's budget notebook holds her room-by-room renovation budget: Ruang Tamu RM10k, Bilik RM8k, Dapur RM5k, Bilik Air RM4k, Lain-lain RM3k, for a total of RM30,000 that she cannot exceed. She keeps the list while watching a K-drama episode and has not yet bought anything, waiting for the keys to be ready.

nodes.name: Tamil language support
nodes.summary: Priya Nair found that the app offers only English and Malay, and submitted feedback asking for Tamil; she said that if a platform wants her community's content and money, their language should be there. Many others also sent feedback asking for Tamil.

nodes.name: Rumah Bajet MY
nodes.summary: Rumah Bajet MY champions transparency in home decor and furniture purchases: total price upfront, a realistic timeline, and someone accountable if something is off. It advises that for handmade pieces, "similar in photo" does not equal similar in hand, so buyers should ask what an item is made of and who repairs it, support local sellers (peniaga tempatan), and buy with their eyes and hands. Its stated golden rule is to compare the total landed cost — item + delivery + installation + any import/forwarding fee — noting a "cheap" Shopee listing can end up pricier than a local seller once overseas shipping kicks in; buyers should ask for exact dimensions, material, and model code and compare like for like, and measure twice since a 10cm error can make an entire cabinet not fit.

nodes.name: Sabah & Sarawak
nodes.summary: Sabah & Sarawak are addressed as a distinct delivery region in Malaysian furniture and home-goods buying. Vista Sofa Factory Outlet, which builds sofas in Muar and sells direct from its outlet, warned that a "2-4 days" KL warehouse lead time becomes 1-2 weeks once freight crosses the South China Sea, and that bulky freight is not cheap. Hafiz Ismail added seat height and seat depth in cm and door/lift clearance to the checklist for bulky items. Malaysia Reno Kaki warned that lead times are not the same for Georgetown 10200, Penang mainland, Sabah, and Sarawak, and that "2-4 hari" can become 12. Nadia Home Diary said the promised date must be checked against the buyer's postcode, since even Shah Alam differs, let alone Sabah & Sarawak.

nodes.name: Grace Chin
nodes.summary: Grace Chin works in computer vision and evaluates CV tools, both her own and vendors'. Her stated view is that the most underrated product skill is knowing what to measure, not model architecture; she spent years early in her career chasing accuracy points on benchmarks that looked impressive and predicted nothing. A metric only earns its place if it changes a decision, and she treats a "97% accuracy" figure as vanity rather than signal unless it tells you whether a shopper finds the product, whether a warehouse counts inventory correctly, or whether a clinician trusts the output. When evaluating a CV tool she asks three questions: what decision the metric informs, what the baseline is and whether it is honest, and what slice it fails on and whether that is said publicly. She holds that teams answering all three earn trust, while those quoting only a headline number are selling a demo, not a product.

nodes.name: Amirah Zulkifli's reading corner
nodes.summary: Amirah Zulkifli's planned reading corner consists of a rattan chair, linen curtain, and warm lamp. The inspo scan put it at RM4,000++.

nodes.name: installation checklist
nodes.summary: Bintang Elektrik published a five-point installation checklist from its Seremban showroom: (1) full model code on the sticker, indoor and outdoor for aircond, checking the exact series; (2) capacity matched to room size, since 1.0HP vs 1.5HP is invisible in a photo; (3) total cost sampai pasang plus test, covering unit, delivery, piping, brackets, vacuum, breaker and labour rather than sticker price; (4) warranty in writing for parts, compressor and labour, with local authorised units preferred over parallel imports; and (5) for gas items such as water heaters, hobs and stoves, a trained installer and proper leak test. Bintang Elektrik states value comes from proper installation and after-sales service, not just the lowest price. Grace Chin called it the cleanest checklist in the thread and added a sixth precondition: the benchmark, defining the metric, how the labelled test set was built, and the false-match rate between near-identical units.

nodes.name: 30-day bounded test
nodes.summary: Rumah Lengkap Marketing set a 30-day bounded test with limits, three volunteer clients (one Klang Valley, one Penang, one Kuching), measured on cost per qualified lead against their Facebook and marketplace baseline, with no exclusivity and no upfront payment; if it fails, the numbers will be published and clients told to spend elsewhere. Three conditions precede any small client spending ringgit: the paid Partner slot must be labelled as advertising upfront before the click in BM and English; the "best offer" badge must not be purchasable and must count total landed cost (unit + delivery + installation + import tax + after-sales) plus seller trust; and cost per qualified lead must be shown in writing with real delivery days by postcode rather than "2-4 days whole Malaysia".

attributes.name: Why I Said No to RM10,000

nodes.name: Why I Said No to RM10,000
nodes.summary: Why I Said No to RM10,000 is a piece by Jason Reno Journal about his rejection of a RM10,000 affiliate deal for a product that had not been tested. He cited it as the reason he is firm that affiliate disclosure must come before the click; in later posts he stated that any affiliate link he shares is labelled before the click, that he had turned down money for untested products before, and that "commission is fine, hidden commission is the problem." He frames his refusal as the basis for not selling what he cannot guarantee, alongside his rule that affiliate commission be labelled on every link before the click. In November 2026 comments he repeated the RM10,000 refusal as the reason he insists the paid Partner slot be labelled "iklan" in BM and English before the click, saying he does not ask a small Klang or Kangar seller to do what he will not do himself, and that a "92% match" without a confidence score and labelled test set is decoration rather than validation.

nodes.name: Wong Kar Fai
nodes.summary: Wong Kar Fai lives in Shah Alam and is replacing a 9-year-old 1.5HP aircond in the master bedroom. He is prioritising cooling capacity, energy efficiency, good installation, and a clear warranty covering parts, compressor and labour, and is seeking a trusted installer around Shah Alam. He asks for quotes stating whether standard installation, piping, brackets and labour are included, and whether the warranty stays valid if a third-party installer is used. He shares his findings to help others avoid hidden fees.

nodes.name: Kaki
nodes.summary: Kaki produced a checklist that Kedai Perabot Seri Jaya called solid, adding that buyers should ask about delivery, installation, and the warranty period, since a cheap sofa arriving unassembled with no service is not cheap, and that comparing a screenshot against the actual unit is a great idea. In November 2026 discussion, Kedai Perabot Seri Jaya acknowledged Kaki's checklist and added furniture-specific points on dimensions, total cost including delivery and installation, and written warranty terms. Dr. Salina Rahmat thanked Kaki, calling the framework plain enough for a non-engineer to use and describing it as the transparency norm the industry should have built itself, adding points on disclosure provenance, crediting creators, and retention periods.

nodes.name: Klang
nodes.summary: Klang is a Malaysian city serving as the home base for several consumers and merchants in an ongoing marketplace discussion. Rajesh Pillai, 47, is renovating the kitchen of an 18-year-old terrace house in Klang with water damage under the sink, and cites an RM350 extra installation charge for an online-bought fridge and a RM600 last-minute hidden delivery charge; he asks sellers whether installation is included, for warranty years covering parts and labour, and whether they have a physical shop to view the unit, screenshots total landed cost every time, checks review count, recency, buyer photos and warranty, and avoids DIY on gas hobs, water heaters and aircond for safety and warranty reasons. Chan Mei Fong, 56, in Klang usually buys appliances from one trusted shop, uses apps only to check prices before visiting, keeps a small notebook recording app price against shop price, must touch items first, and cites the 1998 crisis teaching her every ringgit must count.

nodes.name: DIY YouTube channel
nodes.summary: Ah Boon Fix It runs a DIY YouTube channel as an ex-contractor turned DIY YouTuber. He tells viewers that a listing price is misleading until landed cost is added, and has shown his own version of the "built first, appliance can't fit" mistake on camera, including a kitchen photo suggesting a cabinet 20cm too wide. His sign-off is "If I can fix it, you can fix it too!" and he discloses commission earned on purchases through links he shares.

nodes.name: bounded 30-day test
nodes.summary: Lim Wei Jie endorsed a bounded 30-day test with three voluntary clients, no upfront fee, a deletion test before any photo is collected, and a promise to publish the numbers even if the test fails. He added the precondition of item-level accuracy: before any of the three clients commits money, the vendor must publish top-1 category accuracy versus retrieval precision@1 on the exact model code, how the labelled test set was built including near-identical units, and the false-match rate per category, since 1.0HP versus 1.5HP aircond or NR-BX418VS versus a lookalike are indistinguishable in a frame. He also required the retention period stated in plain language before upload and a verifiable delete, plus full model code, cut-out/clearance dimensions, whether installation is included and by a trained/certified person, and warranty terms (parts and labour, local authorised versus parallel import) for gas and electrical items.

nodes.name: Casella
nodes.summary: Casella is a shopping app whose "buy" button opens Shopee or Taobao, meaning the seller, courier and warranty holder are three different parties. Ah Boon Fix It advises checking the seller's local presence before tapping buy, and discloses that he earns a small commission on purchases made through such links. On 2026-11-04 he repeated this in comments on Budget Reno Bro's East Malaysia weekend check-in post: the listing price is not the real number until landed cost is added, and buyers should check for a local service point because when the item breaks nobody owns it. He also added that outstation sellers do not cover installation, and installing a hob or oven in a condo with no lift access can rise from RM150 to RM400 with carrying charges alone, so that number should be in writing before purchase.

nodes.name: specification comparison table
nodes.summary: Lim Wei Jie's specification comparison method for home appliances calls for a simple table built before deciding on a built-in oven, stove, or hood, with columns for model number, dimensions (W x D x H in mm), cut-out dimensions (built-in items only), power rating or gas type (LPG vs natural gas, to be confirmed, not assumed), warranty period and coverage, whether installation is included (Yes/No plus who installs), and the nearest after-sales service location. If a seller cannot fill in even half of these, Lim Wei Jie moves on, since price alone tells nothing about fit, safety, or long-term support; Lim Wei Jie seeks genuine reviews with actual dimensions from the Seremban/Nilai area. Sarah Thevi said a clear comparison table helps a lot because she will compare 3 models before deciding. Chua Li Ting added a further column for data collected, retention period, and ability to delete it, and would not upload a home photo without a stated retention period and an obvious delete button.

nodes.name: Casella
nodes.summary: Casella is in beta, and its image-scan feature is under scrutiny from Malaysian sellers and buyers. Halim Yaakob, an aircond installer in Johor Bahru, argues that a "92% match" is not a model number and that buyers should screenshot both indoor and outdoor stickers, since 1.0HP and 1.5HP units look alike in photos and different series use different gas (R32 vs R410A), regions and warranties. Vista Sofa Factory Outlet in Muar treats Taobao and Shopee as a benchmark and will test Casella only if it drives qualified local leads (real WhatsApp enquiries and showroom visits in Johor/Melaka) at a workable cost per lead, with any paid Partner slot labelled "iklan" before the click.

nodes.name: group-buy hubs
nodes.summary: Group-buy hubs per city are an admin commitment of Malaysia Reno Kaki, stated on record, so members split freight together. The named coverage areas are KK, Kuching, Sandakan, Sibu, Tawau, Miri, and rural postcodes. Members are asked to drop "GB" plus their area to be connected.

nodes.name: merchant phase
nodes.summary: Vista Sofa Factory Outlet, a sofa maker based in Muar, identified the merchant phase as what local shops have been waiting for. For a paid Partner slot, the outlet said two things matter to small merchants: label it clearly as iklan rather than hiding it, and disclose the cost per lead while showing leads are qualified. Most small merchants have never paid for online leads and will test small only; the outlet said it would proceed if the leads inbox brings real WhatsApp and showroom visits from buyers in Johor, Melaka or KL. The outlet also said the Best offer badge must stay based on total cost, seller trust and service, not on who paid for placement.

nodes.name: Nadia's Linktree page
nodes.summary: Nadia's Linktree page is being built as a small website to organize all of Nadia's recommendations with full details (model code, dimensions, price delivered to the home). It sits alongside her ongoing budget makeover series for B40 families and her stated goal of one day having her own home decor line; for now she is taking small steps and chooses brands to collaborate with carefully, prioritizing honest and transparent ones. On 4 November 2026 she shared that she is quietly testing affiliate links in her bio, will label any commercial content as "iklan" in Malay and English before clicks, and will only recommend items she has personally handled. She cited Kedai Serbaneka Aman, which never paid for online leads, as motivation to prove her influence is genuine.

nodes.name: Budget Reno Bro
nodes.summary: Budget Reno Bro is a Reddit commenter who does not buy items he cannot physically handle, framing his feedback to Rimbun as free market research. He asks makers to disclose cane type (rotan manau or sega), dimensions in cm L×D×H, seat height, finish, and self-collect versus delivery, and stresses the real total cost to the home — item plus delivery plus any installation — calling sticker price only "the trap." He wants to see hands weaving rather than only polished final products, saying process beats polish. He asks whether a maker knows where their piece appears in a scan-and-link app and who earns commission on its sale, insisting on credit and consent for a maker's images, and says he will promote only if the price is real because he won't promote goods he has never held.

nodes.name: TikTok
nodes.summary: TikTok is a platform where Hannah Lau, 24, of Subang Jaya, saves hundreds of room tours while seldom buying. Nadia Home Diary is a Malay-language TikTok room-tour creator who receives constant "where to buy?" comments and is curious about affiliate income. Rina Kecil Living, an Instagram small-space creator, worries that apps profit from her content without crediting her. In a November 4, 2026 post, Rumah Bajet MY warned that a cheap Shopee or TikTok find can double in cost once it crosses the South China Sea, urging buyers to compare total landed cost including shipping to their own postcode, installation, and local warranty service.

nodes.name: sprocket set
nodes.summary: Rosli Ahmad, a buyer and small workshop owner (motor workshop) in Kangar, Perlis (postcode 01000), ordered a sprocket set from a Shah Alam seller in February; the listing stated 2-4 working days, but by day 12 tracking remained at the Petaling Jaya hub, and the seller said "Perlis slalu lambat, boss" with a laughing emoji. Rosli called the outcome dishonest rather than slow, said he would not buy from a seller who cannot show real delivery dates, and demands confirmed transit days in writing for Kangar; he lost one customer job because the motorcycle could not be finished on time. He cites the order as evidence that KL-warehouse delivery estimates must follow the actual postcode, comparing it to Georgetown 10200, Sabah/Sarawak, Kedah and Pantai Timur shipments, and notes Perlis sits in the Peninsula but is often charged as if abroad.

nodes.name: Malaysia Reno Kaki
nodes.summary: Malaysia Reno Kaki is a renovation-focused community on Twitter that issues admin announcements and weekly reno tips. Its "Check Price" guidance warns members to verify fast-delivery promises against their own postcode, since lead times differ for Georgetown 10200, Penang mainland, Sabah and Sarawak, and a "2-4 hari" claim can become 12; members are told to compare total landed cost (unit price, delivery, installation, warranty including original versus parallel import, and trade-in), screenshot promised dates and keep chat logs, report genuine good and bad experiences, and get at least 3 contractor quotes comparing scope rather than price, with certified workers required for electrical and plumbing. It stays neutral in disputes via moderator mediation and fact-checking, bans politics, race, religion and unverified personal attacks, maintains a trusted contractor list updated monthly from member feedback, and holds monthly live Q&A with industry experts at 8-11 PM all weekend.

nodes.name: Singapore
nodes.summary: Singapore is a shopping destination for Muhammad Hazim, 35, of Johor Bahru, who also shops there while comparing prices on an app whose coverage he finds limited. Sri Mutiara Home Centre, located in Johor Bahru minutes from the Causeway, advertises to Singaporean shoppers with a showroom stocked with living room sets, dining tables, bedroom furniture and home decor at prices that beat city markups, plus delivery and assembly, exclusive weekend deals and 10am–8pm opening hours.

nodes.name: Kevin Lim
nodes.summary:
Kevin Lim is a 26-year-old young professional in Subang Jaya who buys often on Shopee. He tested a scan-and-link app for a 1.8L Midea/Xiaomi rice cooker; the first result was a mismatched Taobao electric kettle with a voltage plug issue and no clear RM total, so he deleted the app in 2 minutes. His rule: the first result must be correct or he deletes, though he would reinstall if match badges improve. By November 2026 his cart held two 1.8L rice cookers (one Midea, one Xiaomi) since the previous month, with seller rating, delivery days and warranty checked, waiting for the 6.6 sale to see which drops to a lower total. His routine:
 screenshot listings and compare delivery days side by side, check the full model code on the sticker and warranty coverage in Malaysia, scroll to 2- and 3-star reviews with photos while skipping fake 5-star three-word reviews, and require a clear total (item + shipping + installation, no hidden fees) before buying.

nodes.name: Merchant phase
nodes.summary: The merchant phase lets verified Malaysian stores list products by form, CSV, or Shopee shop import. Local stores that deliver to the user are matched first and shown in a Local stores tab. Users can request a quote from up to 5 stores when there is no exact match. Merchants get a dashboard of impressions, clicks, leads, and missed demand, plus an inbox of billable WhatsApp, quote, and showroom leads.

nodes.name: Kedai Perabot Seri Jaya
nodes.summary: Kedai Perabot Seri Jaya is a family-owned furniture shop in Klang, established in 1985, whose staff describe themselves as non-technical. The shop fears losing customers to cheap imports but needs online discovery; it completed Casella merchant portal verification and listed a selection of its pieces, with the CSV upload proving challenging. It delivers and installs within the Klang Valley, makes and installs its own pieces locally, and quotes open full prices (unit + delivery + installation + warranty), inviting shoppers to test-sit samples at its Klang showroom and to check frame wood, foam density, fabric, stitching and after-sales before comparing prices. For the paid Partner slot it requires clear ROI metrics, written cost per qualified lead, delivery days by postcode, front-labelled IKLAN slots in BM and English, and a Best offer badge that cannot be bought; it is cautiously optimistic, backed by local-first matching.

nodes.name: disclosure timing test
nodes.summary: Jason Reno Journal proposes timing the disclosure rather than only checking that it exists: measure cost per qualified lead when the "iklan"/affiliate label sits before the click versus buried after, then publish the comparison. His read is that early disclosure holds conversion better, not worse. This is one of two additions he makes to the 30-day protocol, alongside publishing measured visual accuracy.

nodes.name: 1.8L rice cooker
nodes.summary: Kevin Lim named a 1.8L rice cooker as the example product for his requirement that an app's first search return the correct result, with a clear RM total, real reviews with photos, delivery days, and warranty; he planned to screenshot and compare, wait for 6.6, and checkout, and to delete the app if the first result is not correct.

nodes.name: handmade local furniture
nodes.summary: Aisyah Rahman said she likes seeking out handmade local furniture, that each woven piece has its own story and differs from factory goods, and that she usually finds shops selling it through Instagram hashtags #buatanmalaysia and #rotan and through word-of-mouth from friends.

nodes.name: benchmark publication
nodes.summary: Grace Chin holds that three things must be published before anyone should trust a "92% match" badge: what the metric actually is (top-1 category accuracy versus retrieval precision@1 on the exact model code, which are not the same), how the labelled test set was built and whether near-identical units (1.0HP vs 1.5HP; NR-BX418VS vs NR-BX418XSB) were included, and the false-match rate. She cites a 2019 case where a "beats the big guy" claim collapsed once the test set turned out biased toward the vendor's own training data. If "match dekat" can move money, the benchmark is the product; otherwise the badge is decoration.

nodes.name: cross-border orders
nodes.summary: For cross-border orders, total landed cost includes import tax and shipping in addition to item price and delivery. Taobao offers show an estimated 10 to 18 days for delivery.

nodes.name: Farah Zainal's curtain order
nodes.summary: Farah Zainal, a Sabah homeowner in Kota Kinabalu, was burned by a West Malaysian curtain order in which the shipping cost more than the curtains themselves. Farah requires per-region and per-poskod rows, screenshots of the full model code including indoor and outdoor stickers for appliances, total landed cost to the house (unit + delivery across the South China Sea + import tax + installation + after-sales), delivery days by poskod in writing, and a confidence score on the badge with a real "no match" option. Farah also holds that provenance — consent, credit, and compensation share — should be published beside precision and recall, since room photos are not free data.

nodes.name: shop-the-whole-room totals
nodes.summary: Shop-the-whole-room totals are planned for the next phase and are not available at beta.

nodes.name: Dr. Salina Rahmat
nodes.summary: Dr. Salina Rahmat makes sofas in Muar. A sofa-buying checklist post attributed to her advises buyers of lookalike sofas online to check four things: whether the frame wood is solid kiln-dried or thin plywood, foam density (soft foam that sinks in six months versus firm foam that holds its shape), fabric and stitching, and delivery plus warranty. The post noted that the same sofa can carry a very different total cost, invited customers to sit on samples at the outlet before deciding, offered quotes via WhatsApp, and emphasized direct factory sales, honest materials, local after-sales, and testing by sitting first. Other home and furniture sellers and creators—Rina Kecil Living, Sarah Thevi, Sinar Home Marketplace, Aisyah Rahman, Chan Mei Fong and Vista Sofa Factory Outlet—circulated or echoed versions of the same checklist in November 2026.

nodes.name: Mr DIY Puchong
nodes.summary: A hardware store in Puchong where Budget Reno Bro bought a shelf and bracket for RM 89.90 and installed them himself in 40 minutes with one Philips screwdriver.

nodes.name: water heater
nodes.summary: Azlan Musa will not compromise on water heaters and gas hobs: they must have a trained installer plus a leak test, with the regulator and hose following LPG or piped standards, prioritising safety over a cheap price. Azlan renovates his terraced house in Kuantan stage by stage, one room at a time, buying items on a schedule and sometimes 2-3 months after saving in an app. He asks whether warranty starts on purchase date or installation date when a unit is bought now and installed the following month, and wants the answer in writing. He asks shops for the full model code on the sticker (indoor and outdoor for air-conditioning), an itemised total (unit, delivery to his Kuantan postcode, piping, bracket, vacuum, breaker, labour), and warranty covering parts, compressor and labour from a local authorised seller.

nodes.name: affiliate link disclosure
nodes.summary: Affiliate links are disclosed before the click, following a stated practice of "test first, trust later." On 2026-11-04, Jason Reno Journal said any affiliate link shared, gadget or renovation tool, is labelled before the click, having previously declined payment for untested products, and that commission is acceptable but hidden commission is not. Nadia Home Diary, a home decor creator in Shah Alam, is quietly testing affiliate links in her bio and requires commissions to be labelled "iklan" up front in both Malay and English, calling disclosure a relationship rather than a disclaimer.

nodes.name: Casella
nodes.summary: Casella is referenced by Malaysia Reno Kaki as a beta during which the community had already stated its position that East Malaysia would not be an afterthought, a position Malaysia Reno Kaki repeated: no more West Malaysia-centric coverage, with East Malaysian creators and voices such as Borneo Home Tales, local suppliers, and KK/Kuching/Sibu/Miri/Tawau members getting the same airtime and the same PIN.

nodes.name: Sabah/Sarawak crew
nodes.summary: The Sabah/Sarawak crew is a group referenced on Twitter alongside Malaysia Reno Kaki as having gone deep on TOTAL LANDED COST, with Rumah Bajet MY addressing East Malaysia readers directly. Rumah Bajet MY noted that shipping to Sabah/Sarawak postcodes can turn an RM40 Semenanjung rate into RM180 to KK or Sibu, that outstation sellers usually do not cover installation (budget RM150–400), and that a 5-year warranty covering only Semenanjung is worth zero there. Malaysia Reno Kaki's buyer filter likewise flags that warranty paper covering only Semenanjung equals zero and that "3-5 hari" delivery is wrong for Kuching.

nodes.name: scan history deletion
nodes.summary: Priya Nair tested whether a "delete my scan history" control actually deletes, saying a delete button that doesn't delete is worse than no button, and that the retention period should be stated in plain language before upload. She also checked where room photos go and how long they are kept, and advised scanning as a guest, denying unneeded permissions, and verifying the delete before deciding.

nodes.name: Seremban renovation
nodes.summary: Seremban renovation is a buyer's-side renovation case referenced in a discussion of creator credit and consent. Lim Wei Jie offered to add the buyer's side from a Seremban renovation, arguing that credit, consent and retention matter not only for creators but for ordinary homeowners whose rooms end up in these photos. Aisyah Rahman closed her comment with wishes that the Seremban business prosper further.

nodes.name: privacy retention and delete
nodes.summary: The Sabah Sarawak Home Group admin team advises checking retention and real delete before uploading, stating that a room photo is not free data.

nodes.name: Wong Kar Fai's notebook
nodes.summary: Wong Kar Fai records a product's model number, total landed cost, and promised delivery date in his notebook before paying, a practice he adopted after nearly buying a fridge on a "Best offer" ad where delivery was extra, old fridge removal was not included, and the warranty card was a parallel import. He also saves offer links and updates them when he finds something better.

nodes.name: merchant dashboard
nodes.summary: The merchant dashboard shows impressions, clicks, leads, and missed demand.

nodes.name: Xiaohongshu renovation groups
nodes.summary: Xiaohongshu renovation groups are a community on Xiaohongshu focused on renovation. People already use them as a way to find out where an item is from.

nodes.name: #CheckLocalFirst
nodes.summary: #CheckLocalFirst is a hashtag used by Malaysian homeowners in a Reddit thread on scan apps and furniture buying. Melissa Anak Jimbun used it while cautioning that for bulky items (sofa, wardrobe, TV console) shipping by poskod is the killer: a RM28 delivery figure is a Klang Valley number, while to Kuching it can jump to RM80–150 plus import tax, and "installation included *conditions apply*" usually means not for East Malaysia; her quote to ship a 3-seater sofa from Taobao to Kuching was RM800 before tax and installation. Amirah Zulkifli used it while describing her drill of scanning, saving, closing the app, then comparing total landed cost manually on Shopee/Mr DIY. In round 70, Melissa cosigned a checklist from Kuching, citing a wardrobe ordered online where West Malaysia got a far cheaper rate and Sarawak paid more, and asking every seller to provide written total landed cost by poskod plus honest delivery days.

nodes.name: Rumah SP Bajet
nodes.summary: Rumah SP Bajet is a budget home project tracked by Syafiq Hamdan under a plan capped at RM5,000. The kitchen cabinet refresh is the second item under that plan. Syafiq reported a local seller with a 4.8 rating and 1.2k sold, a total of RM289 including shipping to Sungai Petani, delivery in 7 days rather than the 2-4 days stated in the listing, a 14-day return window, and a stacked RM12 voucher plus free shipping. He advised writing out total RM, shipping, delivery days, and warranty, and skipping listings that hide RM15 shipping until checkout, and asked for links to cabinet sellers that ship to Kedah.

nodes.name: privacy policy
nodes.summary: Aisyah Rahman, a prospective first condo owner with a tight RM30k budget, has not signed in because she wants to read the privacy policy first, and advises scanning first, then checking local shop prices before paying rather than trusting the sticker price; she also said the total price (delivery + installation + import tax) is what allows a fair comparison. Lau Kok Wai asked whether tags show total landed cost or sticker price only, where room photos go, how long they are kept, and whether deletion is actually permanent, and said that if these cannot be verified without signing up he will take screenshots, note the model code, and call the shop instead.

nodes.name: Courts
nodes.summary: Courts is a retailer named among the places to check an appliance model against before deciding on a purchase. Wong Kar Fai named Courts alongside Shopee, Lazada, SenQ and smaller Penang shops, and also named Courts, Shopee, Lazada, Mudah and two small Penang shops as the places he checks before signing, citing a fridge advertised as a Best offer that then had extra delivery charges, old unit removal not included, and a parallel-import warranty card. In cross-border shopping from Johor Bahru, Muhammad Hazim named Courts among the stores compared between Johor Bahru and Singapore, together with Harvey Norman, Gain City, Best Denki and Mustafa, while citing incomplete app coverage of both sides of the Causeway.

nodes.name: Sarawak
nodes.summary: Sarawak is the East Malaysian state at the centre of a landed-cost argument led by Melissa Anak Jimbun, 35, a Kuching homeowner. Her RM800 quote to ship a 3-seater sofa from Taobao to Kuching, before tax and installation, is cited widely; she holds that Klang Valley figures like RM28 shipping can jump to RM80–150 for Sarawak plus import tax, and that "installation included *conditions apply*" usually excludes East Malaysia. Her rule: ask the total cost — shipping to Sabah/Sarawak plus import tax and installation — and request the full model code indoor and outdoor, total landed cost to her postcode including delivery to Kuching, import tax, installation and breaker, and honest delivery days by postcode rather than "nationwide"; she advises screenshotting the total landed cost by postcode and testing an app's delete button before scanning a home.

nodes.name: affiliate marketing
nodes.summary: Affiliate marketing drew explicit disclosure standards in a Reddit thread. Jason Reno Journal discloses every affiliate link in his videos and declined a RM10,000 affiliate deal for an untested product (Why I Said No to RM10,000), arguing disclosure must appear before the click, not in a hashtag; on 4 November 2026 he endorsed all five points of a thread checklist, naming points 2 and 4 as his red lines, and required written benchmarks before trusting any "92% match" claim. Sabah Sarawak Home Group set three written conditions, including that affiliate commission be labelled on every link before the click, front and centre, and that a retention period be stated before upload. Nadia Home Diary promised to label honestly when a link is affiliate — before the click, not hidden in the bio — and to recommend only items used and trusted. Rina Kecil Living framed a creator's "total landed cost" of work as permission plus credit plus fair pay.

nodes.name: Faizal Rahim's aircond replacement post
